ArraySize Result = ArraySize(Array() [, Dimension]) Returns the size of the array, as specified with Dim or ReDim. Returns the size of the array dimension. If the array isn't yet declared (for example after FreeArray() or if its allocation has failed), it will return -1.
CompareArray Result = CompareArray(Array1(), Array2() [, Flags]) Compare each elements of the two arrays for equality. Recursively compares also contents of structured arrays with dynamic elements (such as embedded arrays, lists or maps). The two arrays are considered the equal if they have the same type and dimensions and if each pair of elements is equal. Returns nonzero if both arrays are the same or zero if they differ.
CopyArray Result = CopyArray(SourceArray(), DestinationArray()) Copy every element of 'SourceArray()' into 'DestinationArray()'. After a successful copy, the two arrays are identical. The arrays must have the same number of dimensions. Returns nonzero if the copy succeeded or zero if it failed.
ExtractArray Result = ExtractArray(Array(), Text$ [, Separator$ [, Limit]]) Splits 'Text$' into 'Array()', using 'Separator$' to find each element. 'Array()' is redimensioned to hold exactly the number of elements found. Returns the number of elements found (and stored into 'Array()').
FreeArray FreeArray(Array()) Free the specified 'Array()' and release all its associated memory. To access it again Dim has to be called. None

A RTT Texture has to be created from #Camera using CreateRenderTexture. The material which will use this RTT texture has to be defined with SetMaterialAttribute(Material, #PB_Material_ProjectiveTexturing, #Camera). This command has to be used in the rendering loop. None
CameraRenderMode CameraRenderMode(#Camera, RenderMode) Changes the mode in which the world is displayed through a camera. When you create a new camera, using the CreateCamera function, the default render mode is to display the world with full details and textures. None
CameraRoll Result = CameraRoll(#Camera [, Mode]) Get the roll of the #Camera. The current roll value of the camera. This value is always between -180.0 and 180.0 degrees.
CameraViewHeight Result = CameraViewHeight(#Camera) Returns the height (in pixels) of the camera frame in the screen. Returns the height (in pixels) of the camera frame in the screen.
CameraViewWidth Result = CameraViewWidth(#Camera) Returns the width (in pixels) of the camera frame in the screen. Returns the width (in pixels) of the camera frame in the screen.
CameraViewX Result = CameraViewX(#Camera) Returns the 'x' position (in pixels) of the camera frame in the screen. Returns the 'x' position (in pixels) of the camera frame in the screen.
CameraViewY Result = CameraViewY(#Camera) Returns the 'y' position (in pixels) of the camera frame in the screen. Returns the 'y' position (in pixels) of the camera frame in the screen.
CameraX Result = CameraX(#Camera [, Mode]) Returns the current 'x' position of the camera in the world. Returns the 'x' position of the camera.
CameraY Result = CameraY(#Camera [, Mode]) Returns the current 'y' position of the camera in the world. Returns the 'y' position of the camera.
CameraYaw Result = CameraYaw(#Camera [, Mode]) Get the yaw of the #Camera. The current yaw value of the camera. This value is always between -180.0 and 180.0 degrees.
CameraZ Result = CameraZ(#Camera [, Mode]) Returns the current position of the camera in the world. Returns the 'z' position of the camera.
CheckObjectVisibility Result = CheckObjectVisibility(#Camera, ObjectID) Checks if an object is visible within a camera view. Returns #True if object is within the selected camera view or #False if outside the visible area.
CreateCamera Result = CreateCamera(#Camera, x, y, Width, Height [, VisibilityMask [, Lod]]) Creates a new camera in the current world, at the position x,y with the specified dimensions. Note that these positions and sizes are the position and sizes of the display on the screen, not the position and size of the camera in the world. Unlike other graphics related functions, these coordinates and dimensions are in percents, from 0 to 100 (float numbers can be used for more precise placement). This could seems odd, but 3D applications should be resolution independent and this is a good way of achieving that. If a camera is created with a height of 50% then it will always fill 50% of the height of the screen, irrespective of whether you use a screen which is 640*480 or 1600*1200. If a camera has already been created with the same number, the previous camera is automatically freed and replaced by the new one. Cameras can be overlapped. This means that it is possible to display a camera which fills the whole screen and put a little camera inside which shows another place in the world. To achieve this, the order of creation is very important: the camera which will be on top should be created last. Returns zero if the camera can't be created. If #PB_Any is used as '#Camera' parameter, the new camera number will be returned as 'Result'.
FreeCamera FreeCamera(#Camera) Frees a camera and releases all its associated memory. This camera must not be used (by using its number with the other functions in this library) after calling this function, unless you create it again. None
IsCamera Result = IsCamera(#Camera) Tests if the given #Camera is a valid and correctly initialized camera. This function is bulletproof and can be used with any value. If the 'Result' is not zero then the object is valid and initialized, else it returns zero. This is the correct way to ensure a camera is ready to use.
MoveCamera MoveCamera(#Camera, x, y, z [, Mode]) Move the specified camera. None
ResizeCamera ResizeCamera(#Camera, x, y, Width, Height) Resizes the camera according to the specified dimension. All values are in percentages, like with CreateCamera. None
RotateCamera RotateCamera(#Camera, x, y, z [, Mode]) Rotates the camera according to the specified x,y,z angle values. None

CGIBuffer *Result = CGIBuffer() For advanced users. Returns the memory buffer address of the raw CGI input (only useful for POST request type). It can be useful to do extra parsing not supported by this library while still using other commands. The size of the buffer is the value returned by ReadCGI. Returns the memory buffer address of the raw CGI input, or zero if an error occurred.
CGICookieName Result$ = CGICookieName(Index) Returns the name of the specified cookie. Returns the name of the specified cookie.
CGICookieValue Result$ = CGICookieValue(Name$) Returns the value of the specified cookie. Returns the value of the specified cookie.
CGIParameterData *Result = CGIParameterData(Name$ [, Index]) Returns the memory buffer address of the specified parameter data. Returns the memory buffer address of the specified parameter data. The parameter type has to be #PB_CGI_File. CGIParameterDataSize can be used to get the size of the memory buffer.
CGIParameterDataSize Result = CGIParameterDataSize(Name$ [, Index]) Returns the size of the specified parameter data size. Returns the data size (in bytes) of the specified parameter. CGIParameterData can be used to get the memory buffer address of the parameter. The parameter type has to be #PB_CGI_File.
CGIParameterName Result = CGIParameterName(Index) Returns the name of the specified parameter. Returns the name of the specified parameter.
CGIParameterType Result = CGIParameterType(Name$ [, Index]) Returns the type of the specified parameter. Returns the type of the specified parameter. It can be one of the following value: #PB_CGI_Text: the parameter is a string #PB_CGI_File: the parameter is a binary file. CGIParameterValue will returns the original filename and CGIParameterData can be used to retrieve the binary data.
CGIParameterValue Result = CGIParameterValue(Name$ [, Index]) Returns the value of the specified parameter. Returns the value of the specified parameter.
CGIVariable Result$ = CGIVariable(Name$) Gets the specified CGI environment variable content. When the CGI is loaded, many information are sent from the web server to the CGI application through environment variables. Returns the value of the specified CGI environment variable.
CountCGICookies Result = CountCGICookies() Returns the number of available cookies. The cookies are small persistent files stored in the web browser to allow to remember a context and ease future navigation when loading the same page later on. Please note than European legislation now impose to inform users that cookies are not being used to gather information unnecessarily. Returns the number of available cookies. The name and value of cookies can be get with CGICookieName and CGICookieValue.
CountCGIParameters Result = CountCGIParameters() Returns the number of available parameters from GET or POST requests. Returns the number of available parameters from GET or POST requests. Parameter information can be get with CGIParameterName, CGIParameterValue and CGIParameterType.
FinishFastCGIRequest FinishFastCGIRequest() Finish the current FastCGI request and free all resources associated to it. It's not mandatory to use this command, as the request will be automatically finished when WaitFastCGIRequest() is called again, or when the thread ends. It can still be useful in some special case where resources are light before doing other processing. Returns non-zero if a new request has been processed.
InitCGI Result = InitCGI([MaxRequestSize]) Initializes the CGI environment. This function has to be called successfully before using any other commands of this library. Returns non-zero if the CGI environment has been correctly initialized.
InitFastCGI Result = InitFastCGI(LocalPort [, BoundIP$]) Initializes FastCGI support. Once called, all the CGI commands switch automatically to FastCGI support. This library support threaded FastCGI processing, when enabling the 'thread-mode' in PureBasic. FastCGI support is only supported through a local socket. InitCGI needs to be called before using this command. Unlike a regular CGI program which is launched at every request, the FastCGI program stays in memory once launched and can handle any number of requests. It can be very useful if the CGI initialization is time consumming (for example connecting a database), so it's only performed once at start. Returns non-zero if the FastCGI environment has been correctly initialized.
ReadCGI Result = ReadCGI() Reads the CGI request input. InitCGI has to be called successfully before trying to the read the CGI input. Returns non-zero if the CGI request has been successfully read. If the request was to big or another error occurred, zero is returned and the CGI program should be ended.
WaitFastCGIRequest Result = WaitFastCGIRequest() Waits for a new incoming request. This command will halt the program execution until a new request is available. InitFastCGI needs to be called successfully before using this command. Returns non-zero if a new request has been processed.
WriteCGIData Result = WriteCGIData(*Buffer, Size) Writes binary data to the CGI output. When sending binary data, the 'content-type' header should be set to 'application/octet-stream'. Returns non-zero if the data has been successfully written to the CGI output.
WriteCGIFile Result = WriteCGIFile(Filename$) Writes a whole file to the CGI output. When sending binary data, the 'content-type' header should be set to 'application/octet-stream'. Returns non-zero if the file has been successfully written to the CGI output.
WriteCGIHeader Result = WriteCGIHeader(Header$, Value$ [, Flags]) Writes a header to the CGI output. The headers needs to be written before any other data. Returns non-zero if the header has been successfully written to the CGI output.
WriteCGIString Result = WriteCGIString(String$ [, Encoding]) Write a string to the CGI output. Returns non-zero if the string has been successfully written to the CGI output.
WriteCGIStringN Result = WriteCGIStringN(String$ [, Encoding]) Write a string to the CGI output, including a carriage return. Returns non-zero if the string has been successfully written to the CGI output.

AddCipherBuffer AddCipherBuffer(#Cipher, *Input, *Output, Size) Add new data to the cipher started with StartAESCipher and copy the ciphered data into the output buffer. None
AddFingerprintBuffer AddFingerprintBuffer(#Fingerprint, *Buffer, Size) Add a new memory buffer into the calculation of a checksum started by StartFingerprint. The checksum returned at the end of the calculation will include all the added buffers as if the checksum was calculated with all of them in one continuous memory buffer. None
AESDecoder Result = AESDecoder(*Input, *Output, Size, *Key, Bits, *InitializationVector [, Mode]) Decodes the specified input buffer using the AES algorithm into the output buffer. Returns nonzero if the decoding was successful, zero otherwise.
AESEncoder Result = AESEncoder(*Input, *Output, Size, *Key, Bits, *InitializationVector [, Mode]) Encodes the specified input buffer using the AES algorithm into the output buffer. Returns nonzero if the encoding was successful, zero otherwise.
Base64Decoder Result = Base64Decoder(Input$, *OutputBuffer, OutputSize) Decodes the specified Base64 encoded string. Returns the length of the decoded data in bytes.
Base64DecoderBuffer Result = Base64DecoderBuffer(*InputBuffer, InputSize, *OutputBuffer, OutputSize) Decodes the specified Base64 encoded buffer. Returns the length of the decoded data in bytes.
Base64Encoder Result$ = Base64Encoder(*InputBuffer, InputSize [, Flags]) Encodes the specified buffer using the Base64 algorithm. This is widely used in e-mail programs but can be useful for any other programs which need an ASCII only (7 bit, only from 32 to 127 characters) encoding for raw binary files. Returns the encoded data as a string.
Base64EncoderBuffer Result = Base64EncoderBuffer(*InputBuffer, InputSize, *OutputBuffer, OutputSize [, Flags]) Encodes the specified buffer using the Base64 algorithm. This is widely used in e-mail programs but can be useful for any other programs which need an ASCII only (7 bit, only from 32 to 127 characters) encoding for raw binary files. Returns the length of the encoded data in bytes.
CloseCryptRandom CloseCryptRandom() Closes the cryptographic safe pseudorandom number generator that was opened with OpenCryptRandom and frees its resources. None
CreatePasswordHash Result$ = CreatePasswordHash(Password$ [, WorkFactor]) Creates a hash digest of a password for storage and later verification of a password. It is not possible to recover the input password from the hash value, but passwords can be verified to see if they match the hash using VerifyPasswordHash later. Returns the hash of the password.
CryptRandom Result = CryptRandom(Maximum) Returns a random number (integer) which lies between (and including) 0 and the Maximum value from the cryptographic safe pseudorandom number generator. Returns the generated random number.
CryptRandomData Result = CryptRandomData(*Buffer, Length) Fills the specified memory buffer with random data from the cryptographic safe pseudorandom number generator. Returns nonzero if the random data was generated successfully and zero otherwise.
DeriveCipherKey Result = DeriveCipherKey(Password$, Salt$, Iterations, *Key, KeyBits, Plugin [, PluginBits]) Creates a cypher key with the specified number of bits from an input password for use in other cypher functions like encryption or decryption. This function implements the PBKDF2 key derivation algorithm. Returns nonzero if the key was generated. Returns zero only if the plugin parameters were invalid.
DESFingerprint Result$ = DESFingerprint(Password$, Key$)
FileFingerprint Result$ = FileFingerprint(Filename$, Plugin [, Bits [, Offset [, Length [, HmacKey$ [, HmacKeyFormat]]]]]) Returns a fingerprint for the specified file. Returns the fingerprint if the calculation was successful. If the file isn't found or an error has happened, the result will be an empty string.
Fingerprint Result$ = Fingerprint(*Buffer, Size, Plugin [, Bits [, HmacKey$ [, HmacKeyFormat]]]) Returns a fingerprint for the given buffer. Returns the fingerprint as an hexadecimal string.
FinishCipher FinishCipher(#Cipher) Finish a cipher stream previously started with StartAESCipher. None
FinishFingerprint Result$ = FinishFingerprint(#Fingerprint) Finishes the calculation of a fingerprint started by StartFingerprint and returns it as an hexadecimal string. Returns the fingerprint as an hexadecimal string.
IsCipher Result = IsCipher(#Cipher) Tests if the given #Cipher number is a valid and correctly initialized cipher. Returns nonzero if #Cipher is a valid cipher and zero otherwise.
IsFingerprint Result = IsFingerprint(#Fingerprint) Tests if the given #Fingerprint is a valid fingerprint calculation created by StartFingerprint. Returns nonzero if the given fingerprint is valid and zero otherwise.
OpenCryptRandom Result = OpenCryptRandom() Opens the cryptographic safe pseudorandom number generator. The CryptRandom and CryptRandomData commands can be used to read data from the opened generator. Returns non-zero if the random number generator could be successfully opened. If the result is zero then there is no cryptographic safe random number generator available on the system.
StartAESCipher Result = StartAESCipher(#Cipher, *Key, Bits, *InitializationVector, Mode) Initializes a new AES cipher stream where data can be added using AddCipherBuffer. If #PB_Any was used as the #Cipher parameter then the auto-generated #Cipher number is returned.
StartFingerprint Result = StartFingerprint(#Fingerprint, Plugin [, Bits [, HmacKey$ [, HmacKeyFormat]]]) Initializes the calculation of a fingerprint in several steps. Unlike Fingerprint function this allows to calculate the fingerprint of large data without the need to load it all into one continuous memory buffer. Returns the #Fingerprint value if #PB_Any was used for that parameter.
StringFingerprint Result$ = StringFingerprint(String$, Plugin [, Bits [, Format[, HmacKey$ [, HmacKeyFormat]]]]) Returns a fingerprint for the given string. Returns the fingerprint as an hexadecimal string.
UseCRC32Fingerprint UseCRC32Fingerprint() Register the CRC32 fingerprint plugin for future use. None
UseMD5Fingerprint UseMD5Fingerprint() Register the MD5 fingerprint plugin for future use. None
UseSHA1Fingerprint UseSHA1Fingerprint() Register the SHA1 fingerprint plugin for future use. None
UseSHA2Fingerprint UseSHA2Fingerprint() Register the SHA2 fingerprint plugin for future use. The standard 224-bit, 256-bit, 384-bit and 512-bit variants are supported. None
UseSHA3Fingerprint UseSHA3Fingerprint() Register the SHA3 fingerprint plugin for future use. The standard 224-bit, 256-bit, 384-bit and 512-bit variants are supported. None
VerifyPasswordHash Result = VerifyPasswordHash(Password$, Hash$) Checks if a given password matches the hash value previously created with CreatePasswordHash. Returns non-zero if the password matches the hash value or zero if it does not match or if the hash value was not valid.
Clipboard (5)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
ClearClipboard ClearClipboard() Clears the clipboard. This means that any data contained within the clipboard is flushed and no longer available from the clipboard. None
GetClipboardImage Result = GetClipboardImage(#Image [, Depth]) Creates a new image from the clipboard image data (if any). Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Image parameter, then the new image number is returned.
GetClipboardText Text$ = GetClipboardText() Returns the text string currently contained within the clipboard. Returns the content of the clipboard if it contains text. If the clipboard contains no data or no text data, then an empty string is returned.
SetClipboardImage SetClipboardImage(#Image) Places a copy of the given image onto the clipboard. If the clipboard currently contains an image, then it will be overwritten. None
SetClipboardText SetClipboardText(Text$) Stores a string into the clipboard. If the clipboard already contains text, it will be overwritten. None
Console (16)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
ClearConsole ClearConsole() Clears the whole console content using the current background color. The background color is set with ConsoleColor. The console has to be in graphical mode, see EnableGraphicalConsole. None
CloseConsole CloseConsole() Close the console previously opened with OpenConsole. Once the console has been closed, it's not possible to use any console-related functions unless you open the console again. The console will automatically be closed when your program ends. No effects with Linux and MacOS. None
ConsoleColor ConsoleColor(CharacterColor, BackgroundColor) Change the colors used by the text display. Any characters printed after calling this function will use the new colors. None
ConsoleCursor ConsoleCursor(Height) Changes the display of the cursor, which is the indicator used to show where the next displayed character will be drawn. This function allows you to change the height of the cursor. None
ConsoleError ConsoleError(Message$) Writes the Message string (plus a newline) to the standard error output of the program. This output can be read for example with the ReadProgramError function of the Process library. None
ConsoleLocate ConsoleLocate(x, y) Moves the cursor to the given position, in character coordinates. Any text you print after calling this function will start from the specified coordinates. None
ConsoleTitle ConsoleTitle(Title$) Changes the console title to the specified string. The console title is typically shown in the title bar of the window which the console is in (when you are viewing the console in a graphical environment such as your desktop). Under Windows, the console title is also the text shown in the start bar and in the task manager representing your console application. None
EnableGraphicalConsole EnableGraphicalConsole(State) Changes the way the characters are drawn on the console between a graphical and a text-only mode. None
Inkey String$ = Inkey() Returns a character string if a key is pressed during the call of Inkey(). It doesn't interrupt (halt) the program flow. If special keys (non-ASCII) have to be handled, RawKey should be called after Inkey(). Returns a string containing the pressed character if it is a non-special key, and an empty string otherwise.
Input String$ = Input() Allows the program to catch an entire line of characters. This function locks the program execution and waits until the user presses the return key. Returns the string that the user entered before pressing the return key.
OpenConsole Result = OpenConsole([Title$ [, Mode]]) Open a console window. This function must be called before any other function of this library. Only one console can be opened at the same time in a PureBasic program. If Result is 0, it has failed and all further call to console functions must be disabled.
Print Print(Text$) Displays the specified 'Text$' in the console. None
PrintN PrintN(Text$) Displays the specified 'Text$' in the console and adds a new line. None
RawKey Result = RawKey() Returns the raw key code of the last Inkey function call. It's useful for extended (non-ASCII) keys (for example, function keys, arrows, etc). Returns the key code of the last pressed key.
ReadConsoleData Result = ReadConsoleData(*Buffer, Size) Reads raw input from the console. This function is only supported in non-graphical mode. It can be used to read not line-based data, or text like files redirected to the program through a pipe. Returns the number of bytes actually read from the input. If zero is returned, this means that there is no more input to read. (an end of file was received)
WriteConsoleData Result = WriteConsoleData(*Buffer, Size) Writes raw data to the console output. This function is only supported in non-graphical mode. It can be used to output data other than text to the console that can then be redirected to a file or another program. Returns the number of bytes actually written to the output.

#PB_CGI_AuthType CGIVariable the authentication method used by the web browser if any authentication method was used. This is not set unless the script is protected.
#PB_CGI_ContentLength CGIVariable used for scripts that are receiving form data using the POST method. This variable tells the byte length of the CGI input data stream. This is required to read the data from the standard input with the POST method.
#PB_CGI_DocumentRoot CGIVariable the root path to the home HTML page for the server.
#PB_CGI_File CGIParameterType the parameter is a binary file. CGIParameterValue will returns the original filename and CGIParameterData can be used to retrieve the binary data.
#PB_CGI_GatewayInterface CGIVariable the version of the common gateway Interface (CGI) specification being used to exchange the data between the client and server. This is usually CGI/1.1 for the current revision level of 1.1.
#PB_CGI_HeaderContentDisposition WriteCGIHeader allows to specify a default filename when sending out a file. WriteCGIHeader(1)
#PB_CGI_HeaderContentLength WriteCGIHeader the length (in bytes) of the output stream (implies binary data). WriteCGIHeader(1)
#PB_CGI_HeaderContentType CGIVariable, WriteCGIHeader tells the media type of data being received from the user. This is used for scripts called using the POST method. WriteCGIHeader(1)
#PB_CGI_HeaderExpires WriteCGIHeader date and time when the document is no longer valid and should be reloaded by the browser. WriteCGIHeader(1)
#PB_CGI_HeaderLocation WriteCGIHeader server redirection (cannot be sent as part of a complete header). WriteCGIHeader(1)
#PB_CGI_HeaderPragma WriteCGIHeader turns document caching on and off. WriteCGIHeader(1)
#PB_CGI_HeaderRefresh WriteCGIHeader client reloads specified document. WriteCGIHeader(1)
#PB_CGI_HeaderSetCookie WriteCGIHeader client stores specified data, useful for keeping track of data between requests. WriteCGIHeader(1)
#PB_CGI_HeaderStatus WriteCGIHeader status of the request (cannot be sent as part of a complete header). WriteCGIHeader(1)
#PB_CGI_HttpAccept CGIVariable the media types of data that the client browser can accept. These data types are separated by commas.
#PB_CGI_HttpAcceptEncoding CGIVariable the encoding type the client browser accepts.
#PB_CGI_HttpAcceptLanguage CGIVariable the language the client browser accepts.
#PB_CGI_HttpCookie CGIVariable used as an environment variable that contains cookies associated with the server domain from the browser.
#PB_CGI_HttpForwarded CGIVariable the forwarded page URL.
#PB_CGI_HttpHost CGIVariable hostname from where the HTPP requests comes from.
#PB_CGI_HttpPragma CGIVariable HTTP pragmas
#PB_CGI_HttpReferer CGIVariable the page address where the HTTP request originated.
#PB_CGI_HttpUserAgent CGIVariable the name of the client web browser being used to make the request.
#PB_CGI_LastHeader WriteCGIHeader This is the last header written, meaning no more headers can be sent. This flag is mandatory for the last header written. WriteCGIHeader(3)
#PB_CGI_PathInfo CGIVariable extra path information added to the end of the URL that accessed the server side script program.
#PB_CGI_PathTranslated CGIVariable a translated version of the PATH_INFO variable translated by the webserver from virtual to physical path information.
#PB_CGI_QueryString CGIVariable this string contains any information at the end of the server side script path that followed a question mark. Used to Return data if the GET method was used by a form. There are length restrictions to the QUERY_STRING.
#PB_CGI_RemoteAddr CGIVariable the IP address of the client computer.
#PB_CGI_RemoteHost CGIVariable the fully qualified domain name of the client machine making the HTTP request. It may not be possible to determine this name since many client computers names are not recorded in the DNS system.
#PB_CGI_RemoteIdent CGIVariable the ability to use this variable is limited to servers that support RFC 931. This variable may contain the client machine's username, but it is intended to be used for logging purposes only, when it is available.
#PB_CGI_RemotePort CGIVariable the clients requesting port.
#PB_CGI_RemoteUser CGIVariable if the CGI script was protected and the user had to be logged in to get access to the script, this value will contain the user's log in name.
#PB_CGI_REquestMethod CGIVariable describes the request method used by the browser which is usually GET, POST, Or HEAD.
#PB_CGI_RequestURI CGIVariable the path to the requested file by the client.
#PB_CGI_ScriptFilename CGIVariable the local filename of the script being executed.
#PB_CGI_ScriptName CGIVariable the virtual path of the CGI script being executed.
#PB_CGI_ServerAdmin CGIVariable the e-mail address of the server administrator.
#PB_CGI_ServerName CGIVariable the server hostname, IP address Or DNS alias name shown as a self referencing URL. This does not include the protocol identifier such as "HTTP:", the machine name, or port number.
#PB_CGI_ServerPort CGIVariable the port number the HTTP requests and responses are being sent on.
#PB_CGI_ServerProtocol CGIVariable this value is usually HTTP which describes the protocol being used between the client and server computers.
#PB_CGI_ServerSignature CGIVariable server information specifying the name and version of the web server and the port being serviced.
#PB_CGI_ServerSoftware CGIVariable the name and version of the web server.

#PB_Compiler_32Bit Compiler Directives Set to 1 if the compiler generates 32-bit code, set to 0 else.

#PB_Compiler_Backend Compiler Directives Determines which kind of compiler is currently used. It can be one of the following:
#PB_Compiler_Console Compiler Directives Console executable (have an effect only on Windows, other act like a regular executable)
#PB_Compiler_Date Compiler Directives Current date, at the compile time, in the PureBasic date format (local time).
#PB_Compiler_Debugger Compiler Directives Set to 1 if the runtime debugger is enabled, set to 0 else. When an executable is created, the debugger is always disabled (this constant will be 0).
#PB_Compiler_DLL Compiler Directives Shared DLL (dynlib on MacOS X and shared object on Linux)
#PB_Compiler_DPIAware Compiler Directives Set to 1 if the compiler generates a DPI aware executable, set to 0 else.
#PB_Compiler_EnableExplicit Compiler Directives Set to 1 if the executable is compiled with enable explicit support, set to 0 else.
#PB_Compiler_Executable Compiler Directives Regular executable
#PB_Compiler_ExecutableFormat Compiler Directives Determines executable format. It can be one of the following:
#PB_Compiler_File Compiler Directives Full path and name of the file being compiled, useful for debug purpose.
#PB_Compiler_Filename Compiler Directives Filename (without path) of the file being compiled, useful for debug purpose.
#PB_Compiler_FilePath Compiler Directives Full path of the file being compiled, useful for debug purpose.
#PB_Compiler_Home Compiler Directives Full path of the PureBasic directory, can be useful to locate include files
#PB_Compiler_InlineAssembly Compiler Directives Set to 1 if the executable is compiled with inline assembly support, set to 0 else.
#PB_Compiler_IsIncludeFile Compiler Directives Set to 1 if the file being compiled has been included by another file, set to 0 else.
#PB_Compiler_IsMainFile Compiler Directives Set to 1 if the file being compiled is the main file, set to 0 else.
#PB_Compiler_Line Compiler Directives Line number of the file being compiled, useful for debug purpose.
#PB_Compiler_LineNumbering Compiler Directives Set to 1 if the executable is compiled with OnError line numbering support, set to 0 else.
#PB_Compiler_Module Compiler Directives Current module name, if the line is inside a module.
#PB_Compiler_Optimizer Compiler Directives Set to 1 if the compiler generates optimized code, set to 0 else.
#PB_Compiler_OS Compiler Directives Determines on which OS the compiler is currently running. It can be one of the following values:
#PB_Compiler_Procedure Compiler Directives Current procedure name, if the line is inside a procedure.
#PB_Compiler_Processor Compiler Directives Determines the processor type for which the program is created. It can be one of the following:
#PB_Compiler_Thread Compiler Directives Set to 1 if the executable is compiled in thread safe mode, set to 0 else.
#PB_Compiler_Unicode Compiler Directives Set to 1 if the executable is compiled in unicode mode, set to 0 else.
#PB_Compiler_Version Compiler Directives Compiler version, in integer format in the form '420' for 4.20.

#PB_Database_Blob DatabaseColumnType Blob format
#PB_Database_Double DatabaseColumnType Numeric double format (a Double (.d) in PureBasic)
#PB_Database_DynamicCursor DatabaseQuery performs the query to access the result in a random manner using PreviousDatabaseRow or FirstDatabaseRow. It can be slower, or even unsupported on some drivers.
#PB_Database_Float DatabaseColumnType Numeric float format (a Float (.f) in PureBasic)
#PB_Database_Long DatabaseColumnType Numeric format (a Long (.l) in PureBasic)
#PB_Database_MySQL OpenDatabase The database will use MySQL backend (UseMySQLDatabase has to be called). OpenDatabase(5)
#PB_Database_ODBC OpenDatabase, OpenDatabaseRequester The database will use ODBC backend (UseODBCDatabase has to be called). OpenDatabase(5), OpenDatabaseRequester(2)
#PB_Database_PostgreSQL OpenDatabase The database will use PostgreSQL backend (UsePostgreSQLDatabase has to be called). OpenDatabase(5)
#PB_Database_Quad DatabaseColumnType Numeric quad format (a Quad (.q) in PureBasic)
#PB_Database_SQLite OpenDatabase The database will use SQLite backend (UseSQLiteDatabase has to be called). OpenDatabase(5)
#PB_Database_StaticCursor DatabaseQuery performs the query to access the result in a sequential manner. It's not possible to rewind with PreviousDatabaseRow or FirstDatabaseRow on some drivers, but it is the faster way to get the data (default).
#PB_Database_String DatabaseColumnType String format (a String (.s) in PureBasic)

#PB_Entity_StaticBody CreateEntityBody, AddSubEntity The body is a static only, which means the mesh can't be animated. This mode allows very precise collisions, as it's done against triangles (also known as tri-mesh collision). It's also fast when colliding with a box or sphere entity body type. It's perfect when using a mesh for a ground or static world. AddSubEntity(3), CreateEntityBody(2)
#PB_Entity_WorldBoundingBox EntityBoundingBox Positions are returned in world coordinates (default) EntityBoundingBox(2)
#PB_EntityAnimation_Average EntityAnimationBlendMode The blend will result of the average of the two animations (default). For example, if the first animation rotates an arm 40 degrees and the second animation rotates the arm 90 degrees, the arm will rotate (40+90)/2 = 65 degrees (if the both animation are played with full weight). EntityAnimationBlendMode(1)
#PB_EntityAnimation_Cumulative EntityAnimationBlendMode The blend will sum the two animations. For example, if the first animation rotates an arm 40 degrees and the second animation rotates the arm 90 degrees, the arm will rotate 40+90 = 130 degrees (if the both animation are played with full weight). EntityAnimationBlendMode(1)
#PB_EntityAnimation_Manual StartEntityAnimation Start the animation in manual mode, the time won't be automatically added after each RenderWorld. StartEntityAnimation(3)
#PB_EntityAnimation_Once StartEntityAnimation Play the animation only once. By default the animation loops automatically when its end is reached. StartEntityAnimation(3)
#PB_EntityAnimation_Started EntityAnimationStatus The animation is running.
#PB_EntityAnimation_Stopped EntityAnimationStatus The animation is stopped (or has ended).
#PB_EntityAnimation_Unknown EntityAnimationStatus The animation doesn't exist in the mesh object.

#PB_Event3D_ActivateWindow WindowEvent3D the window has been activated (got the focus)
#PB_Event3D_CloseWindow WindowEvent3D the window close gadget has been pushed

#PB_Event3D_SizeWindow WindowEvent3D the window has been resized
#PB_Event_* All constants starting with #PB_Event_ BindEvent(1), PostEvent(1), UnbindEvent(1)
#PB_Event_ActivateWindow ScreenWindowEvent, WindowEvent the window has been activated (got the focus) BindEvent(1), PostEvent(1), UnbindEvent(1)
#PB_Event_CloseWindow ScreenWindowEvent, WindowEvent the window close gadget has been pushed BindEvent(1), PostEvent(1), UnbindEvent(1)
#PB_Event_DeactivateWindow WindowEvent the window has been deactivated (lost the focus) BindEvent(1), PostEvent(1), UnbindEvent(1)
#PB_Event_Gadget ScreenWindowEvent, WindowEvent a ScreenGadget has been used BindEvent(1), PostEvent(1), UnbindEvent(1)
#PB_Event_GadgetDrop WindowEvent a Drag & Drop operation was finished on a gadget BindEvent(1), PostEvent(1), UnbindEvent(1)
#PB_Event_LeftClick WindowEvent a left mouse button click has occurred on the window BindEvent(1), PostEvent(1), UnbindEvent(1)
#PB_Event_LeftDoubleClick WindowEvent a left mouse button double-click has occurred on the window BindEvent(1), PostEvent(1), UnbindEvent(1)
#PB_Event_MaximizeWindow WindowEvent the window has been maximized BindEvent(1), PostEvent(1), UnbindEvent(1)
#PB_Event_Menu WindowEvent a menu has been selected BindEvent(1), PostEvent(1), UnbindEvent(1)
#PB_Event_MinimizeWindow WindowEvent the window has been minimized BindEvent(1), PostEvent(1), UnbindEvent(1)
#PB_Event_MoveWindow ScreenWindowEvent, WindowEvent the window has been moved BindEvent(1), PostEvent(1), UnbindEvent(1)
#PB_Event_Repaint WindowEvent the window content has been destroyed and must be repainted (useful for 2D graphics operations) BindEvent(1), PostEvent(1), UnbindEvent(1)
#PB_Event_RestoreWindow WindowEvent the window has been restored to normal size (either from a minimum or maximum size) BindEvent(1), PostEvent(1), UnbindEvent(1)
#PB_Event_RightClick WindowEvent a right mouse button click has occurred on the window. This can be useful to display a popup menu BindEvent(1), PostEvent(1), UnbindEvent(1)
#PB_Event_SizeWindow ScreenWindowEvent, WindowEvent the window has been resized BindEvent(1), PostEvent(1), UnbindEvent(1)
#PB_Event_SysTray WindowEvent an icon in the systray zone was clicked BindEvent(1), PostEvent(1), UnbindEvent(1)
#PB_Event_Timer WindowEvent a timer has reached its timeout BindEvent(1), PostEvent(1), UnbindEvent(1)
#PB_Event_WindowDrop WindowEvent a Drag & Drop operation was finished on a window BindEvent(1), PostEvent(1), UnbindEvent(1)
#PB_Event_WindowResolutionChanged WindowEvent the window has been moved to a screen with a different DPI, and it (and its gadgets) have been rescaled. The new scale factor is available from WindowResolutionX / WindowResolutionY. Only fired on Windows, for executables compiled with the 'DPI Aware' switch set to 'Per-Monitor'. BindEvent(1), PostEvent(1), UnbindEvent(1)

#PB_Explorer_DrivesOnly ExplorerComboGadget The gadget will only display drives to choose from. ExplorerComboGadget(7)

#PB_Explorer_FullRowSelect ExplorerListGadget The selection covers the full row instead of the first column. ExplorerListGadget(7)

#PB_Explorer_LargeIcon ExplorerListGadget Large icon mode
#PB_Explorer_List ExplorerListGadget List icon mode

#PB_Explorer_MultiSelect ExplorerListGadget Enable multiple selection of items in the gadget. ExplorerListGadget(7)
#PB_Explorer_Name AddGadgetColumn displays the name of the file/directory AddGadgetColumn(3)

#PB_Explorer_NoFolders ExplorerListGadget No folders will be displayed. ExplorerListGadget(7)

#PB_Explorer_NoParentFolder ExplorerListGadget There will be no [..] link to the parent folder. ExplorerListGadget(7)

#PB_HID_Manufacturer HIDInfo the manufacturer.
#PB_HID_Path HIDInfo the platform-specific device path.
#PB_HID_Product HIDInfo the product.
#PB_HID_ProductId HIDInfo the device product ID.
#PB_HID_ReleaseNumber HIDInfo the device release number in binary-coded decimal, also known as device version number.
#PB_HID_SerialNumber HIDInfo the serial number.
#PB_HID_Usage HIDInfo the usage for this device.
#PB_HID_UsagePage HIDInfo the usage page this device.
#PB_HID_VendorId HIDInfo the device vendor ID.

#PB_HTTP_Aborted HTTPProgress the download has been aborted with AbortHTTP.
#PB_HTTP_Asynchronous ReceiveHTTPFile, ReceiveHTTPMemory, HTTPRequest, HTTPRequestMemory starts the download asynchronously. HTTPRequest(4), HTTPRequestMemory(5), ReceiveHTTPFile(3), ReceiveHTTPMemory(2)
#PB_HTTP_Debug ReceiveHTTPFile, ReceiveHTTPMemory, HTTPRequest, HTTPRequestMemory to print in the console debug information. HTTPRequest(4), HTTPRequestMemory(5), ReceiveHTTPFile(3), ReceiveHTTPMemory(2)
#PB_HTTP_Delete HTTPRequest, HTTPRequestMemory DELETE request ('Data$' parameter will be sent if specified) HTTPRequest(1), HTTPRequestMemory(1)
#PB_HTTP_ErrorMessage HTTPInfo the HTTP request error message, if something goes wrong (mostly for debugging purpose). HTTPInfo(2)
#PB_HTTP_Failed HTTPProgress the download has failed.
#PB_HTTP_Get HTTPRequest, HTTPRequestMemory GET request ('Data$' parameter will be ignored) HTTPRequest(1), HTTPRequestMemory(1)
#PB_HTTP_Headers HTTPInfo the request headers. HTTPInfo(2)
#PB_HTTP_HeadersOnly HTTPRequest, HTTPRequestMemory gets headers only. HTTPRequest(4), HTTPRequestMemory(5)
#PB_HTTP_NoRedirect ReceiveHTTPFile, ReceiveHTTPMemory, HTTPRequest, HTTPRequestMemory don't follow automatic redirections. GetHTTPHeader(2), HTTPRequest(4), HTTPRequestMemory(5), ReceiveHTTPFile(3), ReceiveHTTPMemory(2)
#PB_HTTP_NoSSLCheck ReceiveHTTPFile, ReceiveHTTPMemory, HTTPRequest, HTTPRequestMemory don't check if the SSL certificate is valid (can be useful for testing purpose). HTTPRequest(4), HTTPRequestMemory(5), ReceiveHTTPFile(3), ReceiveHTTPMemory(2)
#PB_HTTP_Patch HTTPRequest, HTTPRequestMemory PATCH request ('Data$' parameter will be sent if specified) HTTPRequest(1), HTTPRequestMemory(1)
#PB_HTTP_Post HTTPRequest, HTTPRequestMemory POST request ('Data$' parameter will be sent if specified) HTTPRequest(1), HTTPRequestMemory(1)
#PB_HTTP_Put HTTPRequest, HTTPRequestMemory PUT request ('Data$' parameter will be sent if specified) HTTPRequest(1), HTTPRequestMemory(1)
#PB_HTTP_Response HTTPInfo the server response, as text. To get the raw server response, use HTTPMemory. HTTPInfo(2)
#PB_HTTP_StatusCode HTTPInfo the server status code (200: OK, 404: page not found etc.). HTTPInfo(2)
#PB_HTTP_Success HTTPProgress the download has been successfully finished.
#PB_HTTP_WeakSSL ReceiveHTTPFile, ReceiveHTTPMemory, HTTPRequest, HTTPRequestMemory to support older servers. HTTPRequest(4), HTTPRequestMemory(5), ReceiveHTTPFile(3), ReceiveHTTPMemory(2)

Valid return values are: - 1 (1-bit, 2 colors, monochrome image) - 4 (4-bit, 16 colors) - 8 (8-bit, 256 colors) - 16 (16-bit, 65536 colors) - 24 (24-bit, 16 millions colors) - 32 (32-bit, 16 millions colors + 8-bit alpha channel) ImageDepth(2)

#PB_PackerPlugin_Jcalg1 UncompressMemory use the Jcalg1 packer to uncompress the memory. UseJcalg1Packer has to be called to have any effect. UncompressMemory(5)
#PB_PackerPlugin_Lzma CompressMemory, CreatePack, OpenPack, CatchPack, UncompressMemory use the Lzma packer to compress the memory. UseLzmaPacker has to be called to register the plugin. CompressMemory(5), CreatePack(3), OpenPack(3), UncompressMemory(5)
#PB_PackerPlugin_Tar CreatePack, OpenPack, CatchPack use the Tar packer to create the pack file. UseTarPacker has to be called to register the plugin. It can be combined with #PB_Packer_Gzip, #PB_Packer_Bzip2 or #PB_Packer_Xz to create compressed tar archive. CreatePack(3), OpenPack(3)
#PB_PackerPlugin_Zip CompressMemory, CreatePack, OpenPack, CatchPack, UncompressMemory use the Zip packer to compress the memory. UseZipPacker has to be called to register the plugin. CompressMemory(5), CreatePack(3), OpenPack(3), UncompressMemory(5)

#PB_Shadow_Additive WorldShadows shadows will be displayed for the entities which have the cast shadow set with EntityRenderMode and #PB_Entity_CastShadow. This mode is slower than the modulative mode, but it looks much better as the shadows are translucent. Also if some shadows overlap, the shadows will be added resulting in a more realistic darker result.
#PB_Shadow_Color GetWorldAttribute, SetWorldAttribute get the current shadow color as RGBA.
#PB_Shadow_FarDistance GetWorldAttribute, SetWorldAttribute get shadow far distance.
#PB_Shadow_Modulative WorldShadows shadows will be displayed for entities that have the cast shadow set with EntityRenderMode and #PB_Entity_CastShadow. This shadow mode is the fastest available, but is not very good-looking as the shadows are not translucent.
#PB_Shadow_None WorldShadows, EntityRenderMode No shadows will be displayed in the world. This can save a lot of CPU power if shadows aren't needed (default) EntityRenderMode(2)
#PB_Shadow_TextureAdditive WorldShadows shadows will be displayed for the entities which have the cast shadow set with EntityRenderMode and #PB_Entity_CastShadow. This mode is average in speed and quality between modulative and additive shadow, and will work even with water.
#PB_Shadow_TextureModulative WorldShadows shadows will be displayed for the entities which have the cast shadow set with EntityRenderMode and #PB_Entity_CastShadow. This shadow mode is the faster than #PB_Shadow_TextureAdditive but is not very good-looking as the shadows are not translucent.

#PB_SliderJoint_UpperLimit SliderJoint Upper limit of the joint GetJointAttribute(2), SetJointAttribute(2)
#PB_Sort_Ascending CustomSortArray, CustomSortList, SortArray, SortList, SortStructuredArray, SortStructuredList Sort the array in ascending order (lower values first). This is the default. SortArray(2), SortList(2), SortStructuredArray(2), SortStructuredList(2)
#PB_Sort_Descending CustomSortArray, CustomSortList, SortArray, SortList, SortStructuredArray, SortStructuredList Sort the array in descending order (higher values first) SortArray(2), SortList(2), SortStructuredArray(2), SortStructuredList(2)
#PB_Sort_Equal CustomSortArray, CustomSortList Both elements are equal.
#PB_Sort_Greater CustomSortArray, CustomSortList The first element is greater than the second one.
#PB_Sort_Lesser CustomSortArray, CustomSortList The first element is lesser than the second one.
#PB_Sort_NoCase SortArray, SortList, SortStructuredArray, SortStructuredList Sort the string array without case sensitivity (a=A, b=B etc..) SortArray(2), SortList(2), SortStructuredArray(2), SortStructuredList(2)
#PB_Sound3D_Loop PlaySound3D play the sound continuously (starts again when end is reached)
#PB_Sound3D_Streaming LoadSound3D Enable sound streaming playback
#PB_Sound_Frame GetSoundPosition, SetSoundPosition, SoundLength the position is returned in frame (default). GetSoundPosition(2), SetSoundPosition(3), SoundLength(2)
#PB_Sound_Loop PlaySound play the sound continuously (starts again when end is reached) PlaySound(2), PlaySound3D(2)
#PB_Sound_Millisecond GetSoundPosition, SetSoundPosition, SoundLength the position is returned in milliseconds. GetSoundPosition(2), SetSoundPosition(3), SoundLength(2)
#PB_Sound_MultiChannel PlaySound play the sound in a new channel instead of stopping the previously played sound. This allows to use the same sound and to play it on different channels at once. 'Result' will be new allocated channel, and can be used by the other sound commands like SoundVolume, SoundPan etc. PlaySound(2)
#PB_Sound_Paused SoundStatus the sound is paused.
#PB_Sound_Playing SoundStatus the sound is playing.
#PB_Sound_Stopped SoundStatus the sound is stopped.
#PB_Sound_Streaming CatchSound, LoadSound Enable streaming playback (only supported for FLAC, OGG and Opus)) CatchSound(4), LoadSound(3), LoadSound3D(3)
#PB_Sound_Unknown SoundStatus the sound is in an unknown state (an error occurred when getting the state).
#PB_SoundPlugin_FLAC SaveSound Save the sound as lossless FLAC (UseFLACSoundEncoder has to be used). Only 16-bit mono/stereo sounds are supported.
#PB_SoundPlugin_MP3 SaveSound Save the sound as lossy MP3 (UseMP3SoundEncoder has to be used). Only 16-bit mono/stereo sounds are supported.
#PB_SoundPlugin_OGG SaveSound Save the sound as lossy OGG Vorbis (UseOGGSoundEncoder has to be used). Only 16-bit mono/stereo sounds are supported.
#PB_SoundPlugin_Opus SaveSound Save the sound as lossy Opus (UseOpusSoundEncoder has to be used). Only 16-bit mono/stereo sounds are supported, and the sound's sample rate must already be one of 8000, 12000, 16000, 24000 or 48000 hz.
#PB_SoundPlugin_WAV SaveSound Save the sound as an uncompressed PCM WAV file (default)
#PB_Spin3D_Maximum SpinGadget3D Returns the maximum value.
#PB_Spin3D_Minimum SpinGadget3D Returns the minimum value.
#PB_Spin_Maximum SpinGadget Returns the maximum value.
#PB_Spin_Minimum SpinGadget Returns the minimum value.
#PB_Spin_Numeric SpinGadget The SpinGadget will automatically update the text with value of the state, so SetGadgetText is not needed. SpinGadget(8)
#PB_Spin_ReadOnly SpinGadget The StringGadget is not editable, the number is only changeable by the arrows SpinGadget(8)
#PB_Splitter_FirstFixed SplitterGadget When the splitter gadget is resized, the first gadget will keep its size SplitterGadget(8)
#PB_Splitter_FirstGadget SplitterGadget Gets the gadget number of the first gadget.
#PB_Splitter_FirstMinimumSize SplitterGadget Gets the minimum size (in pixels) than the first gadget can have.
#PB_Splitter_SecondFixed SplitterGadget When the splitter gadget is resized, the second gadget will keep its size SplitterGadget(8)
#PB_Splitter_SecondGadget SplitterGadget Gets the gadget number of the second gadget.
#PB_Splitter_SecondMinimumSize SplitterGadget Gets the minimum size (in pixels) than the second gadget can have.
#PB_Splitter_Separator SplitterGadget A 3D-looking separator is drawn in the splitter. SplitterGadget(8)
#PB_Splitter_Vertical SplitterGadget The gadget is split vertically (instead of horizontally which is the default). SplitterGadget(8)
#PB_Sprite_AlphaBlending CatchSprite, CopySprite, CreateSprite, GrabSprite, LoadSprite Sprite is created with per pixel alpha-channel support, needed for DisplayTransparentSprite. The image format has to support it (only PNG and TIFF for now). CatchSprite(3), CopySprite(3), CreateSprite(4), GrabSprite(6), LoadSprite(3)
#PB_Sprite_BilinearFiltering SpriteQuality Bilinear filtering, slower but clean when zooming/rotating. SpriteQuality(1)
#PB_Sprite_BlendDestinationAlpha SpriteBlendingMode(1,2)
#PB_Sprite_BlendDestinationColor SpriteBlendingMode(1,2)
#PB_Sprite_BlendInvertDestinationAlpha SpriteBlendingMode(1,2)
#PB_Sprite_BlendInvertDestinationColor SpriteBlendingMode(1,2)
#PB_Sprite_BlendInvertSourceAlpha SpriteBlendingMode(1,2)
#PB_Sprite_BlendInvertSourceColor SpriteBlendingMode(1,2)
#PB_Sprite_BlendOne SpriteBlendingMode(1,2)
#PB_Sprite_BlendSourceAlpha SpriteBlendingMode(1,2)
#PB_Sprite_BlendSourceColor SpriteBlendingMode(1,2)
#PB_Sprite_BlendZero SpriteBlendingMode(1,2)
#PB_Sprite_NoFiltering SpriteQuality No filtering, faster but ugly when zooming/rotating (default). SpriteQuality(1)
#PB_Sprite_Overwrite SpriteOutput, SpriteVectorOutput The previous sprite content is not read, the drawing starts on a fully transparent output. Faster when the whole sprite is redrawn.
#PB_Sprite_PixelCollision CatchSprite, CopySprite, CreateSprite, GrabSprite, LoadSprite Add special information to handle pixel collision through SpritePixelCollision. CatchSprite(3), CopySprite(3), CreateSprite(4), GrabSprite(6), LoadSprite(3)
#PB_Sprite_Transparent CreateSprite Sprite is created fully transparent (alpha channel value set to 0). If used, DrawingMode should be set to #PB_2DDrawing_AllChannels when using SpriteOutput.
#PB_StatusBar_BorderLess StatusBarImage, StatusBarText, StatusBarProgress without border StatusBarImage(4), StatusBarProgress(4), StatusBarText(4)
#PB_StatusBar_Center StatusBarImage, StatusBarText center the icon in the field StatusBarImage(4), StatusBarText(4)
#PB_StatusBar_Raised StatusBarImage, StatusBarText, StatusBarProgress raised borders (has no effect on OS X and Windows with theme enabled) StatusBarImage(4), StatusBarProgress(4), StatusBarText(4)
#PB_StatusBar_Right StatusBarImage, StatusBarText align the icon to the right of the field StatusBarImage(4), StatusBarText(4)
#PB_String SortStructuredArray, SortStructuredList The structure field to sort is a string (.s or $, fixed strings are not supported) SortStructuredArray(4), SortStructuredList(4)
#PB_String3D_Numeric StringGadget3D Only (positive) integer numbers are accepted. StringGadget3D(7)
#PB_String3D_Password StringGadget3D Password mode, displaying only '*' instead of normal characters. StringGadget3D(7)
#PB_String3D_ReadOnly StringGadget3D Read-only mode. No text can be entered. StringGadget3D(7)
#PB_String_BorderLess StringGadget No borders are drawn around the gadget. StringGadget(7)
#PB_String_CaseSensitive CompareArray, CompareList, CompareMap, CompareMemoryString, Compiler Functions, FindString, RemoveString, ReplaceString String comparison is case sensitive (a=a). (default) CompareMemoryString(3), FindString(4), RemoveString(3), ReplaceString(4)
#PB_String_Equal CompareMemoryString if String1 equals String2
#PB_String_EscapeInternal EscapeString, UnescapeString escape the string using PureBasic internal format (see General rules for accepted escape sequences) (default). EscapeString(2), UnescapeString(2)
#PB_String_EscapeJSON EscapeString, UnescapeString escape the string using the JSON escape characters. This can be useful to easily put any string in a JSON value. EscapeString(2), UnescapeString(2)
#PB_String_EscapeXML EscapeString, UnescapeString escape the string using the XML escape characters. This can be useful to easily put any string in a XML tree. EscapeString(2), UnescapeString(2)
#PB_String_Greater CompareMemoryString if String1 greater than String2
#PB_String_Lower CompareMemoryString if String1 is lower than String2
#PB_String_LowerCase StringGadget All characters are converted to lower case automatically. StringGadget(7)
#PB_String_MaximumLength StringGadget Returns the maximum number of characters which can be entered.
#PB_String_NoCase CompareArray, CompareList, CompareMap, CompareMemoryString, Compiler Functions, FindString, RemoveString, ReplaceString String comparison is case insensitive(a=A). CompareMemoryString(3), FindString(4), RemoveString(3), ReplaceString(4)
#PB_String_NoCaseAscii CompareMemoryString Case insensitive search using only ascii character set (a=A). Much faster than #PB_String_NoCase when full unicode support is not required. CompareMemoryString(3)
#PB_String_NoZero PokeS Doesn't write the terminating null-character. PokeS(4)
#PB_String_Numeric StringGadget Only (positive) integer numbers are accepted. StringGadget(7)
#PB_String_Password StringGadget Password mode, displaying only '*' instead of normal characters. StringGadget(7)
#PB_String_PlaceHolder StringGadget The 'Content$' paramater will be used as place holder (an informative text displayed when the gadget is empty). StringGadget(7)
#PB_String_ReadOnly StringGadget, StringScreenGadget Read-only mode. No text can be entered. StringGadget(7)
#PB_String_UpperCase StringGadget All characters are converted to upper case automatically. StringGadget(7)
#PB_Structure Defined(2)
#PB_System_CPUs CountCPUs the total number of CPU cores installed in the computer (default). CountCPUs(1)
#PB_System_FreePhysical MemoryStatus the available memory, in bytes MemoryStatus(1)
#PB_System_FreeSwap MemoryStatus the available swap memory size, in bytes (Windows and Linux only) MemoryStatus(1)
#PB_System_FreeVirtual MemoryStatus the available virtual memory size, in bytes (Windows only) MemoryStatus(1)
#PB_System_PageSize MemoryStatus the memory page size, in bytes (usually 4KB). MemoryStatus(1)
#PB_System_ProcessCPUs CountCPUs the available CPU cores for the current process. This is useful as the OS can limit a process to use only a small number of CPU. CountCPUs(1)
#PB_System_TotalPhysical MemoryStatus the total amount of installed memory, in bytes MemoryStatus(1)
#PB_System_TotalSwap MemoryStatus the total swap memory size, in bytes (Windows and Linux only) MemoryStatus(1)
#PB_System_TotalVirtual MemoryStatus the total virtual memory size, in bytes (Windows only) MemoryStatus(1)
#PB_Terrain_CastShadows TerrainRenderMode enables dynamic shadow casting on the terrain (can be slow).
#PB_Terrain_Lightmap SetupTerrains enable the light map for the terrains (a texture with static shadows). SetupTerrains(3)
#PB_Terrain_LowLODShadows TerrainRenderMode enables low quality shadow casting (to have a faster rendering).
#PB_Terrain_NormalMapping SetupTerrains enable the normal mapping for the terrains. This is a special texture which simulate relief like small rocks, etc. SetupTerrains(3)
#PB_Text3D_Bottom Text3DAlignment the text will be bottom aligned Text3DAlignment(2)
#PB_Text3D_HorizontallyCentered Text3DAlignment the text will be centered horizontally Text3DAlignment(2)
#PB_Text3D_Left Text3DAlignment the text will be left aligned Text3DAlignment(2)
#PB_Text3D_Top Text3DAlignment the text will be top aligned Text3DAlignment(2)
#PB_Text3D_VerticallyCentered Text3DAlignment the text will be centered vertically Text3DAlignment(2)

#PB_Text_Center TextGadget The text is centered in the gadget. TextGadget(7)
#PB_Text_Right TextGadget The text is right aligned. TextGadget(7)
#PB_Texture_AutomaticUpdate CreateRenderTexture the texture is updated at every RenderWorld automatically (default) CreateRenderTexture(5)
#PB_Texture_CameraViewPort CreateRenderTexture the camera viewport won't be removed, useful to still be able to do a capture from the camera. CreateRenderTexture(5)
#PB_Texture_ManualUpdate CreateRenderTexture the texture is not updated automatically, UpdateRenderTexture has to be called manually. CreateRenderTexture(5)
#PB_Texture_Overwrite TextureOutput The previous texture content is not read back from the graphic card, the drawing starts on a fully transparent output. Faster when the whole texture is redrawn.

#PB_ToolBar_Toggle ToolBarImageButton the button will act as toggle button ToolBarImageButton(3)

#PB_TrackBar_Vertical TrackBarGadget The trackbar is vertical (instead of horizontal which is the default). TrackBarGadget(8)

#PB_Web_Back WebGadget One step back in the navigation history.
#PB_Web_BlockPopupMenu WebGadget Block standard the popup menu. #PB_EventType_PopupMenu is fired if this setting is enabled (Windows only).
#PB_Web_BlockPopups WebGadget Block popup windows. #PB_EventType_PopupWindow is fired if this setting is enabled (Windows only).
#PB_Web_Busy WebGadget Returns nonzero if the gadget is busy loading a page.
#PB_Web_Edge WebGadget Uses the WebView2 engine to render the web page (Windows only). WebView2 is the Edge based component to have modern web page display in Windows application. It's built-in for up-to-date Windows 10 and Windows 11. For older Windows version, it needs to be installed (if not already): distribution guide. WebGadget(7)
#PB_Web_Forward WebGadget One step forward in the navigation history.
#PB_Web_HtmlCode WebGadget Get the current html code from the gadget, including the changes done by scripts or by the user (for example in a 'contenteditable' element). GetGadgetItemText(2), SetGadgetItemText(2)
#PB_Web_NavigationCallback WebGadget Set a callback for monitoring (and disabling) navigation.
#PB_Web_PageTitle WebGadget Get the current title for the displayed page. GetGadgetItemText(2)
#PB_Web_Progress WebGadget Returns the current (sometimes estimated) progress after a #PB_EventType_DownloadProgress event.
#PB_Web_ProgressMax WebGadget Returns the current (sometimes estimated) maximum progress after a #PB_EventType_DownloadProgress event.
#PB_Web_Refresh WebGadget Refresh the current page.
#PB_Web_ScrollX WebGadget Set the horizontal scrolling position (Windows only).
#PB_Web_ScrollY WebGadget Set the vertical scrolling position (Windows only).
#PB_Web_SelectedText WebGadget Get the currently selected text inside the gadget. GetGadgetItemText(2)
#PB_Web_StatusMessage WebGadget Get the current statusbar message. GetGadgetItemText(2)
#PB_Web_Stop WebGadget Stop loading the current page.
#PB_WebView_Debug WebViewGadget Enable the 'inspect' menu item in the context menu to display the web inspector and console. Not supported yet on the Qt subsystem. WebViewGadget(6)
#PB_WebView_HtmlCode SetGadgetItemText(2)
#PB_Window3D_BorderLess OpenWindow3D Creates a window without any borders. OpenWindow3D(7)
#PB_Window3D_Invisible OpenWindow3D Creates the window but doesn't display it. OpenWindow3D(7)
#PB_Window3D_SizeGadget OpenWindow3D Adds the sizeable feature to a window. OpenWindow3D(7)
#PB_Window_BorderLess OpenWindow Creates a window without any borders. OpenWindow(7)
#PB_Window_FrameCoordinate WindowHeight, WindowWidth, WindowX, WindowY height of the window, including borders. WindowHeight(2), WindowWidth(2), WindowX(2), WindowY(2)
#PB_Window_InnerCoordinate WindowHeight, WindowWidth, WindowX, WindowY height of the window inner area (where gadget can be added), excluding borders (default). WindowHeight(2), WindowWidth(2), WindowX(2), WindowY(2)
#PB_Window_Invisible OpenWindow Creates the window but don't display. AddGadgetItem(5), OpenWindow(7)
#PB_Window_Maximize GetWindowState, OpenWindow, SetWindowState The window is maximized. AddGadgetItem(5), OpenWindow(7), SetWindowState(2)
#PB_Window_MaximizeGadget OpenWindow Adds the maximize gadget to the window title bar. #PB_Window_SystemMenu is automatically added. (MacOS only: #PB_Window_SizeGadget will be also automatically added). AddGadgetItem(5), OpenWindow(7)
#PB_Window_Minimize GetWindowState, OpenWindow, SetWindowState The window is minimized. AddGadgetItem(5), OpenWindow(7), SetWindowState(2)
#PB_Window_MinimizeGadget OpenWindow Adds the minimize gadget to the window title bar. #PB_Window_SystemMenu is automatically added. AddGadgetItem(5), OpenWindow(7)
#PB_Window_Modal OpenWindow Disables the parent window ('ParentID' parameter must be specified) until the new window is closed, so the user has to deal with the new window first. The parent window is automatically re-enabled by CloseWindow.
#PB_Window_NoActivate HideWindow, OpenWindow the window will be shown but not activated (only valid when un-hiding the window). AddGadgetItem(5), HideWindow(3), OpenWindow(7)
#PB_Window_NoChildEvents SetWindowCallback the child gadgets events won't be sent to the main window (WinAPI default behavior). SetWindowCallback(3)
#PB_Window_NoGadgets OpenWindow Prevents the creation of a GadgetList. UseGadgetList can be used to do this later. AddGadgetItem(5), OpenWindow(7)
#PB_Window_Normal GetWindowState, SetWindowState The window is neither maximized nor minimized. SetWindowState(2)
#PB_Window_ProcessChildEvents SetWindowCallback the child gadgets events (mostly #WM_NOTIFY) will be sent to the main window. Doesn't work for all gadgets (default). SetWindowCallback(3)
#PB_Window_ScreenCentered HideWindow, OpenWindow the window will be screen centered (only valid when un-hiding the window). HideWindow(3), OpenWindow(7)
#PB_Window_SizeGadget OpenWindow Adds the sizeable feature to a window. AddGadgetItem(5), OpenWindow(7)
#PB_Window_SystemMenu OpenWindow Enables the system menu on the window title bar (default). AddGadgetItem(5), OpenWindow(7)

Database (40)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
AffectedDatabaseRows Result = AffectedDatabaseRows(#Database) Returns the number of rows affected by the last DatabaseUpdate operation. Returns the number of rows affected by the last DatabaseUpdate operation.
CheckDatabaseNull Result = CheckDatabaseNull(#Database, Column) Checks if the content of the specified database column is null. This command is only valid after a successful FirstDatabaseRow, PreviousDatabaseRow or NextDatabaseRow. Returns #True is the data is null, #False otherwise.
CloseDatabase CloseDatabase(#Database) Close the specified #Database (and connections/transactions if any). No further operations are allowed on this database. None
DatabaseColumnIndex Result = DatabaseColumnIndex(#Database, ColumnName$) Returns the index of the column after executing a query with DatabaseQuery in the opened #Database. This can be useful for use with commands like GetDatabaseLong which require a column index. Returns the index of the specified column, -1 if #ColumnName$ is invalid. This is only valid after having executed a query with DatabaseQuery.
DatabaseColumnName Text$ = DatabaseColumnName(#Database, Column) Return the name of the specified column in the #Database. Returns the name of the column.
DatabaseColumns Result = DatabaseColumns(#Database) Returns the numbers of columns (fields) from the last executed database query with DatabaseQuery. Returns the number of columns from the last database query.
DatabaseColumnSize Result = DatabaseColumnSize(#Database, Column) Return the size of the specified column in the #Database. It is especially useful when the size of the column can change depending of the records, like a blob or string column. Returns the size of the column in bytes.
DatabaseColumnType Result = DatabaseColumnType(#Database, Column) Return the type of the specified column in the #Database. Returns the type of the given column. If Result is 0, the type is undefined or the function has failed (e.g. it was not possible to determine the data type). Type values can be: #PB_Database_Long : Numeric format (a Long (.l) in PureBasic) #PB_Database_String: String format (a String (.s) in PureBasic) #PB_Database_Float : Numeric float format (a Float (.f) in PureBasic) #PB_Database_Double: Numeric double format (a Double (.d) in PureBasic) #PB_Database_Quad : Numeric quad format (a Quad (.q) in PureBasic) #PB_Database_Blob : Blob format
DatabaseDriverDescription Text$ = DatabaseDriverDescription() Returns the description of the current database driver. Drivers are listed using the ExamineDatabaseDrivers and NextDatabaseDriver functions. Returns the description string.
DatabaseDriverName Text$ = DatabaseDriverName() Return the name of the current database driver. Drivers are listed using the ExamineDatabaseDrivers and NextDatabaseDriver functions. Returns the name of the driver.
DatabaseError Error$ = DatabaseError() Returns a description of the last database error in text format. This is especially useful with the following functions: OpenDatabase, DatabaseQuery and DatabaseUpdate. Returns the error description.
DatabaseID DatabaseID = DatabaseID(#Database) Returns the unique ID which identifies the given '#Database' in the operating system. This function is useful when another library needs a database reference. Returns the ID for this database connection.
DatabaseQuery Result = DatabaseQuery(#Database, Request$ [, Flags]) Executes a SQL query on the given database. Only queries which doesn't change the database records are accepted ('SELECT' like queries). To performs database modification, use DatabaseUpdate. Returns nonzero if the query was successful or zero if it failed (due to a SQL error or a badly-formatted query).
DatabaseUpdate Result = DatabaseUpdate(#Database, Request$) Executes a modification query on the given database. This command doesn't return any record. To perform a 'SELECT' like query, use DatabaseQuery. Returns nonzero if the query was successful or zero if it failed (due to a SQL error or a badly-formatted query).
ExamineDatabaseDrivers Result = ExamineDatabaseDrivers() Examines the database drivers available on the system. If ODBC isn't installed or no drivers are available, it returns 0, otherwise NextDatabaseDriver can be used to list all the drivers.
FinishDatabaseQuery FinishDatabaseQuery(#Database) Finish the current database SQL query and release its associated resources. Query related functions like FirstDatabaseRow or NextDatabaseRow can't be used anymore. None
FirstDatabaseRow Result = FirstDatabaseRow(#Database) Retrieves information about the first #Database row. The flag #PB_Database_DynamicCursor has to be specified to DatabaseQuery to have this command working. If Result is zero, then no row is available
GetDatabaseBlob Result = GetDatabaseBlob(#Database, Column, *Buffer, BufferLength) Returns the content of the specified database column in the specified buffer as a pointer to the blob memory. This command is only valid after a successful FirstDatabaseRow, PreviousDatabaseRow or NextDatabaseRow. If 'Result' is 0, then the blob can't be retrieved or its content is empty.
GetDatabaseDouble Result.d = GetDatabaseDouble(#Database, Column) Returns the content of the specified database column as a double precision floating-point number. This command is only valid after a successful FirstDatabaseRow, PreviousDatabaseRow or NextDatabaseRow. Returns a double precision floating-point value.
GetDatabaseFloat Result.f = GetDatabaseFloat(#Database, Column) Returns the content of the specified database column as a floating-point number. This command is only valid after a successful FirstDatabaseRow, PreviousDatabaseRow or NextDatabaseRow. Returns a single precision floating-point value.
GetDatabaseLong Result = GetDatabaseLong(#Database, Column) Returns the content of the specified #Database column as an integer number. This command is only valid after a successful FirstDatabaseRow, PreviousDatabaseRow or NextDatabaseRow. Returns the content of the column as an integer value.
GetDatabaseQuad Result.q = GetDatabaseQuad(#Database, Column) Returns the content of the specified #Database column as a quad number. This command is only valid after a successful FirstDatabaseRow, PreviousDatabaseRow or NextDatabaseRow. Returns the content of the column as a quad value.
GetDatabaseString Text$ = GetDatabaseString(#Database, Column) Returns the content of the specified #Database column as a string. This command is only valid after a successful FirstDatabaseRow, PreviousDatabaseRow or NextDatabaseRow. Returns the content of the column as a string.
IsDatabase Result = IsDatabase(#Database) This function evaluates if the given #Database number is a valid and correctly-initialized database. Returns nonzero if #Database is a valid database connection and zero otherwise.
NextDatabaseDriver Result = NextDatabaseDriver() Retrieves information about the next available database driver. This function must be called after ExamineDatabaseDrivers. To get information about the current driver, DatabaseDriverName and DatabaseDriverDescription can be used. If Result is 0, no more drivers are available.
NextDatabaseRow Result = NextDatabaseRow(#Database) Retrieves information about the next database row in the #Database. To access fields within a row, GetDatabaseLong, GetDatabaseFloat, GetDatabaseString can be used. If Result is 0, then no more rows are available (i.e. reached the end of the table).
OpenDatabase Result = OpenDatabase(#Database, DatabaseName$, User$, Password$ [, Plugin]) Opens a new database connection. Returns nonzero if the database connection was established successfully and zero if not. Error information can be received with the DatabaseError command. If #PB_Any was used for the #Database parameter, then the generated number is returned.
OpenDatabaseRequester Result = OpenDatabaseRequester(#Database [, Plugin]) Open the standard ODBC requester to choose which database to open. Returns nonzero if the database connection was established successfully and zero if not. Error information can be received with the DatabaseError command. If #PB_Any was used for the #Database parameter, then the generated number is returned.
PreviousDatabaseRow Result = PreviousDatabaseRow(#Database) Retrieves information about the previous database row in the #Database. The flag #PB_Database_DynamicCursor has to be specified to DatabaseQuery to have this command working. To access to fields inside a row, GetDatabaseLong, GetDatabaseFloat, GetDatabaseString can be used. If Result is 0, then no more rows are available (i.e. reached the start of the table).
SetDatabaseBlob SetDatabaseBlob(#Database, StatementIndex, *Buffer, BufferLength) Set the blob for future use with DatabaseUpdate. None
SetDatabaseDouble SetDatabaseDouble(#Database, StatementIndex, Value.d) Set a double value as a bind variable for the next call to DatabaseQuery or DatabaseUpdate. None
SetDatabaseFloat SetDatabaseFloat(#Database, StatementIndex, Value.f) Set a float as a bind variable for the next call to DatabaseQuery or DatabaseUpdate. None
SetDatabaseLong SetDatabaseLong(#Database, StatementIndex, Value) Set a long value as a bind variable for the next call to DatabaseQuery or DatabaseUpdate. None
SetDatabaseNull SetDatabaseNull(#Database, StatementIndex) Set a bind variable to a NULL value for the next call to DatabaseQuery or DatabaseUpdate. None
SetDatabaseQuad SetDatabaseQuad(#Database, StatementIndex, Value.q) Set a quad value as a bind variable for the next call to DatabaseQuery or DatabaseUpdate. None
SetDatabaseString SetDatabaseString(#Database, StatementIndex, Value$) Set a string as a bind variable for the next call to DatabaseQuery or DatabaseUpdate. None
UseMySQLDatabase Result = UseMySQLDatabase([LibraryName$]) Initialize the MySQL and MariaDB database environment for future use. Returns #True if the MySQL environment is successfully initialized, otherwise returns #False.
UseODBCDatabase Result = UseODBCDatabase() Initialize the ODBC database environment for future use. It attempts to load the ODBC driver and allocate the required resources. If Result is 0, then the ODBC driver is not available or is too old (ODBC 3.0 or higher is needed) and the Database functions should not be used.
UsePostgreSQLDatabase Result = UsePostgreSQLDatabase([LibraryName$]) Initialize the PostgreSQL database environment for future use. When using the optional 'LibraryName$' parameter, it will return #True if the dynamic library has been correctly loaded or #False otherwise. If the optional 'LibraryName$' parameter is not specified, it will always returns #True.
UseSQLiteDatabase Result = UseSQLiteDatabase([LibraryName$]) Initialize the SQLite database environment for future use. When using the optional 'LibraryName$' parameter, it will return #True if the dynamic library has been correctly loaded or #False otherwise. If the optional 'LibraryName$' parameter is not specified, it will always returns #True.
Date (14)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
AddDate Date.q = AddDate(Date.q, Type, Value) Add an amount of time to a date. Returns the new date, -1 otherwise.
ConvertDate Date.q = ConvertDate(Date.q, Format) Converts a date between local time and UTC time. Returns converted date, or -1 if the conversion failed.
Date Date.q = Date([Year, Month, Day, Hour, Minute, Second]) Returns the date value created from the given parameters, or the local system time if no parameters are specified. Returns the specified date value. If the given parameters are not valid (or outside the supported date range) then -1 will be returned.
DateUTC Date.q = DateUTC() Returns the system date as UTC time. Returns the system date as UTC time.
Day Result = Day(Date.q) Returns the day component of the specified date. Returns the day component, -1 otherwise. The result is always between 1 and 31.
DayOfWeek Result = DayOfWeek(Date.q) Returns the weekday of the specified date. Returns a number between 0 and 6 representing the day of the week, -1 otherwise: 0 : Sunday 1 : Monday 2 : Tuesday 3 : Wednesday 4 : Thursday 5 : Friday 6 : Saturday
DayOfYear Result = DayOfYear(Date.q) Returns the number of days elapsed since the beginning of the year of the specified date. Returns the number of days since the beginning of the year, -1 otherwise. The result is always between 1 and 366.
FormatDate Text$ = FormatDate(Mask$, Date.q) Returns a string representation of the given Date. Returns the mask string with all tokens replaced by the date values if the date was valid, an empty string otherwise.
Hour Result = Hour(Date.q) Returns the hour value of the specified date. Returns the hour component of the date, -1 otherwise. The result is always between 0 and 23.
Minute Result = Minute(Date.q) Returns the minute value of the specified date. Returns the minute component of the date, -1 otherwise. The result is always between 0 and 59.
Month Result = Month(Date.q) Returns the month value of the specified date. Returns the month component of the date, -1 otherwise. The result is always between 1 and 12.
ParseDate Date.q = ParseDate(Mask$, String$) Transforms a string date into a regular date value which then can be used by other date functions. Returns the date representing the parsed string. If the input string did not match the mask then the result is -1.
Second Result = Second(Date.q) Returns the second value of the specified date. Returns the second component of the date, -1 otherwise. The result is always between 0 and 59.
Year Result = Year(Date.q) Returns the year value of the specified date. Returns the year component of the date, -1 otherwise.

NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
DesktopDepth Result = DesktopDepth(#Desktop) Returns the color depth of the specified desktop. Returns the depth in bits-per-pixel: 1, 2, 4, 8, 15, 16, 24 or 32-bit
DesktopFrequency Result = DesktopFrequency(#Desktop) Returns the frequency of the specified desktop. Returns the frequency of the specified desktop in Hertz. If the return-value is 0 then the default hardware frequency is being used, or the actual frequency could not be determined.
DesktopHeight Result = DesktopHeight(#Desktop) Returns the height of the specified desktop. Returns the height in pixels.
DesktopMouseX Result = DesktopMouseX() Returns the absolute x position of the mouse on the desktop. Returns the x coordinate (in pixel) of the mouse relative to the top left corner of the primary monitor. The coordinate is negative if the mouse is on a monitor to the left of the primary monitor.
DesktopMouseY Result = DesktopMouseY() Returns the absolute y position of the mouse on the desktop. Returns the y coordinate (in pixel) of the mouse relative to the top left corner of the primary monitor. The coordinate is negative if the mouse is on a monitor above the primary monitor.
DesktopName Result$ = DesktopName(#Desktop) Returns the name (if any) for the specified desktop. Returns a string with the desktop name. If there is no name then an empty string is returned.
DesktopResolutionX Result.d = DesktopResolutionX() Returns the desktop DPI resolution factor on the 'x' axis. Returns the desktop DPI resolution factor on the 'x' axis. If the value is '1', then no DPI factor has been applied to the display on the 'x' axis. If the value is '1.25', a 125% factor has been applied to the display on the 'x' axis.
DesktopResolutionY Result.d = DesktopResolutionY() Returns the desktop DPI resolution factor on the 'y' axis. Returns the desktop DPI resolution factor on the 'y' axis. If the value is '1', then no DPI factor has been applied to the display on the 'y' axis. If the value is '1.25', a 125% factor has been applied to the display on the 'y' axis.
DesktopScaledX Result = DesktopScaledX(Value) Returns the scaled value according to current display DPI on 'x' axis. This is mostly useful to calculate real pixel position independently of the display DPI. Returns the scaled value according to current display DPI on 'x' axis. For example, on a display with a 125% DPI applied, a value of 100 will result to 125.
DesktopScaledY Result = DesktopScaledY(Value) Returns the scaled value according to current display DPI on 'y' axis. This is mostly useful to calculate real pixel position independently of the display DPI. Returns the scaled value according to current display DPI on 'y' axis.
