For example, on a display with a 125% DPI applied, a value of 100 will result to 125.
DesktopUnscaledX Result = DesktopUnscaledX(Value) Returns the unscaled value according to current display DPI on 'x' axis. This is mostly useful to calculate real pixel position independently of the display DPI. Returns the unscaled value according to current display DPI on 'x' axis. For example, on a display with a 125% DPI applied, a value of 125 will result to 100.
DesktopUnscaledY Result = DesktopUnscaledY(Value) Returns the unscaled value according to current display DPI on 'y' axis. This is mostly useful to calculate real pixel position independently of the display DPI. Returns the unscaled value according to current display DPI on 'y' axis. For example, on a display with a 125% DPI applied, a value of 125 will result to 100.
DesktopWidth Result = DesktopWidth(#Desktop) Returns the width for the specified desktop. Returns the width in pixels.
DesktopX Result = DesktopX(#Desktop) Returns the x coordinate of the specified desktop. Returns the x coordinate (in pixel) of the top left corner of the desktop. The coordinate is relative to the top left corner of the primary monitor. It is negative if the specified monitor is to the left of the primary monitor.
DesktopY Result = DesktopY(#Desktop) Returns the y coordinate of the specified desktop. Returns the y coordinate (in pixel) of the top left corner of the desktop. The coordinate is relative to the top left corner of the primary monitor. It is negative if the specified monitor is above the primary monitor.
ExamineDesktops Result = ExamineDesktops() Retrieves information about all the desktops connected to the local computer. This function must be called before using the functions of this library the following functions: DesktopDepth, DesktopFrequency, DesktopHeight, DesktopName and DesktopWidth. The number of desktops on success, zero otherwise.
Dialog (14)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
CreateDialog Result = CreateDialog(#Dialog) Create a new uninitialized dialog. To initialize the dialog, use OpenXMLDialog (to open it as its own window) or XmlDialogGadget (to create it as a gadget embedded in an existing window). Returns nonzero if the dialog was created successfully and zero if not. If #PB_Any was used as the #Dialog parameter, then the auto-generated number is returned in case of success.
DialogError Result$ = DialogError(#Dialog) Returns the last error message (in english) to get more information about dialog creation failure after OpenXMLDialog or XmlDialogGadget. Returns the error message. If no additional information is available, then the error message can be empty.
DialogGadget Result = DialogGadget(#Dialog, Name$) Returns the gadget number of the specified gadget name. Returns the gadget number of the specified gadget name, or -1 if the gadget isn't found in the dialog. For a dialog created with XmlDialogGadget, the root gadget itself can also be retrieved this way, by giving the root <window> element a 'name' attribute in the XML.
DialogID Result = DialogID(#Dialog) Returns the unique ID which identifies the dialog in the operating system. Returns the unique ID which identifies the dialog in the operating system.
DialogWindow Result = DialogWindow(#Dialog) Returns the window number of the dialog. It allows to use any window related commands with the dialog. The dialog has to be initialized successfully with OpenXMLDialog before using this command. Returns the window number of the specified dialog, or -1 if the dialog was created with XmlDialogGadget instead of OpenXMLDialog, as it has no window of its own in that case.
FreeDialog FreeDialog(#Dialog) Free the specified dialog and release its associated memory. If the dialog window was still opened, it will be automatically closed. For a dialog created with XmlDialogGadget, its gadget is freed instead (the window hosting it is left untouched). None
IsDialog Result = IsDialog(#Dialog) Tests if the given dialog number is a valid dialog. Returns nonzero if #Dialog is a valid dialog and zero if not.
OpenXMLDialog Result = OpenXMLDialog(#Dialog, #XML, Name$ [, x, y [, Width, Height [, ParentID]]]) Open the specified dialog and display it on the screen. To access the dialog gadgets use DialogGadget. To get the window number of this dialog use DialogWindow. UseDialogScintillaGadget, UseDialogOpenGLGadget, UseDialogWebGadget and UseDialogWebViewGadget can be used to enable support for these gadgets in the dialog lib. They are not enabled by default to reduce the dialog library size footprint. Returns nonzero if the dialog has been successfully opened, returns zero otherwise. To get more information about the error which has occurred, use DialogError.
RefreshDialog RefreshDialog(#Dialog) Refresh the dialog size to adjust it to any change. For example, when changing the text content of gadgets, the dialog size will may be need adjustments. For a dialog created with XmlDialogGadget, this relayouts its children within the gadget's current size instead (its own size is left untouched, as it is controlled by the caller). None
UseDialogOpenGLGadget UseDialogOpenGLGadget() Enable OpenGLGadget support in the dialog library. This is not enabled by default to reduce the dialog library size footprint if OpenGLGadget is not needed. None
UseDialogScintillaGadget UseDialogScintillaGadget() Enable ScintillaGadget support in the dialog library. This is not enabled by default to reduce the dialog library size footprint if ScintillaGadget is not needed. None
UseDialogWebGadget UseDialogWebGadget() Enable WebGadget support in the dialog library. This is not enabled by default to reduce the dialog library size footprint if WebGadget is not needed. None
UseDialogWebViewGadget UseDialogWebViewGadget() Enable WebViewGadget support in the dialog library. This is not enabled by default to reduce the dialog library size footprint if WebViewGadget is not needed. None
XmlDialogGadget Result = XmlDialogGadget(#Dialog, #XML, Name$ [, x, y [, Width, Height]]) Creates the specified dialog as a gadget (a ContainerGadget), instead of opening it as its own window like OpenXMLDialog does. This allows a dialog defined in XML to be embedded inside an existing window, next to other gadgets. It uses exactly the same XML format as OpenXMLDialog (see its documentation for the full XML reference) - the very same XML document can be used with either command: the root <window> element becomes the created ContainerGadget, and any window-only attribute or flag it may still carry (title, screencentered, systemmenu, ...) is simply ignored. The gadget is created inside the currently active window, exactly like ContainerGadget itself, so XmlDialogGadget has to be called after opening (or after selecting, with UseGadgetList) the window that should host it. To access the dialog gadgets, including the root gadget itself, use DialogGadget (give the root <window> element a 'name' attribute in the XML to retrieve it). Unlike a dialog opened with OpenXMLDialog, DialogWindow returns -1 for a dialog created with XmlDialogGadget, as it has no window of its own. UseDialogScintillaGadget, UseDialogOpenGLGadget, UseDialogWebGadget and UseDialogWebViewGadget can be used to enable support for these gadgets in the dialog lib. They are not enabled by default to reduce the dialog library size footprint. Returns nonzero if the dialog gadget has been successfully created, returns zero otherwise. To get more information about the error which has occurred, use DialogError.
DragDrop (22)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
DragFiles Result = DragFiles(Files$ [, Actions]) Starts a Drag & Drop operation with a list of filenames. Returns one of the above Drag & Drop action values to indicate what action the user took, or #PB_Drag_None if the user aborted the Drag & Drop operation. Note that unlike with the other functions that start Drag & Drop, nothing should be done when #PB_Drag_Move is returned. As the dragged data is only the filename and not the file itself, any action that is taken on the file must be done by the drag target.
DraggedItemIndex Result = DraggedItemIndex() Return the current dragged item index. This function has to be called after NextDraggedItem. Returns the index of the current dragged item (first index is zero).
DragImage Result = DragImage(ImageID [, Actions]) Starts a Drag & Drop operation with image data. Returns one of the above Drag & Drop action values to indicate what action the user took, or #PB_Drag_None if the user aborted the Drag & Drop operation. Note that if #PB_Drag_Move is returned, it is your responsibility to remove the dragged image from your application.
DragOSFormats Result = DragOSFormats(Formats(), Count [, Actions]) Starts a Drag & Drop operation with a list of custom data formats. The types of formats available and the way in which they are represented depends on the Operating system. This function offers the possibility to work with formats not natively supported by PureBasic, while still using the simple mechanisms provided by this library to carry out the Drag & Drop operation. Returns one of the above Drag & Drop action values to indicate what action the user took, or #PB_Drag_None if the user aborted the Drag & Drop operation. Note that if #PB_Drag_Move is returned, it is your responsibility to remove the dragged data from your application.
DragPrivate Result = DragPrivate(Type [, Actions]) Starts a "private" Drag & Drop operation. Unlike the other functions that start Drag & Drop, this data can only be dropped inside the application (Data dragged with functions like DragText or DragImage can be accepted by other applications as well). This function should be used to add Drag & Drop functionality between Gadgets or Windows with data that would not be understood by other applications. Returns one of the above Drag & Drop action values to indicate what action the user took, or #PB_Drag_None if the user aborted the Drag & Drop operation.
DragText Result = DragText(Text$ [, Actions]) Starts a Drag & Drop operation with text data. Returns one of the above Drag & Drop action values to indicate what action the user took, or #PB_Drag_None if the user aborted the Drag & Drop operation. Note that if #PB_Drag_Move is returned, it is your responsibility to remove the dragged text data from your application.
EnableGadgetDrop EnableGadgetDrop(#Gadget, Format, Actions [, PrivateType]) Enables a gadget to be a target for Drag & Drop operations of a specific format. When the user drags data of this format over the gadget, the cursor will indicate that the data can be dropped there. None
EnableWindowDrop EnableWindowDrop(#Window, Format, Actions [, PrivateType]) Enables a window to be a target for Drag & Drop operations of a specific format. Only the area not covered by any gadgets will be the target area. When the user drags data of this format over the window, the cursor will indicate that the data can be dropped there. None
EventDropAction Result = EventDropAction() After a #PB_Event_GadgetDrop or #PB_Event_WindowDrop is received by WaitWindowEvent or WindowEvent, this function returns the action that should be taken with the data. Returns one of the following values: #PB_Drag_Copy: The data should be copied #PB_Drag_Move: The data should be moved (The drag source is responsible for removing the original data) #PB_Drag_Link: The data should be linked
EventDropBuffer *Result = EventDropBuffer() After a #PB_Event_GadgetDrop or #PB_Event_WindowDrop is received by WaitWindowEvent or WindowEvent with an OS specific format, this function can be used to access the data. Returns the memory address where the dropped data is located. The EventDropSize command returns the size of this buffer.
EventDropFiles Result$ = EventDropFiles() After a #PB_Event_GadgetDrop or #PB_Event_WindowDrop is received by WaitWindowEvent or WindowEvent with a format (can be get with EventDropType) of #PB_Drop_Files, this function returns the dropped filenames. Returns a list of filenames or directories, all with full path. The individual names are separated by a Chr(10) (linefeed) character.
EventDropImage Result = EventDropImage(#Image [, Depth]) After a #PB_Event_GadgetDrop or #PB_Event_WindowDrop is received by WaitWindowEvent or WindowEvent with a format (can be get with EventDropType) of #PB_Drop_Image, this function can be used to retrieve the dropped image. Returns nonzero if the image was successfully created and zero if not. If #PB_Any was used for the #Image parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
EventDropPrivate Result = EventDropPrivate() After a #PB_Event_GadgetDrop or #PB_Event_WindowDrop is received by WaitWindowEvent or WindowEvent with a format (can be get with EventDropType) of #PB_Drop_Private, this function returns the 'PrivateType' that was dropped. Returns the private type value used when starting the Drag & Drop operation. (See DragPrivate for more information.)
EventDropSize Result = EventDropSize() After a #PB_Event_GadgetDrop or #PB_Event_WindowDrop is received by WaitWindowEvent or WindowEvent with an OS specific format, this function returns the size of the dropped data. Returns the size in bytes of the memory buffer returned by EventDropBuffer.
EventDropText Result$ = EventDropText() After a #PB_Event_GadgetDrop or #PB_Event_WindowDrop is received by WaitWindowEvent or WindowEvent with a format (can be get with EventDropType) of #PB_Drop_Text, this function returns the text that was dropped. Returns the dropped text.
EventDropType Result = EventDropType() After a #PB_Event_GadgetDrop or #PB_Event_WindowDrop is received by WaitWindowEvent or WindowEvent, this function returns the format of the dropped data. Returns one of the following values, or an OS specific ID for a custom format (see DragOSFormats for more information) #PB_Drop_Text : Text was dropped. (use EventDropText to retrieve it) #PB_Drop_Image : An image was dropped. (use EventDropImage to retrieve it) #PB_Drop_Files : Filenames were dropped. (use EventDropFiles to retrieve them) #PB_Drop_Private: A "private" operation finished. (use EventDropPrivate to know its type)
EventDropX Result = EventDropX() After a #PB_Event_GadgetDrop or #PB_Event_WindowDrop is received by WaitWindowEvent or WindowEvent, this function returns the X position at which the data was dropped. Returns the x coordinate of the drop location relative to the gadget or window in which the data was dropped.
EventDropY Result = EventDropY() After a #PB_Event_GadgetDrop or #PB_Event_WindowDrop is received by WaitWindowEvent or WindowEvent, this function returns the Y position at which the data was dropped. Returns the y coordinate of the drop location relative to the gadget or window in which the data was dropped.
ExamineDraggedItems ExamineDraggedItems() Start to examine the dragged items with the functions NextDraggedItem and DraggedItemIndex. It has to be used after a #PB_Event_DragStart. This function is supported for the following gadgets: ExplorerListGadget, ExplorerTreeGadget, ListIconGadget, ListViewGadget and TreeGadget. None
NextDraggedItem Result = NextDraggedItem() This function must be called after ExamineDraggedItems. It will iterate over dragged items. Returns nonzero if another dragged item is available or zero if there are no more dragged item.
SetDragCallback SetDragCallback(@DragCallback()) A callback function to be called during a Drag & Drop operation initiated from this application. The callback allows to modify the Drag & Drop process provided by PureBasic, for example by providing a custom cursor through the API of the Operating system. None
SetDropCallback SetDropCallback(@DropCallback()) A callback function to be called when data is dragged over a gadget or window that allows data to be dropped (see EnableGadgetDrop / EnableWindowDrop). The callback allows to modify the Drag & Drop process provided by PureBasic, for example by providing extra visual notification on the target gadget or window. None
Engine3D (53)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
Add3DArchive Add3DArchive(Path$, Type) Add a new absolute or relative path to the current 3D path list. All the 3D functions which need to load data (e.g. texture, mesh, sky, world) will use this path. It needs to be put after OpenScreen or OpenWindowedScreen. You may wonder why there is a special way to handle the files for 3D functions? Because it makes the data access more flexible and now, you can access the data using the standard filesystem or directly via the archive file like a .zip file. It's a very cool feature because you can pack all your data in one big compressed file, and then access the assets as if these were contained a standard directory. None
AmbientColor AmbientColor(Color) Changes the ambient color of the world. None
AntialiasingMode AntialiasingMode(Mode) Changes the fullscreen antialiasing mode. This function has to be called before OpenScreen to have any effect. None
BodyPick Result = BodyPick(#Camera, Picked, x, y, Locked) Simulates a mouse click and starts the manipulate the entity at the specified coordinate. The #Entity picked, or -1 if no entity are found at these coordinates.
ConvertLocalToWorldPosition ConvertLocalToWorldPosition(ObjectID, x, y, z) Converts the local x,y,z coordinates into world coordinates. GetX, GetY and GetZ will be used to get the converted coordinates. None
ConvertWorldToLocalPosition ConvertWorldToLocalPosition(ObjectID, x, y, z) Converts the world x,y,z coordinates into local coordinates. GetX, GetY and GetZ will be used to get the converted coordinates. None
CreateWater CreateWater(WaveTextureID, FoamTextureID, WaterColor, SkyColor, Distance.f, WaveBig.f, WaveLittle.f, Swell.f, Foam.f) Creates a world wide water plane. None
EnableWorldCollisions EnableWorldCollisions(State) Enable or disable the collisions in the world. None
EnableWorldPhysics EnableWorldPhysics(State) Enable or disable the physics engine in the world. None
Engine3DStatus Result = Engine3DStatus(Type) Gets the 3D engine current status. The value depending of the specified 'Type'.
ExamineWorldCollisions Result = ExamineWorldCollisions(Contacts) Examine the collisions which have occurred in the world since the last call. Collisions have to be enabled with EnableWorldCollisions before using this command. To step through the collisions, use NextWorldCollision. Returns nonzero if the collisions can be examined, returns zero otherwise.
FetchOrientation FetchOrientation(ObjectID [, Mode]) Get the orientation of the specified object. GetX, GetY, GetZ and GetW will be used to get orientation values. None
FirstWorldCollisionEntity Result = FirstWorldCollisionEntity() Returns the #Entity number of the first object in the collision being examined with ExamineWorldCollisions. Returns the #Entity number of the first object in the current collision.
Fog Fog(Color, Intensity, StartDistance, EndDistance) Creates a fog at the specified distance of the camera. The fog effect is applied to all cameras. The fog is also applied automatically to the SkyBox and SkyDome commands if called before them. None
GetW Result = GetW() Returns the w value of the last called command. The only supported command is FetchOrientation. Returns the w value of the last called command.
GetWorldAttribute Result.f = GetWorldAttribute(Attribute) Get the specified attribute of the world. Returns the value of the specified attribute.
GetX Result = GetX() Returns the x value of the last called command. Supported commands are FetchOrientation, ConvertLocalToWorldPosition and ConvertWorldToLocalPosition. Returns the x value of the last called command.
GetY Result = GetY() Returns the y value of the last called command. Supported commands are FetchOrientation, ConvertLocalToWorldPosition and ConvertWorldToLocalPosition. Returns the y value of the last called command.
GetZ Result = GetZ() Returns the z value of the last called command. Supported commands are FetchOrientation, ConvertLocalToWorldPosition and ConvertWorldToLocalPosition. Returns the z value of the last called command.
InitEngine3D Result = InitEngine3D([Flags [, LibraryName$]) Initializes the 3D environment for later use. You must put this function at the top of your source code if you want to use any of the 3D functions. Returns non-zero if the library has been successfully loaded, zero otherwise. If initialization fails, the program should quit or all 3D function calls should be disabled.
LoadWorld Result = LoadWorld(Filename$) This function loads an entire world. Currently, the Quake3 BSP format is the only one supported but more formats will follow. The Filename$ must be accessible in the 3D path, so the Add3DArchive function should be used before calling this function. A world can be easily created using third party tools like 'Quark'. A world can contain a sky, building, lights and more. Actually, all Quake 3 maps can be loaded out of the box with full detail. If the 'Result' is 0, the world could not be loaded. The BSP format is owned by iD Software and can only be used in freeware programs. Commercial software must acquire a license from iD to use this format. The license scheme is beyond PureBasic and Fantaisie Software can't be responsible for the incorrect use of this function.
MousePick Result = MousePick(#Camera, x, y [, PickMask]) Simulates a mouse click and returns which object is under the specified 2D point on the specified camera. The returned value can be: -1 : Nothing has been detected #PB_World_WaterPick: the click occurred on the water. 0 and above: the click occurred on the #Entity. The entity pick is based on its bounding box, not on its mesh. To get more information about the picked object position, use PickX, PickY and PickZ.
MouseRayCast Result = MouseRayCast(#Camera, x, y, PickMask) Casts a ray from the 2D point through the scene, and checks if an object is crossing the ray. This function doesn't rely on the physic engine. The normals value at the impact point are available with NormalX, NormalY and NormalZ. Returns the number of the object in contact with the ray, -1 otherwise.
NextWorldCollision Result = NextWorldCollision() Go to the next collision. ExamineWorldCollisions needs to be called successfully before using this command. To get more information about the current collision, use FirstWorldCollisionEntity, SecondWorldCollisionEntity, WorldCollisionContact, WorldCollisionNormal and WorldCollisionAppliedImpulse. Returns nonzero if there is another collision to be examined, or zero if there is no more collisions.
NormalX Result.f = NormalX() Returns the 'x' normal value at the crossed point, after RayCast, RayCollide or MouseRayCast. Returns the 'x' normal value at the crossed point.
NormalY Result.f = NormalY() Returns the 'y' normal value at the crossed point, after RayCast, RayCollide or MouseRayCast. Returns the 'y' normal value at the crossed point.
NormalZ Result.f = NormalZ() Returns the 'z' normal value at the crossed point, after RayCast, RayCollide or MouseRayCast. Returns the 'z' normal value at the crossed point.
Parse3DScripts Parse3DScripts() Parses all the .materials OGRE scripts found in the paths set with Add3DArchive. This allows the use of meshes with complex materials scripts directly in PureBasic. When creating the entity the constant #PB_Material_None has to be specified, so all the material information will be taken from the script, if it was correctly loaded. None
PickX Result.f = PickX() After MousePick or RayPick, it returns the 'x' position of the picked object in world coordinates. After PointPick, it returns the 'x' direction of the picked point, between -1 and 1.
PickY Result.f = PickY() After MousePick or RayPick, it returns the 'y' position of the picked object in world coordinates. After PointPick, it returns the 'y' direction of the picked point, between -1 and 1.
PickZ Result.f = PickZ() After MousePick or RayPick, it returns the 'z' position of the picked object in world coordinates. After PointPick, it returns the 'z' direction of the picked point, between -1 and 1.
Pitch Pitch(ObjectID, Value.f, Mode) Pitch the specified object. None
PointPick Result = PointPick(#Camera, x, y) Allows to get the direction the specified 2D point on the specified camera. Returns non-zero if the pick was successful. To get the point direction, use PickX, PickY and PickZ.
RayCast Result = RayCast(x, y, z, DestinationX, DestinationY, DestinationZ, PickMask) Casts a ray between the first point and the second point, and checks if an object is crossing the ray. This function doesn't rely on the physic engine. The normals value at the impact point are available with NormalX, NormalY and NormalZ. Returns -1 if the ray has collided with any object.
RayCollide Result = RayCollide(x, y, z, DestinationX, DestinationY, DestinationZ [, CollisionGroup , CollisionMask]]) Casts a ray between the first point and the second point, and checks if an entity is colliding the ray. This function relies on the physic engine, which needs to be activated with EnableWorldPhysics before using this command. Only entities with bodies will react to the ray. To get the position about the collide point, use PickX, PickY and PickZ. The normals values at the collide point are available with NormalX, NormalY and NormalZ. Returns the entity number if the ray has collided with one, or -1 if no collision has occurred.
RayPick Result = RayPick(x, y, z, DestinationX, DestinationY, DestinationZ [, PickMask]) Casts a ray between the first point and the second point, and checks if an object is crossing the ray. The returned value can be: -1 : Nothing has been crossed. #PB_World_WaterPick: the ray crossed the water. 0 and above: the ray crossed an #Entity. The entity detection is based on its bounding box, not on its mesh. To get more information about the picked object position, use PickX, PickY and PickZ.
RenderWorld Result = RenderWorld([ElapsedPhysicTime]) Renders the whole world on the screen. This function should be called once all 3D operations are finished and only one time per frame. Returns the elapsed time since the last frame in milliseconds. It can be useful to have an accurate time based simulation if the frame render time isn't stable.
Roll Roll(ObjectID, Value.f, Mode) Roll the specified object. None
SecondWorldCollisionEntity Result = SecondWorldCollisionEntity() Returns the #Entity number of the second object in the collision being examined with ExamineWorldCollisions(). Returns the #Entity number of the second object in the current collision.
SetGUITheme3D SetGUITheme3D(ThemeName$, FontName$) As CEGUI support skinning, this command allow to select which theme and which font to use for the GUI. This command has to be called before any other GUI commands to have an effect. None
SetOrientation SetOrientation(ObjectID, x, y, z, w) Set the orientation of the specified object. None
SetRenderQueue SetRenderQueue(ObjectID, Queue [, Priority]) Change the render order of the specified object. None
SetWorldAttribute SetWorldAttribute(Attribute, Value.f) Set the specified attribute of the world. Change the value of the specified attribute.
ShowGUI ShowGUI(Transparency, ShowMouse [, #Camera, Enable]) Shows or hides the whole GUI elements, which are composed of 3d windows and 3d gadgets. None
SkyBox Result = SkyBox(TextureName$ [, FogColor, FogIntensity, FogStartDistance, FogEndDistance]) Loads a 6 face cube and creates an artificial box which is far away from the camera but close to the world. This is a very useful function to easily make a closed world. Returns non-zero if the SkyBox has been successfully created. If the textures can't be loaded, the skybox is created with blank textures.
SkyDome Result = SkyDome(TextureID, SkyColor, RiseColor [, NbCloudLayers, Height.f, SpeedX.f, SpeedZ.f]) Creates a new SkyDome which is a curved moving sky displayed using the specified cloud texture. Returns non-zero if the SkyDome has been successfully created.
WorldCollisionAppliedImpulse Result.f = WorldCollisionAppliedImpulse() Returns the applied impulse about the collision being examined with ExamineWorldCollisions. ExamineWorldCollisions 'Contacts' parameter has to be set to #True to have this command working. The applied impulse about the collision being examined with ExamineWorldCollisions.
WorldCollisionContact WorldCollisionContact() Fetch contact information about the collision being examined with ExamineWorldCollisions(). ExamineWorldCollisions 'Contacts' parameter has to be set to #True to have this command working. The contact vector values can be retrieved with GetX, GetY and GetZ. None
WorldCollisionNormal WorldCollisionNormal() Fetch contact normal information about the collision being examined with ExamineWorldCollisions(). ExamineWorldCollisions 'Contacts' parameter has to be set to #True to have this command working. The contact normal vector values can be retrieved with GetX, GetY and GetZ. None
WorldDebug WorldDebug(Mode) Changes the world debug mode. This can be very useful to help finding issues with collisions or picking for example. None
WorldGravity WorldGravity(Gravity.f [, x, y, z]) Changes the gravity of the world when the physics engine is enabled with EnableWorldPhysics. None
WorldShadows WorldShadows(Type [, Distance.f [, Color [, TextureSize]]]) Sets how shadows will be rendered in the world. None
Yaw Yaw(ObjectID, Value.f, Mode) Yaw the specified object. None
Entity (58)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
AddSubEntity Result = AddSubEntity(#Entity, #SubEntity, Type, [OffsetX, OffsetY, OffsetZ [, SizeX, SizeY, SizeZ [, AxisX, AxisY, AxisZ]]]) Add a sub entity to an entity. Returns zero if the entity can't be created.
ApplyEntityForce ApplyEntityForce(#Entity, x, y, z [, PositionX, PositionY, PositionZ [, Mode [, PositionMode]]]) Apply the specified force to the entity. The new force value replace any previous force previously applied to the entity. None
ApplyEntityImpulse ApplyEntityImpulse(#Entity, x, y, z [, PositionX, PositionY, PositionZ [, Mode]]) Apply an impulse to the entity. The new impulse is added to the current force of the entity. None
ApplyEntityTorque ApplyEntityTorque(#Entity, x, y, z [, Mode]) Apply a rotation force to the entity. The new rotation force replace any previous force previously applied to the entity. None
ApplyEntityTorqueImpulse ApplyEntityTorqueImpulse(#Entity, x, y, z [, Mode]) Apply a rotation impulse to the entity. The new impulse is added to the rotation force previously applied to the entity. None
AttachEntityObject AttachEntityObject(#Entity, Bone$, ObjectID [, x, y, z, Pitch, Roll, Yaw]) Attach an existing object to an entity bone. An object can be detached from an entity with DetachEntityObject. None
CopyEntity Result = CopyEntity(#Entity, #NewEntity) Creates a #NewEntity which is the exact copy of the specified #Entity. If #PB_Any is used as '#NewEntity' parameter, the new entity number will be returned as 'Result'. If the 'Result' is 0, the entity copy has failed. If #NewEntity was already created, it will be automatically freed and replaced by the new one.
CreateEntity Result = CreateEntity(#Entity, MeshID, MaterialID, [x, y, z [, PickMask [, VisibilityMask]]) Creates a new #Entity using the specified Mesh and Material. Returns zero if the entity can't be created. If #PB_Any is used as '#Entity' parameter, the new entity number is returned.
CreateEntityBody CreateEntityBody(#Entity, Type [, Mass [, Restitution, Friction [, Axis [, SizeX, SizeY, SizeZ]]]]) Changes the type of the body associated with the #Entity. To have its collisions managed by the physic engine, an entity has to set a body. In fact, only the body is known by the physic engine, which will do all the calculation about the entity, check the mass, friction and if it collides will move back the real entity. To have any effect, the physic engine needs to be activated with the EnableWorldPhysics. None
DetachEntityObject DetachEntityObject(#Node, ObjectID) Detach a previously attached object from an #Entity bone. The supported objects are the following: - Entity : use EntityID as 'ObjectID'. - Camera : use CameraID as 'ObjectID'. - Light : use LightID as 'ObjectID'. - BillboardGroup : use BillboardGroupID as 'ObjectID'. - ParticleEmitter: use ParticleEmitterID as 'ObjectID'. An object can be attached to an entity bone with AttachEntityObject.
DisableEntityBody DisableEntityBody(#Entity, Disable) Disable an entity body. The physic engine doesn't affect the entity anymore when an entity body is disabled. None
EnableManualEntityBoneControl EnableManualEntityBoneControl(#Entity, Bone$, State, InheritOrientation) Enable the manual control of a bone. It can be manually moved with MoveEntityBone, rotated with RotateEntityBone or scaled with ScaleEntityBone. None
EntityAngularFactor EntityAngularFactor(#Entity, x, y, z) Changes the angular factor of the #Entity. None
EntityBonePitch Result = EntityBonePitch(#Entity, Bone$) Returns the pitch of the entity bone. The current pitch value of the bone. This value is always between -180.0 and 180.0 degrees.
EntityBoneRoll Result = EntityBoneRoll(#Entity, Bone$) Returns the roll of the entity bone. The current roll value of the bone. This value is always between -180.0 and 180.0 degrees.
EntityBoneX Result = EntityBoneX(#Entity, Bone$ [, OffsetX, OffsetY, OffsetZ]) Returns the 'x' position of the bone in the world. Returns the 'x' position of the #Entity bone in the world.
EntityBoneY Result = EntityBoneY(#Entity, Bone$ [, OffsetX, OffsetY, OffsetZ]) Returns the 'y' position of the bone in the world. Returns the 'y' position of the #Entity bone in the world.
EntityBoneYaw Result = EntityBoneYaw(#Entity, Bone$) Returns the yaw of the entity bone. The current yaw value of the bone. This value is always between -180.0 and 180.0 degrees.
EntityBoneZ Result = EntityBoneZ(#Entity, Bone$ [, OffsetX, OffsetY, OffsetZ]) Returns the 'z' position of the bone in the world. Returns the 'z' position of the #Entity bone in the world.
EntityBoundingBox Result = EntityBoundingBox(#Entity, Flags) Returns the position of the bounding box, either in local or world coordinate. Returns the position of the bounding box, either in local or world coordinate.
EntityCollide Result = EntityCollide(#Entity, #Entity2) Checks if the two specified entities are colliding. To have its collisions managed by the physic engine, an entity needs a body created with CreateEntityBody. To have any effect, the physic engine needs to be activated with the EnableWorldPhysics. Return non-zero if the two entities are colliding.
EntityCustomParameter EntityCustomParameter(#Entity, SubEntity, ParameterIndex, Value1.f, Value2.f, Value3.f, Value4.f) Set a custom parameter value to the #Entity material shader script. To have any effect, the material associated to the entity should have a shader script (either GLSL or HLSL). None
EntityDirection EntityDirection(#Entity, x, y, z [, Mode, LocalDirectionVector]) Set the direction for the entity. None
EntityDirectionX Result = EntityDirectionX(#Entity) Get the 'x' direction of the entity. Returns the 'x' direction of the entity.
EntityDirectionY Result = EntityDirectionY(#Entity) Get the 'y' direction of the entity. Returns the 'y' direction of the entity.
EntityDirectionZ Result = EntityDirectionZ(#Entity) Get the 'z' direction of the entity. Returns the 'z' direction of the entity.
EntityFixedYawAxis EntityFixedYawAxis(#Entity, Enable [, VectorX, VectorY, VectorZ]) Change the fixed yaw axis of the entity. The default behaviour of a entity is to yaw around its own Y axis. None
EntityID EntityID = EntityID(#Entity) Returns the unique ID which identifies the given '#Entity' in the operating system. This function is very useful when another library needs a entity reference.
EntityLinearFactor EntityLinearFactor(#Entity, x, y, z) Changes the linear factor for the #Entity. When moved, the entity linear velocity is multiplied by the linear factor to get the final velocity. This is very useful to constraint an entity move on one or several axis. By default, the linear factor is 1 for all axis meaning no impact on the velocity. The entity needs a physic body to support linear velocity constraint. None
EntityLookAt EntityLookAt(#Entity, x, y, z [, DirectionX, DirectionY, DirectionZ]) The point (in world unit) that an entity is facing. The position of the entity is not changed. None
EntityParentNode Result = EntityParentNode(#Entity) Returns the parent NodeID. Returns the parent NodeID, if any. This can be either a real node, or a bone if the entity is attached to a bone. If the entity has no parent node, it will returns 0.
EntityPitch Result = EntityPitch(#Entity [, Mode]) Get the pitch of the #Entity. The current pitch value of the specified entity. This value is always between -180.0 and 180.0 degrees.
EntityRenderMode EntityRenderMode(#Entity, Mode) Changes the render mode of the specified entity. None
EntityRoll Result = EntityRoll(#Entity [, Mode]) Get the roll of the #Entity. The current roll value of the specified entity. This value is always between -180.0 and 180.0 degrees.
EntityVelocity EntityVelocity(#Entity, x, y, z) Changes the linear velocity of the #Entity. The linear factor is applied to the entity before any move. To get the final value, see EntityLinearFactor for more information. The entity needs a physic body to support linear velocity. To get the current entity velocity, use GetEntityAttribute. None
EntityX Result = EntityX(#Entity [, Mode]) Returns the current position of the entity in the world. Returns the 'x' position of the entity.
EntityY Result = EntityY(#Entity [, Mode]) Returns the current position of the entity in the world. Returns the 'y' position of the entity.
EntityYaw Result = EntityYaw(#Entity [, Mode]) Get the yaw of the #Entity. The current yaw value of the specified entity. This value is always between -180.0 and 180.0 degrees.
EntityZ Result = EntityZ(#Entity [, Mode]) Returns the current position of the entity in the world. Returns the 'z' position of the entity.
FetchEntityMaterial Result = FetchEntityMaterial(#Entity, #Material [, SubEntity]) Fetch the material associated to the specified #Entity with SetEntityMaterial. Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure.
FreeEntity FreeEntity(#Entity) Free the specified #Entity created with CreateEntity before. All its associated memory is released and this object can't be used anymore. None
FreeEntityBody FreeEntityBody(#Entity) Free the body associated with the entity. None
FreeEntityJoints FreeEntityJoints(#Entity) Free all joints associated with the entity. None
GetEntityAttribute Result.f = GetEntityAttribute(#Entity, Attribute) Get the specified attribute of the given entity. Returns the value of the specified attribute or 0 if the entity does not support the attribute.
GetEntityCollisionGroup Result = GetEntityCollisionGroup(#Entity) Get the current entity collision group, as set with SetEntityCollisionFilter. The current entity collision group.
GetEntityCollisionMask Result = GetEntityCollisionMask(#Entity) Get the current entity collision mask, as set with SetEntityCollisionFilter. The current entity collision mask.
GetEntityMesh Result = GetEntityMesh(#Entity) Returns the #Mesh used by the entity. Returns the #Mesh used by the entity.
HideEntity HideEntity(#Entity, State) Hides or shows the specified #Entity. 'State' can take the following values: 1: the #Entity is hidden 0: the #Entity is shown
IsEntity Result = IsEntity(#Entity) Tests if the given #Entity is a valid and correctly initialized entity. This function is bulletproof and can be used with any value. If the 'Result' is not zero then the object is valid and initialized, else it returns zero. This is the correct way to ensure an entity is ready to use.
MoveEntity MoveEntity(#Entity, x, y, z [, Mode]) Move the specified entity. None
MoveEntityBone MoveEntityBone(#Entity, Bone$, x, y, z, Mode) Move the specified entity bone. The bone has to be in manual mode, set with EnableManualEntityBoneControl. None
RotateEntity RotateEntity(#Entity, x, y, z [, Mode]) Rotates the entity according to the specified x,y,z angle values. None
RotateEntityBone RotateEntityBone(#Entity, Bone$, x, y, z, Mode) Rotates the entity bone according to the specified x,y,z angle values. The bone has to be in manual mode, set with EnableManualEntityBoneControl. None
ScaleEntity ScaleEntity(#Entity, x, y, z [, Mode]) Scales the entity according to the specified x,y,z values. When using #PB_Relative mode, this is a factor based scale which means the entity size will be multiplied with the given value to obtain the new size. None
ScaleEntityBone ScaleEntityBone(#Entity, Bone$, x, y, z, Mode) Scale the specified entity bone. The bone has to be in manual mode, set with EnableManualEntityBoneControl. None
SetEntityAttribute SetEntityAttribute(#Entity, Attribute, Value.f) Set the specified attribute value to the given entity. None
SetEntityCollisionFilter SetEntityCollisionFilter(#Entity, CollisionGroup, CollisionMask) Set the entity collision group and mask. None
SetEntityMaterial SetEntityMaterial(#Entity, MaterialID [, SubEntity]) Assign a material to the specified #Entity. An entity can only have one material assigned at once. None
EntityAnimation (12)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
AddEntityAnimationTime AddEntityAnimationTime(#Entity, Animation$, Time) Add time to the specified #Entity animation. None
EntityAnimationBlendMode EntityAnimationBlendMode(#Entity, Mode) Changes the #Entity animation blendmode. None
EntityAnimationStatus Result = EntityAnimationStatus(#Entity, Animation$) Return the specified #Entity animation status. The return value can be one of the following constants: #PB_EntityAnimation_Stopped: The animation is stopped (or has ended). #PB_EntityAnimation_Started: The animation is running. #PB_EntityAnimation_Unknown: The animation doesn't exist in the mesh object.
GetEntityAnimationLength Result = GetEntityAnimationLength(#Entity, Animation$) Returns the #Entity animation length. The entity animation length (in milliseconds).
GetEntityAnimationTime Result = GetEntityAnimationTime(#Entity, Animation$) Returns the current #Entity animation time. The current entity animation time (in milliseconds) or 0 if the animation isn't running.
GetEntityAnimationWeight Result = GetEntityAnimationWeight(#Entity, Animation$) Returns the #Entity animation weight. The weight is useful when playing several animations at once. For example to do a smooth transition from one animation to another, it is possible to reduce progressively the weight of the first animation and increase the weight of the second animation. The current entity animation weight (value between 0.0 and 1.0). If the weight is 0, then the animation has no effect. If the weight is 1, then animation is fully playing.
SetEntityAnimationLength SetEntityAnimationLength(#Entity, Animation$, Length) Change the #Entity animation length.
SetEntityAnimationTime SetEntityAnimationTime(#Entity, Animation$, Time) Changes the current #Entity animation time. This is an absolute time position. To change the time relative to the current time, use AddEntityAnimationTime. None
SetEntityAnimationWeight SetEntityAnimationWeight(#Entity, Animation$, Weight) Changes the #Entity animation weight. The weight is useful when playing several animations at once. For example to do a smooth transition from one animation to another, it is possible to reduce progressively the weight of the first animation and increase the weight of the second animation. None
StartEntityAnimation StartEntityAnimation(#Entity, Animation$ [, Flags]) Start the specified #Entity animation. The animation is always started from the beginning. None
StopEntityAnimation StopEntityAnimation(#Entity, Animation$) Stop the specified #Entity animation. None
UpdateEntityAnimation UpdateEntityAnimation(#Entity, Animation$) Update the #Entity animation. For example, if the vertices of the mesh have been modified the animation cache needs to be recalculated. None
File (40)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
CloseFile CloseFile(#File) Close the specified file. None
CreateFile Result = CreateFile(#File, Filename$ [, Flags]) Create an empty file. Returns nonzero if the file was created successfully and zero if there was an error. If #PB_Any was used as the #File parameter then the new generated number is returned on success.
Eof Result = Eof(#File) Checks whether the end of the file has been reached. Returns nonzero if the read-pointer is at the end of the file or zero if not.
FileBuffersSize FileBuffersSize(#File, Size) Changes the size of the memory buffer used for file operations. None
FileID Result = FileID(#File) Returns the operating system handle of the file. Returns the file handle.
FileSeek FileSeek(#File, NewPosition.q [, Mode]) Change the read/write pointer position in the file. None
FlushFileBuffers Result = FlushFileBuffers(#File) Ensures that all buffered operations are written to disk. Nonzero if the buffer has been successfully written the disk. If an error occurred (ie: disk full, disk error), it will return zero.
IsFile Result = IsFile(#File) Tests if the given #File number is a valid and correctly initialized file. Returns nonzero if #File is a valid file and zero otherwise.
Loc Position.q = Loc(#File) Returns the read/write pointer position in the file. Returns the file pointer position relative to the start of the file in bytes.
Lof Length.q = Lof(#File) Returns the length of the specified file. Returns the length of the file in bytes.
OpenFile Result = OpenFile(#File, Filename$ [, Flags]) Opens a file for reading/writing or creates a new file if it does not exist. Returns nonzero if the file was opened successfully and zero if there was an error. If #PB_Any was used as the #File parameter then the new generated number is returned on success.
ReadAsciiCharacter Number.a = ReadAsciiCharacter(#File) Read an ASCII character (1 byte) from a file, starting at the current file position. Returns the read ASCII character or zero if there was an error.
ReadByte Number.b = ReadByte(#File) Read a byte (1 byte) from a file, starting at the current file position. Returns the read byte or zero if there was an error.
ReadCharacter Result.c = ReadCharacter(#File [, Format]) Read a character from a file, starting at the current file position. Returns the read character or zero if there was an error.
ReadData Result = ReadData(#File, *MemoryBuffer, LengthToRead) Read the content from the file to the specified memory buffer, starting at the current file position. Returns the number of bytes actually read from the file. If there is an error, the return value is zero.
ReadDouble Number.d = ReadDouble(#File) Read a double (8 bytes) from a file, starting at the current file position. Returns the read double value or zero if there was an error.
ReadFile Result = ReadFile(#File, Filename$ [, Flags]) Open an existing file for read-only operations. Returns nonzero if the file was opened successfully and zero if there was an error. If #PB_Any was used as the #File parameter then the new generated number is returned on success.
ReadFloat Number.f = ReadFloat(#File) Read a float (4 bytes) from a file, starting at the current file position. Returns the read float value or zero if there was an error.
ReadInteger Number.i = ReadInteger(#File) Read an integer (4 bytes in 32-bit executable, 8 bytes in 64-bit executable) from a file, starting at the current file position. Returns the read value or zero if there was an error.
ReadLong Number.l = ReadLong(#File) Read a long (4 bytes) from a file, starting at the current file position. Returns the read value or zero if there was an error.
ReadQuad Number.q = ReadQuad(#File) Read a quad (8 bytes) from a file, starting at the current file position. Returns the read number or zero if there was an error.
ReadString Text$ = ReadString(#File [, Flags [, Length]]) Read a string from a file until an 'End Of Line' or a 'Null' character is found (Unix, DOS and Macintosh file formats are supported). Returns the read string, or an empty string if the read has failed.
ReadStringFormat Result = ReadStringFormat(#File) Checks if the current file position contains a BOM (Byte Order Mark) and tries to identify the String encoding used in the file. Returns one of the following values: #PB_Ascii : No BOM detected. This usually means a plain text file. #PB_UTF8 : UTF-8 BOM detected. #PB_Unicode: UTF-16 (little endian) BOM detected. #PB_UTF16BE: UTF-16 (big endian) BOM detected. #PB_UTF32 : UTF-32 (little endian) BOM detected. #PB_UTF32BE: UTF-32 (big endian) BOM detected. The #PB_Ascii, #PB_UTF8 and #PB_Unicode results may be used directly in further calls to ReadString to read the file. The other results represent string formats that cannot be directly read with PureBasic string functions. They are included for completeness so that an application can display a proper error-message.
ReadUnicodeCharacter Number.u = ReadUnicodeCharacter(#File) Read a unicode character (2 bytes) from a file, starting at the current file position. Returns the read character or zero if there was an error.
ReadWord Number.w = ReadWord(#File) Read a word (2 bytes) from a file, starting at the current file position. Returns the read number or zero if there was an error.
TruncateFile TruncateFile(#File) Cuts the file at the current file position and discards all data that follows. None
WriteAsciiCharacter Result = WriteAsciiCharacter(#File, Number.a) Write an ASCII character (1 byte) to a file. Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.
WriteByte Result = WriteByte(#File, Number.b) Write a byte number (1 byte) to a file. Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.
WriteCharacter Result = WriteCharacter(#File, Character.c [, Format]) Write a character number (1 byte in ASCII, 2 bytes in unicode) to a file. Returns nonzero if the operation was successful or zero if it failed.
WriteData Result = WriteData(#File, *MemoryBuffer, Length) Write the content of the specified memory buffer to a file. Returns the number of bytes actually written to the file. If there is an error, the return-value is zero.
WriteDouble Result = WriteDouble(#File, Number.d) Write a double number (8 bytes) to a file. Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.
WriteFloat Result = WriteFloat(#File, Number.f) Write a float number (4 bytes) to a file. Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.
WriteInteger Result = WriteInteger(#File, Number) Write an integer number (4 bytes in 32-bit executable, 8 bytes in 64-bit executable) to a file. Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.
WriteLong Result = WriteLong(#File, Number) Write a long number (4 bytes) to a file. Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.
WriteQuad Result = WriteQuad(#File, Number.q) Write a quad number (8 bytes) to a file. Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.
WriteString Result = WriteString(#File, Text$ [, Format]) Write a string to a file. Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.
WriteStringFormat Result = WriteStringFormat(#File, Format) Writes a BOM (Byte Order Mark) at the current position in the file. Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.
WriteStringN Result = WriteStringN(#File, Text$ [, Format]) Write a string to a file and add an 'end of line' character. Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.
WriteUnicodeCharacter Result = WriteUnicodeCharacter(#File, Number) Write a unicode character (2 bytes) to a file. Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.
WriteWord Result = WriteWord(#File, Number) Write a word number (2 bytes) to a file. Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.
FileSystem (29)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
CheckFilename Result = CheckFilename(Filename$) Checks if the specified Filename$ doesn't contain invalid characters for the file-system. For example, on Windows '/' and '\' characters are not allowed in the filename. Returns nonzero if the filename does not contain invalid characters and zero if it does.
CopyDirectory Result = CopyDirectory(SourceDirectory$, DestinationDirectory$, Pattern$ [, Mode]) Copy the contents of the source directory to the destination. Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.
CopyFile Result = CopyFile(SourceFilename$, DestinationFilename$) Copy the source file to the destination. Returns nonzero if the operation was successful or zero if it failed.
CreateDirectory Result = CreateDirectory(DirectoryName$) Creates a new directory. Returns nonzero if the operation was successful or zero if it failed.
DeleteDirectory Result = DeleteDirectory(Directory$, Pattern$ [, Mode]) Deletes the specified Directory$ or files in that Directory$ matching the provided pattern. Returns nonzero if the operation was successful or zero if it failed.
DeleteFile Result = DeleteFile(Filename$ [, Mode]) Deletes the specified file. Returns nonzero if the operation was successful or zero if it failed.
DirectoryEntryAttributes Attributes = DirectoryEntryAttributes(#Directory) Returns the attributes of the current entry in the directory being listed with ExamineDirectory and NextDirectoryEntry functions. Returns the attributes of the current file. On Windows, Attributes is a combination of the following values: #PB_FileSystem_Hidden : File is hidden #PB_FileSystem_Archive : File has been changed and not archived since the last time #PB_FileSystem_Compressed: File is compressed #PB_FileSystem_Normal : Normal attributes #PB_FileSystem_ReadOnly : File is in read-only mode #PB_FileSystem_System : File is a system file On Linux or MacOSX, Attributes is a combination of these values: #PB_FileSystem_Link : The file is a symbolic link #PB_FileSystem_ReadUser : Access flags for the owning user #PB_FileSystem_WriteUser #PB_FileSystem_ExecUser #PB_FileSystem_ReadGroup : Access flags for the owning user's group #PB_FileSystem_WriteGroup #PB_FileSystem_ExecGroup #PB_FileSystem_ReadAll : Access flags for all other users #PB_FileSystem_WriteAll #PB_FileSystem_ExecAll
DirectoryEntryDate Result = DirectoryEntryDate(#Directory, DateType) Returns the date of the current entry in the directory being listed with ExamineDirectory and NextDirectoryEntry functions. Returns the specified date of the current directory entry in the format of the PureBasic Date library.
DirectoryEntryName Filename$ = DirectoryEntryName(#Directory) Returns the name of the current entry in the directory being listed with ExamineDirectory and NextDirectoryEntry functions. Returns the name of the current directory entry.
DirectoryEntrySize Size.q = DirectoryEntrySize(#Directory) Returns the size of the current entry in the directory being listed with ExamineDirectory and NextDirectoryEntry functions. Returns the size of the current directory entry in bytes.
DirectoryEntryType Result = DirectoryEntryType(#Directory) Returns the type of the current entry in the directory being listed with ExamineDirectory and NextDirectoryEntry functions. Returns one of the following values: #PB_DirectoryEntry_File : This entry is a file. #PB_DirectoryEntry_Directory: This entry is a directory.
ExamineDirectory Result = ExamineDirectory(#Directory, DirectoryName$, Pattern$) Start to examine a directory for listing with the functions NextDirectoryEntry, DirectoryEntryName and DirectoryEntryType. Returns nonzero if the directory can be enumerated or zero if there was an error. If #PB_Any was used as the #Directory parameter then the generated directory number is returned.
FileSize Result.q = FileSize(Filename$) Returns the size of the specified file. This function can also be used to check if a file or directory exists or not. Returns the size of the file in bytes, or one of the following values: -1: File not found. -2: File is a directory.
FinishDirectory FinishDirectory(#Directory) Finish the enumeration started with ExamineDirectory. This frees the resources associated with the #Directory listing. None
GetCurrentDirectory Result$ = GetCurrentDirectory() Returns the current directory for the program. Returns the full path of the current directory. It will end with a path separator #PS, #PS$ ('\' for Windows or '/' otherwise). It's very unlikely, but if this function fails, it will return an empty string.
GetExtensionPart Extension$ = GetExtensionPart(FullPathName$) Retrieves the file extension part of a full path. Returns the file extension. For example, if the full path is "C:\PureBasic\PB.exe", the result will be "exe".
GetFileAttributes Attributes = GetFileAttributes(Filename$) Returns the attributes of the given file. Returns the attributes of the file. If the file does not exist or the attributes cannot be read, the result is the value -1. On Windows, Attributes is a combination of the following values: #PB_FileSystem_Hidden : File is hidden #PB_FileSystem_Archive : File has been changed and not archived since the last time #PB_FileSystem_Compressed: File is compressed #PB_FileSystem_Normal : Normal attributes #PB_FileSystem_ReadOnly : File is in read-only mode #PB_FileSystem_System : File is a system file On Linux or MacOSX, Attributes is a combination of these values: #PB_FileSystem_Link : The file is a symbolic link #PB_FileSystem_ReadUser : Access flags for the owning user #PB_FileSystem_WriteUser #PB_FileSystem_ExecUser #PB_FileSystem_ReadGroup : Access flags for the owning user's group #PB_FileSystem_WriteGroup #PB_FileSystem_ExecGroup #PB_FileSystem_ReadAll : Access flags for all other users #PB_FileSystem_WriteAll #PB_FileSystem_ExecAll
GetFileDate Result = GetFileDate(Filename$, DateType) Returns the date of the specified file. Returns the requested date in the format of the PureBasic Date library.
GetFilePart Filename$ = GetFilePart(FullPathName$ [, Mode]) Retrieves the file part of a full path. Returns the file name. For example, if the full path is "C:\PureBasic\PB.exe", the result will be "PB.exe".
GetHomeDirectory Result$ = GetHomeDirectory() Returns the home directory path of the currently logged user. Returns the full path of the home directory. It will end with a path separator #PS, #PS$ ('\' for Windows or '/' otherwise). It's very unlikely, but if this function fails, it will return an empty string.
GetPathPart Path$ = GetPathPart(FullPathName$) Retrieves the path part of a full path. Returns the path part. For example, if the full path is "C:\PureBasic\PB.exe", the result will be "C:\PureBasic\".
GetTemporaryDirectory Result$ = GetTemporaryDirectory() Returns the temporary directory name. Returns the full path to the temporary directory. It will end with a path separator #PS, #PS$ ('\' for Windows or '/' otherwise). It's very unlikely, but if this function fails, it will return an empty string.
GetUserDirectory Result$ = GetUserDirectory(Type) Returns the directory path of the specified directory type. Returns the full path of the specified directory. It will end with a path separator #PS, #PS$ ('\' for Windows or '/' otherwise). If the type is not found it will return an empty string.
IsDirectory Result = IsDirectory(#Directory) Tests if the given directory number is a valid and correctly initialized directory enumeration. Returns nonzero if the given input is a valid enumeration and zero otherwise.
NextDirectoryEntry Result = NextDirectoryEntry(#Directory) This function must be called after an ExamineDirectory. It will go step-by-step into the directory and list its contents. Returns nonzero if a new entry was read from the directory and zero if there are no more entries.
RenameFile Result = RenameFile(OldFilename$, NewFilename$) Rename the old file to the new file. Returns nonzero if the operation succeeded and zero if it failed.
SetCurrentDirectory Result = SetCurrentDirectory(Directory$) Changes the current directory for the program. Returns nonzero if the current directory has been successfully changed, return zero otherwise.
SetFileAttributes Result = SetFileAttributes(Filename$, Attributes) Set the attributes of the given Filename$. Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero otherwise.
SetFileDate Result = SetFileDate(Filename$, DateType, Date) Changes the date of the specified file. Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero otherwise.
Font (5)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
FontID FontID = FontID(#Font) Returns the unique system identifier of the #Font. Returns the unique system ID of the font. This result is sometimes also referred to as a 'Handle'. Take a look at the extra chapter Handles and Numbers for more information.
FreeFont FreeFont(#Font) Free the given Font, previously loaded with LoadFont. None
IsFont Result = IsFont(#Font) Tests if the given #Font is a valid and correctly initialized font. Returns nonzero if #Font is a valid font and zero otherwise.
LoadFont Result = LoadFont(#Font, Name$, YSize [, Flags]) Tries to open the specified font. Returns nonzero if the font was loaded successfully and zero if not. If #PB_Any was used for the #Font parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
RegisterFontFile Result = RegisterFontFile(FileName$) Register a font file for use with the LoadFont command. All fonts contained in the file are then available. Returns nonzero if the file was successfully registered, zero otherwise.
Ftp (23)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
AbortFTPFile AbortFTPFile(#Ftp) Aborts the current background file transfer previously started with SendFTPFile or ReceiveFTPFile. If no file transfer is in progress, this function has no effect. None
CheckFTPConnection Result = CheckFTPConnection(#Ftp) Checks if the specified #Ftp connection is still connected to the server. Returns nonzero if the connection is still open and zero if the server closed the connection.
CloseFTP CloseFTP(#Ftp) Closes the specified #Ftp client connection previously opened with OpenFTP and free any associated resources. None
CreateFTPDirectory Result = CreateFTPDirectory(#Ftp, Directory$) Creates a new directory on the FTP server. Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.
DeleteFTPDirectory Result = DeleteFTPDirectory(#Ftp, Directory$) Deletes a directory on the FTP server. Returns nonzero if the directory was deleted or zero if the operation failed.
DeleteFTPFile Result = DeleteFTPFile(#Ftp, Filename$) Deletes a file on the FTP server. Returns nonzero if the file was deleted or zero if the operation failed.
ExamineFTPDirectory Result = ExamineFTPDirectory(#Ftp) Starts to examine the content of the current FTP directory. Returns nonzero if the operation succeeded or zero if it failed.
FinishFTPDirectory FinishFTPDirectory(#Ftp) Finishes the enumeration started with ExamineFTPDirectory. This allows to free the resources associated with the FTP listing. None
FTPDirectoryEntryAttributes Attributes = FTPDirectoryEntryAttributes(#Ftp) Returns the attributes of the current entry in the FTP enumeration being listed with the ExamineFTPDirectory and NextFTPDirectoryEntry functions. Returns a combination of the following values: #PB_FTP_ReadUser : Access flags for the owning user #PB_FTP_WriteUser #PB_FTP_ExecuteUser #PB_FTP_ReadGroup : Access flags for the owning user's group #PB_FTP_WriteGroup #PB_FTP_ExecuteGroup #PB_FTP_ReadAll : Access flags for all other users #PB_FTP_WriteAll #PB_FTP_ExecuteAll
FTPDirectoryEntryDate Result = FTPDirectoryEntryDate(#Ftp) Returns the date of the current entry in the FTP enumeration being listed with ExamineFTPDirectory and NextFTPDirectoryEntry functions. Returns the date of the entry in the format of the Date library.
FTPDirectoryEntryName Filename$ = FTPDirectoryEntryName(#Ftp) Returns the name of the current entry in the FTP enumeration being listed with ExamineFTPDirectory and NextFTPDirectoryEntry functions. Returns the entry name.
FTPDirectoryEntryRaw Entry$ = FTPDirectoryEntryRaw(#Ftp) Returns the raw line of the current entry in the FTP enumeration being listed with ExamineFTPDirectory and NextFTPDirectoryEntry functions, as it has been sent by the FTP server. It can be useful when the server isn't supported by ExamineFTPDirectory, so the information about the directory listing can still be retrieved and parsed accordingly. Returns the entry line as sent by the FTP server.
FTPDirectoryEntrySize Size = FTPDirectoryEntrySize(#Ftp) Returns the size of the current entry in the FTP enumeration being listed with ExamineFTPDirectory and NextFTPDirectoryEntry functions. Returns the size in bytes.
FTPDirectoryEntryType Result = FTPDirectoryEntryType(#Ftp) Returns the type of the current entry in the FTP enumeration being listed with ExamineFTPDirectory and NextFTPDirectoryEntry functions. Returns one of the following constants: #PB_FTP_File : This entry is a file. #PB_FTP_Directory: This entry is a directory.
FTPProgress Result.q = FTPProgress(#Ftp) Returns the progress of the current file transfer, started either with ReceiveFTPFile or SendFTPFile. Returns the actual number of bytes which has been received/sent or one of the following values: #PB_FTP_Started : The file transfer is in the initialization phase. #PB_FTP_Finished: The file transfer is finished correctly. #PB_FTP_Error : The file transfer is finished but an error occurred.
GetFTPDirectory Result$ = GetFTPDirectory(#Ftp) Returns the current FTP directory. Return the current FTP directory, relative to the FTP root.
IsFtp Result = IsFtp(#Ftp) Tests if the given #Ftp number is a valid and correctly initialized ftp client. Returns nonzero if the given number is a valid and correctly initialized client connection.
NextFTPDirectoryEntry Result = NextFTPDirectoryEntry(#Ftp) Moves to the next entry in an enumeration started with ExamineFTPDirectory. Returns nonzero if the next entry is available or zero if there are no more entries to examine.
OpenFTP Result = OpenFTP(#Ftp, ServerName$, User$, Password$ [, Flags [, Port]]) Tries to open a connection on the specified FTP or SFTP server. Returns nonzero if the connection was established correctly and zero if there was an error. If #PB_Any is used as the #Ftp parameter then the generated number for the connection is returned on success.
ReceiveFTPFile Result = ReceiveFTPFile(#Ftp, RemoteFilename$, Filename$ [, Asynchronous]) Receives a file from a FTP server. Returns nonzero if the file was downloaded correctly, or the asynchronous transfer was initialized correctly. On failure, the return-value is zero.
RenameFTPFile Result = RenameFTPFile(#Ftp, Filename$, NewFilename$) Renames a file on the FTP server. Returns nonzero if the file was renamed successfully and zero otherwise.
SendFTPFile Result = SendFTPFile(#Ftp, Filename$, RemoteFilename$ [, Asynchronous]) Sends a file to a FTP server. Returns nonzero if the file was uploaded correctly, or the asynchronous transfer was initialized correctly. On failure, the return-value is zero.
SetFTPDirectory Result = SetFTPDirectory(#Ftp, Directory$) Changes the current #Ftp directory, relative to the current directory. Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.
Gadget (85)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
AddGadgetColumn AddGadgetColumn(#Gadget, Position, Title$, Width) Adds a new column to the specified gadget. None
AddGadgetItem Result = AddGadgetItem(#Gadget, Position, Text$ [, ImageID [, Flags]]) Add a new item to the specified gadget. The return-value is only valid with the MDIGadget. If #PB_Any was used as the 'Position' parameter when adding an item to the MDIGadget, the return-value is the number that identifies the new MDI window.
BindGadgetEvent BindGadgetEvent(#Gadget, @Callback() [, EventType]) Bind a gadget event to a callback. It's an additional way to handle events in PureBasic, which works without problem with the regulars WindowEvent / WaitWindowEvent commands. It also allows to have real-time event notifications as the callback can be invoked as soon as the event occurs (useful for ScrollBarGadget, ScrollAreaGadget etc.). A gadget event can be unbound with UnbindGadgetEvent. None
ButtonGadget Result = ButtonGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height, Text$ [, Flags]) Create a button gadget in the current GadgetList. Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
ButtonImageGadget Result = ButtonImageGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height, ImageID [, Flags]) Create a button gadget with an image in the current GadgetList. Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
CalendarGadget Result = CalendarGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height [, Date [, Flags]]) Create a calendar gadget in the current GadgetList. This gadget displays a month calendar and lets the user select a date. Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
CanvasGadget Result = CanvasGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height [, Flags]) Create a canvas gadget in the current GadgetList. This gadget provides a drawing surface without alpha channel and events for mouse and keyboard interaction to easily create custom views. Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
CanvasOutput OutputID = CanvasOutput(#Gadget) Returns the OutputID of a CanvasGadget to perform 2D rendering operation on it. Returns the output ID or zero if drawing is not possible. This value should be passed directly to the StartDrawing function to start the drawing operation. The return-value is valid only for one drawing operation and cannot be reused.
CanvasVectorOutput VectorOutputID = CanvasVectorOutput(#Gadget [, Unit]) Returns the OutputID of a CanvasGadget to perform vector drawing operations on it. Returns the output ID or zero if drawing is not possible. This value should be passed directly to the StartVectorDrawing function to start the drawing operation. The return-value is valid only for one drawing operation and cannot be reused.
CheckBoxGadget Result = CheckBoxGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height, Text$ [, Flags]) Create a checkbox gadget in the current GadgetList. Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
ClearGadgetItems ClearGadgetItems(#Gadget) Clears all the items from the specified gadget. None
CloseGadgetList CloseGadgetList() Terminate the current gadget list creation and go back to the previous GadgetList. None
ComboBoxGadget Result = ComboBoxGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height [, Flags]) Create a ComboBox gadget in the current GadgetList. Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
ContainerGadget Result = ContainerGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height [, Flags]) Creates a container gadget in the current GadgetList. It's a simple panel gadget which can contain other gadgets. Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
CountGadgetItems Result = CountGadgetItems(#Gadget) Returns the number of items in the specified gadget. Returns the number of items in the gadget.
DateGadget Result = DateGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height [, Mask$ [, Date [, Flags]]]) Creates a String gadget in the current GadgetList, in which a date and/or time can be entered. Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
DisableGadget DisableGadget(#Gadget, State) Disable or enable the gadget. None
DisableGadgetRedraw DisableGadgetRedraw(#Gadget, State) Disables or enables the redrawing of a gadget. When a large number of items is added to a gadget such as ListIconGadget, TreeGadget or ListViewGadget, each insertion normally triggers a repaint which can make the update slow and flickering. Disabling the redraw before the mass update and enabling it again afterwards performs a single repaint once all the items are in place. Every call which disables the redraw must be paired with a call which enables it again. Enabling the redraw automatically refreshes the gadget content. The current selection and scroll position are kept across the operation. None
EditorGadget Result = EditorGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height [, Flags]) Creates an Editor gadget in the current GadgetList. Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
ExplorerComboGadget Result = ExplorerComboGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height, Directory$, [, Flags]) Creates a ComboBox that lets you display a path and all its parent folders, so the user can choose one of them. You can find such a ComboBox, for example, in the OpenFileRequester. Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
ExplorerListGadget Result = ExplorerListGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height, Directory$, [, Flags]) Creates a listing of a directory just as Explorer does. It lets the user choose a file or a folder and (if you do not prevent it by a flag) navigate through the whole directory tree. Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
ExplorerTreeGadget Result = ExplorerTreeGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height, Directory$, [, Flags]) Creates a tree listing of the directory tree just as Explorer does. It lets the user navigate through his file-system, and choose a file or folder. Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
FrameGadget Result = FrameGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height, Text$ [, Flags]) Creates a Frame gadget in the current GadgetList. This kind of gadget is decorative only. Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
FreeGadget FreeGadget(#Gadget) Free and remove the gadget from the display (and free its gadgetlist if the gadget was a container). None
GadgetHeight Result = GadgetHeight(#Gadget [, Mode]) Returns the height of the specified gadget. Returns the height of the gadget in pixels.
GadgetID GadgetID = GadgetID(#Gadget) Returns the unique system identifier of the #Gadget. Returns the system identifier. This result is sometimes also known as 'Handle'. Look at the extra chapter Handles and Numbers for more information.
GadgetItemID Result = GadgetItemID(#Gadget, Item) Returns the OS handle for the given item in a gadget. This is especially useful for use with the OS API. Returns the OS handle for the item or zero on failure.
GadgetToolTip GadgetToolTip(#Gadget, Text$) Associate the specified Text$ with the #Gadget. A tooltip text is text which is displayed when the mouse cursor is over the gadget for a small amount of time (typically a yellow floating box). None
GadgetType Result = GadgetType(#Gadget) Returns the type of gadget that is represented by the specified gadget number. It can be useful to write generic functions that work with more than one type of gadget. Returns one of the following values: #PB_GadgetType_Button : ButtonGadget #PB_GadgetType_ButtonImage : ButtonImageGadget #PB_GadgetType_Calendar : CalendarGadget #PB_GadgetType_Canvas : CanvasGadget #PB_GadgetType_CheckBox : CheckBoxGadget #PB_GadgetType_ComboBox : ComboBoxGadget #PB_GadgetType_Container : ContainerGadget #PB_GadgetType_Date : DateGadget #PB_GadgetType_Editor : EditorGadget #PB_GadgetType_ExplorerCombo : ExplorerComboGadget #PB_GadgetType_ExplorerList : ExplorerListGadget #PB_GadgetType_ExplorerTree : ExplorerTreeGadget #PB_GadgetType_Frame : FrameGadget #PB_GadgetType_HyperLink : HyperLinkGadget #PB_GadgetType_Image : ImageGadget #PB_GadgetType_IPAddress : IPAddressGadget #PB_GadgetType_ListIcon : ListIconGadget #PB_GadgetType_ListView : ListViewGadget #PB_GadgetType_MDI : MDIGadget #PB_GadgetType_OpenGL : OpenGLGadget #PB_GadgetType_Option : OptionGadget #PB_GadgetType_Panel : PanelGadget #PB_GadgetType_ProgressBar : ProgressBarGadget #PB_GadgetType_Scintilla : ScintillaGadget #PB_GadgetType_ScrollArea : ScrollAreaGadget #PB_GadgetType_ScrollBar : ScrollBarGadget #PB_GadgetType_Shortcut : ShortcutGadget #PB_GadgetType_Spin : SpinGadget #PB_GadgetType_Splitter : SplitterGadget #PB_GadgetType_String : StringGadget #PB_GadgetType_Text : TextGadget #PB_GadgetType_TrackBar : TrackBarGadget #PB_GadgetType_Tree : TreeGadget #PB_GadgetType_Web : WebGadget #PB_GadgetType_WebView : WebViewGadget #PB_GadgetType_Unknown : The type is unknown. Most likely it is not a PB gadget at all.
GadgetWidth Result = GadgetWidth(#Gadget [, Mode]) Returns the width of the specified gadget. Returns the width of the gadget in pixels.
GadgetX Result = GadgetX(#Gadget [, Mode]) Returns the X position of the specified gadget. Returns the X position relative to the gadgets parent or window (in pixels).
GadgetY Result = GadgetY(#Gadget [, Mode]) Returns the Y position of the specified gadget. Returns the Y position relative to the gadgets parent or window in pixels.
GetActiveGadget Result = GetActiveGadget() Returns the gadget number of the Gadget that currently has the keyboard focus. Returns the #Gadget number of the Gadget with the focus. If no Gadget has the focus, -1 is returned.
GetGadgetAttribute Value = GetGadgetAttribute(#Gadget, Attribute) Gets an attribute value of the specified gadget. Returns the value of the specified gadget attribute or 0 if the gadget does not support the attribute.
GetGadgetColor Color = GetGadgetColor(#Gadget, ColorType) Returns a color setting from the specified gadget. Returns the current color setting. This function returns the color that was previously set by SetGadgetColor. If no custom color is set for the #Gadget and ColorType, the function returns #PB_Default.
GetGadgetData Result = GetGadgetData(#Gadget) Returns the 'Data' value that has been stored for this gadget with the SetGadgetData function. This allows to associate a custom value with any gadget. Returns the current data value. If there was never a data value set for this gadget, the return-value will be 0.
GetGadgetFont FontID = GetGadgetFont(#Gadget) Get the FontID associated with the specified gadget. Returns the FontID for the gadget or the one used for newly created gadgets. Note: On Mac OSX, this function returns 0 if the gadget does not have a specific font associated with it.
GetGadgetItemAttribute Value = GetGadgetItemAttribute(#Gadget, Item, Attribute [, Column]) Gets an attribute value of the specified gadget item. Returns the attribute value or zero if the item or attribute does not exist.
GetGadgetItemColor Color = GetGadgetItemColor(#Gadget, Item, ColorType [, Column]) Returns a color setting from the specified gadget item. Returns the current color setting. This function returns the color that was previously set by SetGadgetItemColor. If no custom color is set for the #Gadget and ColorType, the function returns #PB_Default.
