GetGadgetItemData Result = GetGadgetItemData(#Gadget, Item) Returns the value that was previously stored with this gadget item with the SetGadgetItemData function. This allows to associate a custom value with the items of a gadget. Returns the stored data. If no value has been stored with the item yet, the return-value will be 0.
GetGadgetItemState Result = GetGadgetItemState(#Gadget, Item) Returns the item state of the specified gadget. Returns the state of the gadget item or 0 if there is an error. See below for the meaning of this value depending on the gadget type.
GetGadgetItemText Result$ = GetGadgetItemText(#Gadget, Item [, Column]) Returns the item text of the specified gadget. Returns the text of the gadget item or an empty string if there is an error.
GetGadgetState Result = GetGadgetState(#Gadget) Returns the current state of the gadget. Returns the state of the gadget. See below for its meaning depending on the gadget type.
GetGadgetText String$ = GetGadgetText(#Gadget) Returns the gadget text content of the specified gadget. Returns the gadget text, or an empty string if the gadget does not support text content.
HideGadget HideGadget(#Gadget, State) Hide or show a gadget. None
HyperLinkGadget Result = HyperLinkGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height, Text$, Color [, Flags]) Creates an HyperLink gadget in the current GadgetList. A hyperlink gadget is a text area which reacts to the mouse pointer by changing its color and the cursor shape. Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
ImageGadget Result = ImageGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height, ImageID [, Flags]) Creates an Image gadget in the current GadgetList. Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
IPAddressGadget Result = IPAddressGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height) Creates an IPAddress gadget in the current GadgetList. It allows you to easily enter a full IPv4 address. Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
IsGadget Result = IsGadget(#Gadget) Tests if the given gadget number is a valid and correctly initialized gadget. Returns nonzero if the input is a valid gadget and zero otherwise.
ListIconGadget Result = ListIconGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height, FirstColumnTitle$, FirstColumnWidth [, Flags]) Creates a ListIcon gadget in the current GadgetList. Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
ListViewGadget Result = ListViewGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height [, Flags]) Creates a ListView gadget in the current GadgetList. Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
MDIGadget Result = MDIGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height, SubMenu, MenuItem [, Flags]) Creates a client area, in which child windows can be displayed. These child windows are fully movable and sizable by the user in this area. Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
OpenGadgetList OpenGadgetList(#Gadget [, Item]) Use the specified gadget as a GadgetList, to dynamically add new gadgets to it. None
OpenGLGadget Result = OpenGLGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height [, Flags]) Creates an OpenGL gadget in the current GadgetList. This gadget provides an OpenGL drawing context and events for mouse and keyboard interaction to easily create 3D opengl view. Most of the OpenGL commands are directly available in PureBasic using the underscore API notation (command ending with an underscore, like 'glBegin_()'). Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
OptionGadget Result = OptionGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height, Text$) Creates an OptionGadget in the current GadgetList. Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.

ProgressBarGadget Result = ProgressBarGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height, Minimum, Maximum [, Flags]) Creates a ProgressBar gadget in the current GadgetList. Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.

RemoveGadgetItem RemoveGadgetItem(#Gadget, Position) Removes an item of the specified gadget. None
ResizeGadget ResizeGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height) Resize the specified gadget to the given position and dimensions. None
ScrollAreaGadget Result = ScrollAreaGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height, ScrollAreaWidth, ScrollAreaHeight [, ScrollStep [, Flags]]) Creates a ScrollArea gadget in the current GadgetList. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
ScrollBarGadget Result = ScrollBarGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height, Minimum, Maximum, PageLength [, Flags]) Creates a scrollbar gadget in the current GadgetList. Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
SetActiveGadget SetActiveGadget(#Gadget) Activates (sets the keyboard focus on) the gadget specified by the given gadget number. Activating a gadget allows it to become the current object to receive messages and handle keystrokes. None
SetGadgetAttribute SetGadgetAttribute(#Gadget, Attribute, Value) Changes an attribute value of the specified gadget. None
SetGadgetColor SetGadgetColor(#Gadget, ColorType, Color) Changes a color attribute on the given gadget. None
SetGadgetData SetGadgetData(#Gadget, Value) Stores the given value with the specified gadget. This value can later be read with the GetGadgetData function. This allows to associate a custom value with any gadget. None

SetGadgetItemColor SetGadgetItemColor(#Gadget, Item, ColorType, Color [, Column]) Changes a color attribute of the given gadget item. None
SetGadgetItemData SetGadgetItemData(#Gadget, Item, Value) Stores the given value with the specified gadget item. This value can later be read with the GetGadgetItemData function. This allows to associate a custom value with the items of a gadget. None
SetGadgetItemImage SetGadgetItemImage(#Gadget, Item, ImageID) Changes the image of the specified gadget item. None
SetGadgetItemState SetGadgetItemState(#Gadget, Item, State) Changes the item state of the specified gadget. None
SetGadgetItemText SetGadgetItemText(#Gadget, Item, Text$ [, Column]) Changes the item text of the specified gadget. None
SetGadgetState SetGadgetState(#Gadget, State) Change the current state of the specified gadget. None
SetGadgetText SetGadgetText(#Gadget, Text$) Change the gadget text content of the specified gadget. None
ShortcutGadget Result = ShortcutGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height, Shortcut) Creates a gadget for keyboard shortcut selection in the current GadgetList. The user can select it and hold down a keyboard combination to select a new shortcut. Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.

If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.

If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
StringGadget Result = StringGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height, Content$ [, Flags]) Creates a String gadget in the current GadgetList. It allows the user to enter a single line of text. TextGadget Result = TextGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height, Text$ [, Flags]) Creates a Text gadget in the current GadgetList. A TextGadget is a basic text area for displaying, not entering, text. Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
TrackBarGadget Result = TrackBarGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height, Minimum, Maximum [, Flags]) Creates a TrackBar gadget in the current GadgetList. It allows you to select a range of values with a slide bar, like ones found in several multimedia players. Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
TreeGadget Result = TreeGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height [, Flags]) Creates a Tree gadget in the current GadgetList. Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
UnbindGadgetEvent UnbindGadgetEvent(#Gadget, @Callback() [, EventType]) Unbind a gadget event from a callback. If no matching event callback is found, this command has no effect. None
UseGadgetList Result = UseGadgetList(WindowID) Selects the GadgetList window to which gadgets will be added. If there is no GadgetList on this window yet (because it was created with the #PB_Window_NoGadgets flag in OpenWindow or because it is not a PB window) it will be created. Returns the WindowID of the previous GadgetList window, or 0 if there was none. This value can be used to go back to the previous GadgetList later.
WebGadget Result = WebGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height, URL$ [, Flags]) Creates a Web gadget in the current GadgetList. It can display html pages. Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success. This function fails if the required components for the WebGadget cannot be loaded. See below for the requirements for the WebGadget on each OS.

If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget3D parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.

OpenGadgetList3D OpenGadgetList3D(#Gadget3D [, Item]) Use the specified 3D gadget as a GadgetList, to dynamically add new gadgets to it. Once the all the needed changes are done, CloseGadgetList3D should be called.
OptionGadget3D Result = OptionGadget3D(#Gadget3D, x, y, Width, Height, Text$) Creates an OptionGadget in the current GadgetList. The first time this function is called, a group is created and all following calls of OptionGadget3D will add a gadget to this group. To finish the group, just create a gadget of another type. These kind of gadgets are very useful as only one gadget from the group can be selected at any time. Nonzero on success, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget3D parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
PanelGadget3D Result = PanelGadget3D(#Gadget3D, x, y, Width, Height) Creates a panel gadget in the current GadgetList. Once a panel is created, its list of panels is empty. Nonzero on success, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget3D parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.

If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget3D parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.

ScrollAreaGadget3D Result = ScrollAreaGadget3D(#Gadget3D, x, y, Width, Height, ScrollAreaWidth, ScrollAreaHeight, ScrollStep) Creates a ScrollArea gadget in the current GadgetList. It's very useful when a gadget is too big to fit the window dimension. In that case, it can be put into a scrollarea. All the scrolling is handled automatically by the gadget. This is a container gadget, intended to have one or several gadget in its scroll area. Once the gadget is created, all future created gadgets will be created inside the scroll area. When all the needed gadgets have been created, CloseGadgetList3D must be called to return to the previous GadgetList. OpenGadgetList3D can be used later to add others gadgets on the fly in the scroll area. Nonzero on success, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget3D parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
ScrollBarGadget3D Result = ScrollBarGadget3D(#Gadget3D, x, y, Width, Height, Minimum, Maximum, PageLength [, Flags]) Creates a scrollbar gadget in the current GadgetList. It's widely used when displaying only a part of an object. Nonzero on success, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget3D parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
SetActiveGadget3D SetActiveGadget3D(#Gadget3D) Activates (sets the focus on) the gadget specified by the given #Gadget3D number. This is mainly used with ComboBoxGadget3D and StringGadget3D. Activating a gadget allows it to become the current object to receive messages and handle keystrokes. None
SetGadgetAttribute3D SetGadgetAttribute3D(#Gadget3D, Attribute, Value) Changes the attribute value of the specified 3D gadget. None
SetGadgetData3D SetGadgetData3D(#Gadget3D, Value) Stores the given value with the specified #Gadget3D. This value can later be read with the GetGadgetData3D function. This allows to associate a custom value with any gadget. None
SetGadgetItemData3D SetGadgetItemData3D(#Gadget3D, Item, Value) Stores the given value with the specified #Gadget3D item. This value can later be read with the GetGadgetItemData3D function. This allows to associate a custom value with the items of a gadget. This value will remain with the item, even if the item changes its index (for example because other items were deleted). None
SetGadgetItemState3D SetGadgetItemState3D(#Gadget3D, Item, State) Changes the item state of the specified #Gadget3D. None
SetGadgetItemText3D SetGadgetItemText3D(#Gadget3D, Item, Text$ [, Column]) Changes the item text of the specified #Gadget3D. None
SetGadgetState3D SetGadgetState3D(#Gadget3D, State) Changes the current state of the specified #Gadget3D. None
SetGadgetText3D SetGadgetText3D(#Gadget3D, Text$) Change the gadget text content of the specified 3D gadget. None
SpinGadget3D Result = SpinGadget3D(#Gadget3D, x, y, Width, Height, Minimum, Maximum) Creates a spin gadget in the current GadgetList. Nonzero on success, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget3D parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
StringGadget3D Result = StringGadget3D(#Gadget3D, x, y, Width, Height, Content$ [, Flags]) Creates a String gadget in the current GadgetList. This gadget accepts only one line of text. To get multi-line input, use the EditorGadget3D function. Nonzero on success, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget3D parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
TextGadget3D Result = TextGadget3D(#Gadget3D, x, y, Width, Height, Text$) Creates a text gadget in the current GadgetList. This is a basic text area for displaying, not entering, text. Nonzero on success, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget3D parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
Help (2)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
CloseHelp CloseHelp() Close the help window previously opened with OpenHelp. None
OpenHelp OpenHelp(Filename$, Topic$) Open and display a help window. None
HID (17)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
CloseHID CloseHID(#HID) Close the specified HID device. None
DisableHIDBlockingMode Result = DisableHIDBlockingMode(#HID, Status) Enable or disable blocking mode for the specified HID device. When blocking mode is disabled, read operations will return immediately even if no data is available. None
ExamineHIDs Result = ExamineHIDs([VendorId [, ProductId]]) Start the enumeration of available HID devices. Returns nonzero if the enumeration was started successfully and zero if there was an error.
GetHIDIndexedString Result$ = GetHIDIndexedString(#HID, Index) Get the specified indexed string value from the HID device. HID devices can store multiple strings at different indices, such as product name, manufacturer, etc. Returns the string value, or an empty string if there was an error.
GetHIDReportDescriptor *Buffer = GetHIDReportDescriptor(#HID) Get the HID report descriptor from the device as memory buffer. Returns the report descriptor as a memory buffer. To get the size of the descriptor, use MemorySize. Once the descriptor is no more needed, it can be freed with FreeMemory.
HIDError Result$ = HIDError() Read the last error information. Returns a string describing the last HID error that occurred.
HIDInfo Result$ = HIDInfo(Type [, #HID]) Get more information about the HID device. Returns a string containing the requested HID information.
IsHID Result = IsHID(#HID) Check if the given '#HID' is an initialized HID object. Returns nonzero if #HID is a valid HID device and zero otherwise.
NextHID Result = NextHID() Get the next HID device in the enumeration started with ExamineHIDs(). Returns nonzero if another HID device was found and zero if there are no more devices.
OpenHID Result = OpenHID(#HID, VendorId, ProductId [, SerialNumber]) Open the specified HID device for read or write operations. Returns nonzero if the device was opened successfully and zero if there was an error.
OpenHIDPath Result = OpenHIDPath(#HID, Path$) Open the specified HID device for read or write operations using a device path. Returns nonzero if the device was opened successfully and zero if there was an error.
ReadHIDData Result = ReadHIDData(#HID, *Buffer, Size [, Timeout]) Read data from the specified HID device. Returns the number of bytes actually read, or zero if there was an error or timeout.
ReceiveHIDFeatureReport Result = ReceiveHIDFeatureReport(#HID, *Buffer, Size) Receive a feature report from the HID device. Feature reports are used for bidirectional configuration and status information. Returns the number of bytes received, or zero if there was an error.
ReceiveHIDInputReport Result = ReceiveHIDInputReport(#HID, *Buffer, Size) Receive an input report from the HID device. Input reports are used for device-to-host communication and include the report ID. Returns the number of bytes received, or zero if there was an error.
SendHIDFeatureReport Result = SendHIDFeatureReport(#HID, *Buffer, Size) Send a feature report to the HID device. Feature reports are used for bidirectional configuration and status information. Returns the number of bytes sent, or zero if there was an error.
SendHIDOutputReport Result = SendHIDOutputReport(#HID, *Buffer, Size) Send an output report to the HID device. Output reports are used for host-to-device communication and include the report ID. Returns the number of bytes sent, or zero if there was an error.
WriteHIDData Result = WriteHIDData(#HID, *Buffer, Size) Write data to the specified HID device. Returns the number of bytes actually written, or zero if there was an error.
Http (15)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
AbortHTTP AbortHTTP(HttpConnection) Aborts the progress of the specified asynchronous download, started either with ReceiveHTTPFile or ReceiveHTTPMemory. It's also usable for HTTPRequest and HTTPRequestMemory (if #PB_HTTP_Asynchronous was used). None
FinishHTTP Result = FinishHTTP(HttpConnection) Free the resources associated to the specified asynchronous download, started either with ReceiveHTTPFile or ReceiveHTTPMemory. It must be always called after a successful call of ReceiveHTTPFile or ReceiveHTTPMemory. Depending on which Receive command was used to start the download, FinishHTTP() returns one of the following results: ReceiveHTTPFile: Amount of received bytes (size of the stored file). ReceiveHTTPMemory with the #PB_HTTP_Asynchronous flag set: Address of the memory area where the received data was stored. With MemorySize the amount of received data can be determined then.
GetURLPart Result$ = GetURLPart(URL$, Parameter$) Get a specific part of the given URL$. This can be a named parameter in the URL string or another part of the URL. Returns the parameter value or other part of the URL.
HTTPInfo Result$ = HTTPInfo(HttpRequest, Type [, Flags]) Returns information about an HTTP request created with HTTPRequest or HTTPRequestMemory. A string depending of the 'Type' parameter.
HTTPMemory *Buffer = HTTPMemory(HttpRequest) Returns a memory buffer containing the whole response of an HTTP request created with HTTPRequest or HTTPRequestMemory. Once done with it, the buffer needs to be freed with FreeMemory. If the flag #PB_HTTP_Asynchronous was used when calling HTTPRequest or HTTPRequestMemory, this command is only valid if the request has been successful. A memory buffer containing the whole response of an HTTP request. Once done with it, the buffer needs to be freed with FreeMemory.
HTTPProgress Result = HTTPProgress(HttpConnection) Returns the progress of the specified asynchronous download, started either with ReceiveHTTPFile or ReceiveHTTPMemory. The status of the download. It can be the current number of received bytes or one of the following values: #PB_HTTP_Success : the download has been successfully finished. #PB_HTTP_Failed : the download has failed. #PB_HTTP_Aborted : the download has been aborted with AbortHTTP.
HTTPProxy HTTPProxy(URL$ [, User$, Password$]) Specify a proxy to use for the following HTTP commands: ReceiveHTTPFile, ReceiveHTTPMemory, HTTPRequest and HTTPRequestMemory. None
HTTPRequest Result = HTTPRequest(Type, URL$ [, Data$ [, Flags [, Headers()]]]) Send an HTTP request with optional text data. If binary data needs to be sent, HTTPRequestMemory can be used. This command is designed to handle REST like web APIs easily. FinishHTTP needs to be always called once the request has been executed. Returns the HTTP request identifier if the call has been successfully initialized, zero otherwise. HTTPInfo can be used to get some info about the request. If #PB_HTTP_Asynchronous was specified, HTTPProgress can be used and AbortHTTP must be used. HTTPMemory can be used to get the result as a raw buffer (the raw buffer must be freed with FreeMemory). FinishHTTP has to be always called to finish a successfully initialized HTTP request, even if the call was synchronous.
HTTPRequestMemory Result = HTTPRequestMemory(Type, URL$ [, *Data, DataSize [, Flags [, Headers()]]]) Send an HTTP request with optional binary data. If text only data needs to be sent HTTPRequest can be used. This command is designed to handle REST like web API easily. FinishHTTP needs to be always called once the request has been executed. Returns the HTTP request identifier if the call has been successfully initialized, zero otherwise. HTTPInfo can be used to get some info about the request. If #PB_HTTP_Asynchronous was specified, HTTPProgress and AbortHTTP can be used. HTTPMemory can be used to get the result as a raw buffer (the raw buffer must be freed with FreeMemory). FinishHTTP has to be always called to finish a successfully initialized HTTP request, even if the call was synchronous.
HTTPTimeout HTTPTimeout(ConnectTimeout [, GlobalTimeout]) Specify timeout to use for the following HTTP commands: ReceiveHTTPFile, ReceiveHTTPMemory, HTTPRequest and HTTPRequestMemory. None
ReceiveHTTPFile Result = ReceiveHTTPFile(URL$, Filename$ [, Flags [, UserAgent$]]) Download a file to disk from the given URL$. Returns nonzero if the download was successful, zero otherwise. If #PB_HTTP_Asynchronous was specified, it returns the 'HttpConnection' value needed for HTTPProgress, AbortHTTP and FinishHTTP. When using #PB_HTTP_Asynchronous, FinishHTTP needs to be called when the download is finished (successfully or not).
ReceiveHTTPMemory *Buffer = ReceiveHTTPMemory(URL$ [, Flags [, UserAgent$]]) Download a file to a new memory buffer from the given URL$. Returns the new memory buffer address if the download was successful, zero otherwise. MemorySize can be used to get the size of the downloaded item. The memory buffer needs to be freed with FreeMemory once finished using it. If #PB_HTTP_Asynchronous was specified, it returns the 'HttpConnection' value needed for HTTPProgress, AbortHTTP and FinishHTTP. When using #PB_HTTP_Asynchronous, FinishHTTP needs to be called when the download is finished (successfully or not).
SetURLPart Result$ = SetURLPart(URL$, Parameter$, Value$) Set a specific part of the given URL$. Returns the modified URL.
URLDecoder Result$ = URLDecoder(URL$ [, Format]) Returns a decoded URL$ which has been encoded with the HTTP format. Returns the decoded URL.
URLEncoder Result$ = URLEncoder(URL$ [, Format]) Returns the URL$ encoded to the HTTP format. Returns the encoded URL. To convert an encoded URL back to a unencoded format, use URLDecoder
Image (24)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
AddImageFrame Result = AddImageFrame(#Image [, Index]) Adds a new frame to the specified image. The new frame will have the same dimension and depth like the image. Returns nonzero if the new frame has been successfully created, zero otherwise.
CatchImage Result = CatchImage(#Image, *MemoryAddress [, Size]) Load the specified image from the given memory area. Returns nonzero if the image was loaded successfully and zero if the image could not be loaded. If #PB_Any was specified as the #Image parameter then the auto-generated number is returned on success.
CopyImage Result = CopyImage(#Image1, #Image2) Creates an identical copy of an image. If the image is multi-frame, the current frame will be used for the copy. Returns nonzero if the image was copied successfully and zero if the copy could not be created. If #PB_Any was specified as the #Image2 parameter then the auto-generated number is returned on success.
CreateImage Result = CreateImage(#Image, Width, Height [, Depth [, BackColor]]) Create an empty image (with black background) which can be used to do rendering on it. Returns nonzero if the image was created successfully and zero if the image could not be created. If #PB_Any was specified as the #Image parameter then the auto-generated number is returned on success.
EncodeImage *Buffer = EncodeImage(#Image [, ImagePlugin [, Flags [, Depth]]]) Encode the specified image into a memory buffer. Returns a pointer to a newly allocated memory buffer containing the encoded image, or zero if the encoding has failed. MemorySize can be used to get the size of the encoded image. FreeMemory has to be used to free the buffer after use.
FreeImage FreeImage(#Image) Free the specified image and release its associated memory. None
GetImageFrame Index = GetImageFrame(#Image) Gets the current frame index of the image. The current frame index (starting from 0). If the image is not multi-frame, it will always return 0.
GetImageFrameDelay Result = GetImageFrameDelay(#Image) Returns the display delay (in milliseconds) for the current image frame. Each frame can have its own delay. Returns the display delay (in milliseconds) for the current image frame.
GrabImage Result = GrabImage(#Image1, #Image2, x, y, Width, Height) Create a new image with the selected area on the source image. If the image is multi-frame, the current frame will be used for the grab. Returns nonzero if the image was created successfully and zero if the image could not be created. If #PB_Any was specified as the #Image2 parameter then the auto-generated number is returned on success.
ImageDepth Result = ImageDepth(#Image [, Flags]) Returns the depth of the #Image, as it is stored internally by PureBasic. Returns one of the possible depth values described above.
ImageFormat Result = ImageFormat(#Image) Return the original image format. Returns the image original format. It can be one of the following value: #PB_ImagePlugin_JPEG #PB_ImagePlugin_JPEG2000 #PB_ImagePlugin_PNG #PB_ImagePlugin_TGA #PB_ImagePlugin_TIFF #PB_ImagePlugin_BMP #PB_ImagePlugin_ICON #PB_ImagePlugin_GIF #PB_ImagePlugin_WEBP If the image was not loaded from one of these formats, it will return zero. This is the case for images created with CreateImage or GrabImage.
ImageFrameCount Result = ImageFrameCount(#Image) Returns the number of frames of the image. Returns the frame count of the image. If the image is not multi-frame, it will always return 1.
ImageHeight Result = ImageHeight(#Image) Returns the height of the given image. Returns the height of the image in pixels.
ImageID Result = ImageID(#Image) Returns the ImageID of the image. Returns the operating system handle of the image.
ImageOutput OutputID = ImageOutput(#Image) Returns the OutputID of the image to perform 2D rendering operation on it. Alternatively, the ImageVectorOutput command can be used to perform vector drawing on the image. If the image is multi-frame, the current frame will be used. Returns the output ID or zero if drawing is not possible. This value should be passed directly to the StartDrawing function to start the drawing operation. The return-value is valid only for one drawing operation and cannot be reused.
ImageVectorOutput VectorOutputID = ImageVectorOutput(#Image [, Unit]) Returns the OutputID of the image to perform 2D vector drawing operations on it. If the image is multi-frame, the current frame will be used. Returns the output ID or zero if drawing is not possible. This value should be passed directly to the StartVectorDrawing function to start the drawing operation. The return-value is valid only for one drawing operation and cannot be reused.
ImageWidth Result = ImageWidth(#Image) Returns the width of the given image. Returns the width of the image in pixels.
IsImage Result = IsImage(#Image) Tests if the given image number is a valid and correctly initialized image. Returns nonzero if #Image is a valid image and zero if not.
LoadImage Result = LoadImage(#Image, Filename$ [, Flags]) Load the specified image from a file. Returns nonzero if the image was loaded successfully and zero if the image could not be loaded. If #PB_Any was specified as the #Image parameter then the auto-generated number is returned on success.
RemoveImageFrame Result = RemoveImageFrame(#Image, Index) Removes the specified frame from the image. Returns nonzero if the frame has been successfully removed, zero otherwise.
ResizeImage Result = ResizeImage(#Image, Width, Height [, Mode]) Resize the #Image to the given dimension. Returns nonzero if the operation succeeded and zero if it failed.
SaveImage Result = SaveImage(#Image, Filename$ [, ImagePlugin [, Flags [, Depth]]]) Saves the specified image to disk. Returns nonzero if the operation succeeded and zero if it failed.
SetImageFrame SetImageFrame(#Image, Index) Changes the current frame of the image. If the image is not multi-frame, this function has no effect. ImageOutput, ImageVectorOutput, CopyImage and GrabImage works on the current frame. None
SetImageFrameDelay Result = SetImageFrameDelay(#Image, Delay) Sets the display delay (in milliseconds) for the current image frame. Each frame can have its own delay. Sets the display delay (in milliseconds) for the current image frame.
ImagePlugin (13)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
UseGIFImageDecoder UseGIFImageDecoder() Enables the GIF image support for the CatchImage, LoadImage, CatchSprite and LoadSprite functions. Only LoadImage and CatchImage support multi-frame GIF (it will result in a multi-frame image). None
UseJPEG2000ImageDecoder UseJPEG2000ImageDecoder() Enables the JPEG 2000 image support for the CatchImage, LoadImage, CatchSprite and LoadSprite functions. None
UseJPEG2000ImageEncoder UseJPEG2000ImageEncoder() Enables the JPEG 2000 image support for the SaveImage and SaveSprite functions. None
UseJPEGImageDecoder UseJPEGImageDecoder() Enables the JPEG (Joint Picture Expert Group) image support for the CatchImage, LoadImage, CatchSprite and LoadSprite functions. None
UseJPEGImageEncoder UseJPEGImageEncoder() Enables the JPEG (Joint Picture Expert Group) image support for the SaveImage and SaveSprite functions. None
UseOSImageDecoder UseOSImageDecoder() Enables image loading through the imaging library provided by the operating system for the CatchImage, LoadImage, CatchSprite and LoadSprite functions. The following system libraries are used: GDI+ on Windows, ImageIO on macOS and GdkPixbuf (or Qt) on Linux. As no decoder is embedded in the executable, this plugin adds almost no code to the final program, and the list of supported formats as well as their security fixes automatically follow the operating system updates. A single call to this function replaces UseJPEGImageDecoder, UsePNGImageDecoder, UseGIFImageDecoder and the other individual decoders. It can still be combined with them: the automatic image format detection will pick the right decoder for each file. None
UseOSImageEncoder UseOSImageEncoder() Enables image saving through the imaging library provided by the operating system for the SaveImage and SaveSprite functions. The following system libraries are used: GDI+ on Windows, ImageIO on macOS and GdkPixbuf (or Qt) on Linux. As no encoder is embedded in the executable, this plugin adds almost no code to the final program. This single call provides the encoders for the #PB_ImagePlugin_JPEG, #PB_ImagePlugin_PNG, #PB_ImagePlugin_BMP, #PB_ImagePlugin_TIFF and #PB_ImagePlugin_GIF constants of SaveImage, so for example SaveImage with #PB_ImagePlugin_JPEG works without UseJPEGImageEncoder. If a dedicated encoder (such as UseJPEGImageEncoder) is also used, that one takes precedence. None
UsePNGImageDecoder UsePNGImageDecoder() Enables the PNG (Portable Network Graphic) image support for the CatchImage, LoadImage, CatchSprite and LoadSprite functions. None
UsePNGImageEncoder UsePNGImageEncoder() Enables the PNG (Portable Network Graphic) image support for SaveImage and SaveSprite. None
UseTGAImageDecoder UseTGAImageDecoder() Enables the TGA (Targa) image support for the CatchImage, LoadImage, CatchSprite and LoadSprite functions. None
UseTIFFImageDecoder UseTIFFImageDecoder() Enables the TIFF image support for the CatchImage, LoadImage, CatchSprite and LoadSprite functions. None
UseWebPImageDecoder UseWebPImageDecoder() Enables the WebP image support for the CatchImage, LoadImage, CatchSprite and LoadSprite functions. None
UseWebPImageEncoder UseWebPImageEncoder() Enables the WebP image support for the SaveImage and SaveSprite functions. None
Joint (11)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
ConeTwistJoint Result = ConeTwistJoint(#Joint, EntityID, TransformX, TransformY, TransformZ, EntityID2, TransformX2, TransformY2, TransformZ2) Creates a new cone twist joint between the two given entities. Cone twist can be used to attach arm or legs to body, etc. Returns zero if the joint can't be created. If #PB_Any is used as '#Joint' parameter, the new joint number will be returned as 'Result'.
EnableHingeJointAngularMotor EnableHingeJointAngularMotor(#Joint, Enable, TargetVelocity, MaxMotorImpulse) Enables the angular motor on the specified hinge joint. None
FreeJoint FreeJoint(#Joint) Frees the specified joint and releases all its associated memory. The joint must not be used (by using its number with the other functions in this library) after calling this function. None
GenericJoint Result = GenericJoint(#Joint, EntityID, TransformX, TransformY, TransformZ, EntityID2, TransformX2, TransformY2, TransformZ2) Creates a new joint, based on one or two points. Returns zero if the joint can't be created. If #PB_Any is used as '#Joint' parameter, the new joint number will be returned as 'Result'.
GetJointAttribute Result = GetJointAttribute(#Joint, Attribute) Get the specified attribute value of the given joint and its associated entities. Returns the value of the specified attribute or 0 if the joint does not support the attribute.
HingeJoint Result = HingeJoint(#Joint, EntityID, PivotX, PivotY, PivotZ, AxisX, AxisY, AxisZ, EntityID2, PivotX2, PivotY2, PivotZ2, AxisX2, AxisY2, AxisZ2) Creates a new hinge joint between the two given entities. Hinge can be used to simulate door, moving bridge etc. Returns zero if the joint can't be created. If #PB_Any is used as '#Joint' parameter, the new joint number will be returned as 'Result'.
HingeJointMotorTarget HingeJointMotorTarget(#Joint, Angle, Velocity) Sets the specified hinge joint motor target. None
IsJoint Result = IsJoint(#Joint) Tests if the given joint number is a valid and correctly initialized joint. Nonzero if the joint is valid, zero otherwise.
PointJoint Result = PointJoint(#Joint, EntityID, PivotX, PivotY, PivotZ [, EntityID2, PivotX2, PivotY2, PivotZ2]) Creates a new joint, based on one or two points. Returns zero if the joint can't be created. If #PB_Any is used as '#Joint' parameter, the new joint number will be returned as 'Result'.
SetJointAttribute SetJointAttribute(#Joint, Attribute, Value [, Axis]) Set the specified attribute value of the given joint and its associated entities. None
SliderJoint Result = SliderJoint(#Joint, EntityID, TransformX, TransformY, TransformZ, EntityID2, TransformX2, TransformY2, TransformZ2) Create a new slider joint between the two given entities. Slider can be used to move an entity with constraint on a plane surface, etc. Returns zero if the joint can't be created. If #PB_Any is used as '#Joint' parameter, the new joint number will be returned as 'Result'.
Joystick (7)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
ExamineJoystick Result = ExamineJoystick(#Joystick) Updates the current joystick state. It needs to be called before using the following functions: JoystickButton, JoystickAxisX, JoystickAxisY and JoystickAxisZ. Returns nonzero if the joystick state has been correctly updated, zero otherwise.
InitJoystick Result = InitJoystick() Initialize the joystick environment for later use. This function must be called before any other functions within this library. Returns the number of joysticks available for use.
JoystickAxisX Result = JoystickAxisX(#Joystick [, Pad [, Mode]]) Returns the joystick X axis state. Returns the joystick X axis value, depending of the specified mode.
JoystickAxisY Result = JoystickAxisY(#Joystick [, Pad [, Mode]]) Returns the joystick Y axis state. Returns the joystick Y axis value, depending of the specified mode.
JoystickAxisZ Result = JoystickAxisZ(#Joystick [, Pad [, Mode]]) Returns the joystick Z axis state. This axis is often referred to as trigger on new gamepads. Returns the joystick Z axis value, depending of the specified mode.
JoystickButton Result = JoystickButton(#Joystick, Button) Returns the joystick button state.
JoystickName Result$ = JoystickName(#Joystick) Returns the joystick's name. It can be useful when having several joysticks connected, to identify the right one. Returns the joystick name.
Json (53)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
AddJSONElement Result = AddJSONElement(JSONValue [, Index]) Add a new array element to a JSON value of type #PB_JSON_Array. Returns the address of the added JSON value. The newly added value initially has type #PB_JSON_Null.
AddJSONMember Result = AddJSONMember(JSONValue, Key$) Add a new member to a JSON value of type #PB_JSON_Object. If a member with the specified key already exists, it will be replaced. Returns the address of the added JSON member value. The newly added value initially has type #PB_JSON_Null.
CatchJSON Result = CatchJSON(#JSON, *Buffer, Size [, Flags]) Parse JSON data from a memory buffer. The contents of the memory buffer are expected to be encoded in UTF-8 format. The JSONValue function can be used to access the contained JSON value(s) after parsing. Nonzero if the JSON data was parsed correctly, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used for the #JSON parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
ClearJSONElements ClearJSONElements(JSONValue) Remove all array elements from a JSON value of type #PB_JSON_Array. None
ClearJSONMembers ClearJSONMembers(JSONValue) Remove all object members from a JSON value of type #PB_JSON_Object. None
ComposeJSON Result$ = ComposeJSON(#JSON [, Flags]) Compose the given JSON data into a string. A string can be parsed back into JSON data using the ParseJSON function. The JSON data as a string.
CreateJSON Result = CreateJSON(#JSON [, Flags]) Create new, empty JSON data. Initially, the data will contain a JSON value of type #PB_JSON_Null. The JSONValue function can be used to access this value to change it. Nonzero if the JSON data was created correctly, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used for the #JSON parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
ExamineJSONMembers Result = ExamineJSONMembers(JSONValue) Starts to examine the members of a JSON value of type #PB_JSON_Object. The individual members can be examined with the NextJSONMember, JSONMemberKey and JSONMemberValue functions. Returns nonzero if the object can be enumerated or zero if there was an error.
ExportJSON Result = ExportJSON(#JSON, *Buffer, Size [, Flags]) Export the given JSON data to a memory location. The JSON data will be encoded in UTF-8 format. Returns the number of bytes written to the memory location on success. If the function fails, the result is 0.
ExportJSONSize Result = ExportJSONSize(#JSON [, Flags]) Returns the size in bytes needed to successfully export the given JSON data to a memory buffer with the specified flags. The number of bytes needed to export the JSON data.
ExtractJSONArray ExtractJSONArray(JSONValue, Array()) Extract elements from the given JSON value of type #PB_JSON_Array into the specified Array(). The array will be resized to the number of elements contained in the JSON value. None
ExtractJSONList ExtractJSONList(JSONValue, List()) Extract elements from the given JSON value of type #PB_JSON_Array into the specified List(). The list will be resized to the number of elements contained in the JSON value. None
ExtractJSONMap ExtractJSONMap(JSONValue, Map()) Extract members from the given JSON value of type #PB_JSON_Object into the specified Map(). The map will be resized to the number of elements contained in the JSON value. None
ExtractJSONStructure ExtractJSONStructure(JSONValue, *Buffer, Structure [, Flags]) Extract members from the given JSON value of type #PB_JSON_Object into the specified structure memory. The structure will be cleared of any previous content before extracting the JSON values, unless #PB_JSON_NoClear flag is set. None
FreeJSON FreeJSON(#JSON) Frees the JSON data and its contained values. None
GetJSONBoolean Result = GetJSONBoolean(JSONValue) Return the boolean value of a JSON value of type #PB_JSON_Boolean. A JSON value can be set to a boolean with SetJSONBoolean. The boolean value #True or #False.
GetJSONDouble Result.d = GetJSONDouble(JSONValue) Return the value of a JSON value of type #PB_JSON_Number as a double precision floating point value. A JSON value can be set to a number with SetJSONDouble, SetJSONFloat, SetJSONInteger or SetJSONQuad. The number as a double.
GetJSONElement Result = GetJSONElement(JSONValue, Index) Return the JSON array element at the given 'Index' of a JSON value of type #PB_JSON_Array. The address of the JSON value at the specified array index. If the given 'Index' is out of range, the result is 0.
GetJSONFloat Result.f = GetJSONFloat(JSONValue) Return the value of a JSON value of type #PB_JSON_Number as a single precision floating point value. A JSON value can be set to a number with SetJSONDouble, SetJSONFloat, SetJSONInteger or SetJSONQuad. The number as a float.
GetJSONInteger Result = GetJSONInteger(JSONValue) Return the value of a JSON value of type #PB_JSON_Number as an integer value. A JSON value can be set to a number with SetJSONDouble, SetJSONFloat, SetJSONInteger or SetJSONQuad. The number as an integer.
GetJSONMember Result = GetJSONMember(JSONValue, Key$) Return the JSON object member with the given Key$ of a JSON value of type #PB_JSON_Object. The address of the JSON value with the specified key. If the given 'Key$' does not exist in the object, the result is 0.
GetJSONQuad Result.q = GetJSONQuad(JSONValue) Return the value of a JSON value of type #PB_JSON_Number as an quad value. A JSON value can be set to a number with SetJSONDouble, SetJSONFloat, SetJSONInteger or SetJSONQuad. The number as an quad.
GetJSONString Result$ = GetJSONString(JSONValue) Return the value of a JSON value of type #PB_JSON_String as a string. The string contained in the JSON value.
InsertJSONArray InsertJSONArray(JSONValue, Array()) Insert the specified Array() into the given JSON value. The JSON value will be changed to type #PB_JSON_Array. None
InsertJSONList InsertJSONList(JSONValue, List()) Insert the specified List() into the given JSON value. The JSON value will be changed to type #PB_JSON_Array. None
InsertJSONMap InsertJSONMap(JSONValue, Map()) Insert the specified Map() into the given JSON value. The JSON value will be changed to type #PB_JSON_Object. None
InsertJSONStructure InsertJSONStructure(JSONValue, *Buffer, Structure) Insert the contents of the specified structure memory into the given JSON value. The JSON value will be changed to type #PB_JSON_Object and contain one member for each member in the structure. None
IsJSON Result = IsJSON(#JSON) Tests if the given #JSON number represents valid and correctly initialized JSON data. Nonzero if #JSON is valid JSON data, zero otherwise.
JSONArraySize Result = JSONArraySize(JSONValue) Returns the number of elements in a JSON value of type #PB_JSON_Array. The number of elements in the JSON array.
JSONErrorLine Result = JSONErrorLine() Returns the line number within the JSON input of the last failed JSON parsing operation with ParseJSON, CatchJSON or LoadJSON. The line number (1-based) of the last JSON parser error.
JSONErrorMessage Result$ = JSONErrorMessage() Returns a message describing the cause for the failure at the last JSON parsing operation with ParseJSON, CatchJSON or LoadJSON. The error message in english.
JSONErrorPosition Result = JSONErrorPosition() Returns the character position within the line of the last failed JSON parsing operation with ParseJSON, CatchJSON or LoadJSON. The character position (1-based) of the last JSON parser error within the line reported by JSONErrorLine.
JSONMemberKey Result$ = JSONMemberKey(JSONValue) After a call to NextJSONMember, returns the key of the currently examined JSON object member of the specified JSON value of type #PB_JSON_Object. The key of the current JSON object member.
JSONMemberValue Result = JSONMemberValue(JSONValue) After a call to NextJSONMember, returns the address of the currently examined JSON object member of the specified JSON value of type #PB_JSON_Object. The address of the current JSON object member.
JSONObjectSize Result = JSONObjectSize(JSONValue) Returns the number of members in a JSON value of type #PB_JSON_Object. The number of members in the JSON object.
JSONType Result = JSONType(JSONValue) Returns the type of the given JSON value. It can be one of the following: #PB_JSON_Null The value represents the JSON literal null. #PB_JSON_String The value contains a string. GetJSONString can be used to read the string. #PB_JSON_Number The value contains a number. GetJSONDouble, GetJSONFloat, GetJSONInteger or GetJSONQuad can be used to read the number. #PB_JSON_Boolean The value contains a boolean. GetJSONBoolean can be used to read the value. #PB_JSON_Array The value contains an array of JSON elements. JSONArraySize returns the size of the array. GetJSONElement can be used to get a specific array element. AddJSONElement, RemoveJSONElement, ResizeJSONElements or ClearJSONElements can be used to modify the array. #PB_JSON_Object The value contains an object (a set of key/value pairs). JSONObjectSize returns the number of members in the object. GetJSONMember returns a specific member value. ExamineJSONMembers can be used to examine the member values. AddJSONMember, RemoveJSONMember or ClearJSONMembers can be used to modify the object.
JSONValue Result = JSONValue(#JSON) Returns the value of the specified #JSON data. The type of the value can be checked with JSONType. The JSON value. The result is never 0 for a valid #JSON data.
LoadJSON Result = LoadJSON(#JSON, FileName$ [, Flags]) Parse JSON data from a file. The contents of the file are expected to be encoded in UTF-8 format. Files with another character encoding cannot be read by this command. The JSONValue function can be used to access the contained JSON value(s) after parsing. Nonzero if the JSON data was parsed correctly, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used for the #JSON parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
NextJSONMember Result = NextJSONMember(JSONValue) After a call to ExamineJSONMembers, this function is used to iterate over all members of the specified JSON value of type #PB_JSON_Object. JSONMemberKey and JSONMemberValue can be used to get information about the current member. Returns non-zero if another JSON member was found. If the result is zero then there are no more JSON members to be examined.
ParseJSON Result = ParseJSON(#JSON, Input$ [, Flags]) Parse JSON data from a string. The JSONValue function can be used to access the contained JSON value(s) after parsing. Nonzero if the JSON data was parsed correctly, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used for the #JSON parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
RemoveJSONElement RemoveJSONElement(JSONValue, Index) Remove the element at the specified index from a JSON value of type #PB_JSON_Array. None
RemoveJSONMember RemoveJSONMember(JSONValue, Key$) Remove the memver with the specified key from a JSON value of type #PB_JSON_Object. None
ResizeJSONElements ResizeJSONElements(JSONValue, Size) Resize a JSON value of type #PB_JSON_Array so that it has the given number of elements. None
SaveJSON Result = SaveJSON(#JSON, FileName$ [, Flags]) Save the given JSON data to a file. The file will be encoded in UTF-8 (without a leading byte-order mark). Returns non-zero if the file was saved successfully. If there is an error while saving the file, the result is zero.
SetJSONArray Result = SetJSONArray(JSONValue) Change the type of the JSON value to #PB_JSON_Array. The array will have no elements (even if the value previously contained array elements). Returns the Array number, zero otherwise.
SetJSONBoolean SetJSONBoolean(JSONValue, Value) Change the type of the JSON value to #PB_JSON_Boolean and store the given boolean value. None
SetJSONDouble SetJSONDouble(JSONValue, Value.d) Change the type of the JSON value to #PB_JSON_Number and store the given double value. None
SetJSONFloat SetJSONFloat(JSONValue, Value.f) Change the type of the JSON value to #PB_JSON_Number and store the given float value. None
SetJSONInteger SetJSONInteger(JSONValue, Value) Change the type of the JSON value to #PB_JSON_Number and store the given integer value. None
SetJSONNull SetJSONNull(JSONValue) Clear the JSON value and set the type to #PB_JSON_Null. None
SetJSONObject Result = SetJSONObject(JSONValue) Change the type of the JSON value to #PB_JSON_Object. The object will have no members (even if the value previously contained object members). Returns the Object number, zero otherwise.
SetJSONQuad SetJSONQuad(JSONValue, Value.q) Change the type of the JSON value to #PB_JSON_Number and store the given quad value. None
SetJSONString SetJSONString(JSONValue, String$) Change the type of the JSON value to #PB_JSON_String and store the given string. None
Keyboard (6)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
ExamineKeyboard ExamineKeyboard() Updates the keyboard state. This function has to be called before using KeyboardInkey, KeyboardPushed or KeyboardReleased. None
InitKeyboard Result = InitKeyboard() Initializes the keyboard environment for later use. This function has to be called before any other function in this library. Nonzero if the keyboard access can be initialized, zero otherwise.
KeyboardInkey String$ = KeyboardInkey() Returns the last typed character, very useful when keyboard input is required within a gaming application, such as the name in highscore, in game console, etc.). The last typed character.
KeyboardMode KeyboardMode(Flags) Changes the current behavior of the keyboard. This function affects KeyboardPushed and KeyboardReleased. None
KeyboardPushed Result = KeyboardPushed(KeyID) Checks if the specified key is pressed. Any number of keys may be pressed at the same time. The function ExamineKeyboard must be called before this function in order to update the keyboard state. The keyboard behavior can be changed with KeyboardMode. To check if a specified key has been pushed and released, see KeyboardReleased. Nonzero if the specified key is pushed, zero otherwise.
KeyboardReleased Result = KeyboardReleased(KeyID) Checks if the specified key has been pushed and released. This function is useful for switch key checks, like a 'Pause' key in a game (one time the game is paused, next time it will continue). The function ExamineKeyboard must be called before this function to update the keyboard state. The keyboard behavior can be changed with KeyboardMode. Nonzero if the specified key has been pushed and released, zero otherwise.
Library (15)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
CallCFunction Result = CallCFunction(#Library, FunctionName$ [,Parameter1 [, Parameter2...]]) Calls a function, in the specified library, in such a manner that the parameters are handled in the same fashion as a normal 'C' language function. Returns the return-value of the called function or zero if the library does not contain a function with the given name.
CallCFunctionFast Result = CallCFunctionFast(*FunctionPointer [,Parameter1 [, Parameter2...]]) Calls a function directly, using its address. The function is expected to use the cdecl calling convention (the convention used by the C language). Returns the return-value of the called function.
CallFunction Result = CallFunction(#Library, FunctionName$ [,Parameter1 [, Parameter2...]]) Calls a function in the specified library, by using its name. The specified library must have previously been opened with the OpenLibrary function. The function is expected to use the stdcall calling convention (the standard in most DLLs on Windows). Returns the return-value of the called function or zero if the library does not contain a function with the given name.
CallFunctionFast Result = CallFunctionFast(*FunctionPointer [,Parameter1 [, Parameter2...]]) Calls a function directly, using its address. The function is expected to use the stdcall calling convention (the standard in most DLLs on Windows). Returns the return-value of the called function.
CloseLibrary CloseLibrary(#Library) Closes a library previously opened using OpenLibrary, and frees any memory associated with this library. None
CountLibraryFunctions Result = CountLibraryFunctions(#Library) Counts the number of functions available in a library. The library must be open when this function is called. Returns the number of functions available in the library.
ExamineLibraryFunctions Result = ExamineLibraryFunctions(#Library) Initiates the process of examining the functions contained within a library. Returns nonzero if the functions can be examined and zero if not.
GetFunction Result = GetFunction(#Library, FunctionName$) Checks if the library, previously opened using the OpenLibrary function, contains the given function and returns the function pointer. Returns the address to the function in the library on success and zero if the library does not contain a function with that name.
GetFunctionEntry Result = GetFunctionEntry(#Library, FunctionEntry) Checks if the library, contains the given function entry. This searches for a library function by its position within the libraries function table, rather than by its name. Returns the address to the function in the library on success and zero if the library does not contain a function with that index.
IsLibrary Result = IsLibrary(#Library) Tests if the given library number is valid and if the library has been correctly initialized. Returns nonzero if the input is a valid library and zero if not.
LibraryFunctionAddress Result = LibraryFunctionAddress() Returns the address of the function in the library currently being examined with the ExamineLibraryFunctions and NextLibraryFunction functions. Returns the address of the current function in memory. This is useful as parameter for the functions CallFunctionFast or CallCFunctionFast.
LibraryFunctionName Result$ = LibraryFunctionName() Returns the name of the function in the library currently being examined with the ExamineLibraryFunctions and NextLibraryFunction functions. Returns the name of the current function.
LibraryID Result = LibraryID(#Library) Returns the unique ID which identifies the specified library in the operating system. Returns the unique ID.
NextLibraryFunction Result = NextLibraryFunction() Moves to the next library function in an enumeration started with ExamineLibraryFunctions. Returns nonzero if the next library function was found and zero if there are no more functions to be examined.
OpenLibrary Result = OpenLibrary(#Library, Filename$) Opens a shared library in order that the functions within it may be accessed. Returns nonzero if the library was opened successfully and zero if not. If #PB_Any was used as the #Library parameter then the generated number for the library is returned on success.
Light (24)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
CopyLight Result = CopyLight(#Light, #NewLight) Creates a new light which is the exact copy of the specified light. All light attributes such as: color, specular color, position etc. are duplicated. Nonzero if the light was successfully duplicated, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used for the #NewLight parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
CreateLight Result = CreateLight(#Light, Color [, x, y, z [, Flags]]) Creates a new #Light of the given color in the current world. If WorldShadows is required, it must be called before creating lights. Nonzero if the light was successfully created, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used for the #Light parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
DisableLightShadows DisableLightShadows(#Light, State) Disables or enables the light shadow casting. None
FreeLight FreeLight(#Light) Frees the specified #Light. All its associated memory is released and at this point, the object no longer may be used. None
GetLightColor Result = GetLightColor(#Light, Type) Gets the specified light color value. The specified light RGB color value.
HideLight HideLight(#Light, State) Hides or shows the specified #Light. None
IsLight Result = IsLight(#Light) Tests if the given light is valid and correctly initialized. Nonzero if the light is valid, zero otherwise.
LightAttenuation LightAttenuation(#Light, Range, Attenuation) Changes the light attenuation. None
LightDirection LightDirection(#Light, x, y, z) Changes the direction of a light. The position of the light is not changed. None
LightDirectionX Result = LightDirectionX(#Light [, Mode]) Returns the 'x' direction vector of the light. The 'x' direction vector of the light. This value is always between -1.0 and 1.0.
LightDirectionY Result = LightDirectionY(#Light [, Mode]) Returns the 'y' direction vector of the light. The 'y' direction vector of the light. This value is always between -1.0 and 1.0.
LightDirectionZ Result = LightDirectionZ(#Light [, Mode]) Returns the 'z' direction vector of the light. The 'z' direction vector of the light. This value is always between -1.0 and 1.0.
LightID LightID = LightID(#Light) Returns the unique system identifier of the light. The unique system identifier of the light.
LightLookAt LightLookAt(#Light, x, y, z) Changes the #Light orientation in the world, to point towards the specified x,y,z point. None
LightPitch Result = LightPitch(#Light [, Mode]) Gets the pitch of the #Light. The current pitch value of the light.
LightRoll Result = LightRoll(#Light [, Mode]) Gets the roll of the #Light. The current roll value of the light.
LightX Result = LightX(#Light [, Mode]) Returns the current position of the light in the world. The 'x' position of the light.
LightY Result = LightY(#Light [, Mode]) Returns the current position of the light in the world. The 'y' position of the light.
LightYaw Result = LightYaw(#Light [, Mode]) Gets the yaw of the #Light. The current yaw value of the light.
LightZ Result = LightZ(#Light [, Mode]) Returns the current position of the light in the world. The 'z' position of the light.
MoveLight MoveLight(#Light, x, y, z [, Mode]) Moves the specified light. None
RotateLight RotateLight(#Light, x, y, z [, Mode]) Rotates the #Light according to the specified x,y,z angle values. None
SetLightColor SetLightColor(#Light, Type, Color) Changes the light color value. None
SpotLightRange SpotLightRange(#Light, InnerAngle, OuterAngle [, FallOff]) Changes the spot #Light behavior. The light has to be created with the #PB_Light_Spot flag. None
List (24)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
AddElement *Result = AddElement(List()) Adds a new empty element after the current element or as the first item in the list if there are no elements in it. This new element becomes the current element of the list. Returns non-zero if the new element was created and zero otherwise. The value returned is a pointer to the new element data.
ChangeCurrentElement ChangeCurrentElement(List(), *NewElement) Changes the current element of the specified list to the given new element. This function is very useful if you want to "remember" an element, and restore it after performing other processing. None
ClearList ClearList(List()) Clears all the elements in this list and releases their memory. After this call the list is still usable, but the list is empty (i.e. there are no elements in it). None
CompareList Result = CompareList(List1(), List2() [, Flags]) Compare each elements of the two lists for equality. Recursively compares also contents of structured lists with dynamic elements (such as embedded arrays, lists or maps). The two lists are considered the equal if they have the same type and size and if each pair of elements is equal. Returns nonzero if both lists are the same or zero if they differ.
CopyList Result = CopyList(SourceList(), DestinationList()) Copy the contents of one list to another list. After a successful copy, the two lists are identical. Returns non-zero if the copy succeeded and zero otherwise.
DeleteElement *Result = DeleteElement(List() [, Flags]) Remove the current element from the list. After this call, the new current element is the previous element (the one before the deleted element). If that element does not exist (in other words, you deleted the first element in the list) then there is no more current element, as it will be before the first element, like after a ResetList. Returns the memory address of the new current element of the list. If the list has no current element after the deletion, the result is 0.
ExtractList Result = ExtractList(List(), Text$ [, Separator$ [, Limit]]) Splits 'Text$' into 'List()', using 'Separator$' to find each element. 'List()' is cleared first. Returns the number of elements found (and stored into 'List()').
FirstElement *Result = FirstElement(List()) Changes the current list element to the first list element. Returns the address of the data in the first list element if successful and zero if there if there are no elements in the list.
FreeList FreeList(List()) Free the specified list and release all its associated memory. To access this list again later, NewList has to be called for it. None
InsertElement *Result = InsertElement(List()) Inserts a new empty element before the current element, or at the start of the list if the list is empty (i.e. has no elements in it). This new element becomes the current element of the list. Returns non-zero if the new element was created and zero otherwise. The value returned is a pointer to the new element data.
JoinList Result$ = JoinList(List() [, Separator$ [, Limit]]) Joins all the elements of 'List()' into a single string, using 'Separator$' between each element. Returns the resulting string.
LastElement *Result = LastElement(List()) Change the current list element to the last list element. Returns the address of the data in the last list element if successful and zero if there if there are no elements in the list.
ListIndex Index = ListIndex(List()) Find out the position of the current element in the list, considering that the first element is at the position 0. This function is very fast, and can be used a lot without performance issue (it doesn't iterate the list but uses a cached value). A number containing the position of the current element within the list. The first element is at position 0, the next at 1 and so on. A value of -1 means there is no current element (either the list is empty or ResetList has been used).
ListSize Result = ListSize(List()) Returns the number of elements in the list. It does not change the current element. This function is very fast (it doesn't iterates all the list but uses a cached result) and can be safely used to determine if a list is empty or not. The total number of elements in the list. If the list is not initialized, it returns -1 (for example after FreeList).
MergeLists MergeLists(SourceList(), DestinationList() [, Location]) Moves all elements from the SourceList() to the DestinationList(). This is a fast operation because the element data itself is not moved to merge the two lists. None
MoveElement MoveElement(List(), Location [, *RelativeElement]) Moves the current element of the specified list to a different position in the list. The moved element remains the current element of the list. This is a fast operation because the element data itself is not moved to change the location in the list. None
NextElement *Result = NextElement(List()) Moves from the current element to the next element in the list, or onto the first element if you have previously called ResetList Returns the address of the data in the next list element if successful and zero if there if there is no next element.
PopListPosition PopListPosition(List()) Restores the current element of the list previously remembered using PushListPosition. None
PreviousElement *Result = PreviousElement(List()) Moves from the current element to the previous element in the list. Returns the address of the data in the previous list element if successful and zero if there if there is no previous element.
PushListPosition PushListPosition(List()) Remembers the current element (if any) of the list so it can later be restored using PopListPosition. The position is remembered on a stack (a lifo stack: last in, first out), so multiple calls to this function are possible. None
ResetList ResetList(List()) Resets the current list element to be before the first element. This means no element is actually valid. However, this is very useful to allow you to process all the elements by using NextElement. None
SelectElement *Result = SelectElement(List(), Position) Change the current list element to the element at the specified position. This is very useful if you want to jump to a specific position in the list without manually iterating through the list using a loop. Returns the data address of the selected element if successful or zero if the position is out of range.
SplitList SplitList(SourceList(), DestinationList() [, KeepCurrent]) Moves the elements in SourceList() from the current element onwards to the DestinationList(). This is a fast operation because the element data itself is not moved to split the list. None
SwapElements SwapElements(List(), *FirstElement, *SecondElement) Swaps the position of two elements in the specified list. This command is a fast way to reorganize a list, because it does not actually move the element data itself. None
Mail (13)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
AddMailAttachment Result = AddMailAttachment(#Mail, Description$, Filename$ [, MimeType$]) Add a file attachment to the mail. Returns nonzero if the attachment was added successfully and zero if not.
AddMailAttachmentData Result = AddMailAttachmentData(#Mail, Description$, *Buffer, BufferLength [, MimeType$]) Add memory data as an attachment to the mail. Returns nonzero if the attachment was added successfully and zero if not.
AddMailRecipient AddMailRecipient(#Mail, Address$, Flags) Add a recipient to the specified mail. None
CreateMail Result = CreateMail(#Mail, From$, Subject$ [, Encoding]) Create a new, empty mail. Returns nonzero if the mail was created successfully and zero if not. If #PB_Any was used as the #Mail parameter, then the auto-generated number is returned in case of success.
FreeMail FreeMail(#Mail) Free the specified mail and release its associated memory. None
GetMailAttribute Result$ = GetMailAttribute(#Mail, Attribute) Return the specified mail attribute. Returns the attribute as a string. An empty string is returned if the attribute does not exist.
GetMailBody Result$ = GetMailBody(#Mail) Return the specified mail body, previously set with SetMailBody. Returns the body as a string.
IsMail Result = IsMail(#Mail) Tests if the given mail number is valid and if the mail has been correctly initialized. Returns nonzero if the specified number was valid.
MailProgress Result = MailProgress(#Mail) Return the progress of the specified mail transfer, started with SendMail. Returns the number of transferred bytes, or one of the following values: #PB_Mail_Connected: The mail transfer is in its initialization phase. #PB_Mail_Finished : The mail transfer is finished correctly. #PB_Mail_Error : The mail transfer is finished but an error occurred.
RemoveMailRecipient RemoveMailRecipient(#Mail [, Address$ [, Flags]) Remove a recipient from the specified mail. None
SendMail Result = SendMail(#Mail, Smtp$ [, Port [, Flags [, User$, Password$]]]) Send the specified mail. Returns nonzero if the mail was sent correctly and zero otherwise.
SetMailAttribute SetMailAttribute(#Mail, Attribute, Value$) Change the specified mail attribute with the new value. None
SetMailBody SetMailBody(#Mail, Body$) Change the mail body. GetMailBody can be used to read the body content. None
Map (13)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
AddMapElement Result = AddMapElement(Map(), Key$ [, Flags]) Adds a new empty element in the Map() using the specified key. This new element becomes the current element of the map. Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. The value returned is a pointer to the new element data.
ClearMap ClearMap(Map()) Clears all the elements in the specified map and releases their memory. After this call the map is still usable, but is empty (i.e. there are no more elements in it). None
CompareMap Result = CompareMap(Map1(), Map2() [, Flags]) Compare each elements of the two maps for equality. Recursively compares also contents of structured maps with dynamic elements (such as embedded arrays, lists or maps). The two maps are considered the equal if they have the same type and size and if each pair of elements is equal. Returns nonzero if both maps are the same or zero if they differ.
CopyMap Result = CopyMap(SourceMap(), DestinationMap()) Copy every element of the source to the destination map. Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If the two maps do not have the same type then the copy will fail.
DeleteMapElement Result = DeleteMapElement(Map() [, Key$]) Removes the current element or the element with the given key from the specified map. Returns the memory address of the new current element of the map. If the map has no current element after the deletion, the result is 0.
FindMapElement Result = FindMapElement(Map(), Key$) Change the current map element to the element associated at the specified key. Returns nonzero if the key was found and zero otherwise. The value returned is a pointer to the element data.
FreeMap FreeMap(Map()) Free the specified map and release all its associated memory. To access it again NewMap has to be called. None
MapKey Key$ = MapKey(Map()) Returns the key of the current map element. Returns the key of the current element. If there is no current element, an empty string is returned.
MapSize Result = MapSize(Map()) Returns the number of elements in the specified map. It does not change the current element. Returns the number of elements in the map.
NextMapElement Result = NextMapElement(Map()) Moves from the current element to the next element in the specified map, or onto the first element if ResetMap was previously called. Returns nonzero if the next element was set and zero if there is no next element. The value returned is a pointer to the new element data.
PopMapPosition PopMapPosition(Map()) Restores the current element of the map previously remembered using PushMapPosition. None
PushMapPosition PushMapPosition(Map()) Remembers the current element (if any) of the map so it can later be restored using PopMapPosition. The position is remembered on a stack structure, so multiple calls to this function are possible. None
ResetMap ResetMap(Map()) Resets the current element of the specified map to be before the first element. This means no more current element. However, this is very useful to process all the elements by using NextMapElement. None
Material (33)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
AddMaterialLayer AddMaterialLayer(#Material, TextureID [, Mode [, TextureCoordinateIndex]]) Adds a new layer to the material and put the specified texture in it. None
CopyMaterial Result = CopyMaterial(#Material, #NewMaterial) Creates a new material which is the exact copy of the specified material. Nonzero if the material was successfully duplicated, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used for the #NewMaterial parameter, then the generated number is returned on success.
CountMaterialLayers Result = CountMaterialLayers(#Material) Returns the number of layers the material contains. The number of layers the material contains.
CreateAnimatedMaterial Result = CreateAnimatedMaterial(#Material, TextureArray(), Duration.f) Creates a new animated material using the specified textures. Nonzero if the animated material was successfully created, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used for the #Material parameter, then the generated number is returned on success.
CreateMaterial Result = CreateMaterial(#Material, TextureID [, Color]) Creates a new material using the specified texture. Nonzero if the material was successfully created, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used for the #Material parameter, then the generated number is returned on success.
CreateShader Result = CreateShader(ShaderID, VertexProgram$, FragmentProgram$) Creates a new shader using the specified vertex and fragment programs. Nonzero if the shader was successfully created, zero otherwise.
CreateShaderMaterial Result = CreateShaderMaterial(#Material, ShaderID) Creates a new shader based material. Nonzero if the shader based material was successfully created, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used for the #Material parameter, then the generated number is returned on success.
DisableMaterialLighting DisableMaterialLighting(#Material, State) Enables or disables the dynamic #Material lighting. The object which will use this material will be not affected by a dynamic light, created with the CreateLight function. Dynamic lighting is enabled by default when a material is created. None
FreeMaterial FreeMaterial(#Material) Frees the specified #Material. All its associated memory is released and this object can't be used anymore. None
GetMaterialAttribute Result = GetMaterialAttribute(#Material, Attribute) Get the specified material attribute. The value of the specified attribute.
GetMaterialColor Result = GetMaterialColor(#Material, Type) Get the specified material color. Returns the RGB color value. Separate color channel value can easily be retrieved with Red, Green and Blue.
GetScriptMaterial Result = GetScriptMaterial(#Material, Name$) Get a material defined in an OGRE script file. Scripts are loaded and parsed when calling Parse3DScripts. Nonzero if the material was successfully created, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used for the #Material parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
IsMaterial Result = IsMaterial(#Material) Tests if the given material is valid and correctly initialized. Nonzero if the material is valid, zero otherwise.
MaterialAnimation MaterialAnimation(#Material, Texture$, NbFrames, Time.f) Add an animated texture to the material. An animated texture is composed of any number of textures, all the same size, with the frame number appended before the extension in their filename. For example, if "test.jpg" is specified as 'Texture$' and 'NbFrames' is set to 3, the textures "test_0.jpg", "test_1.jpg" and "test_2.jpg" will be loaded and used for the material. None
MaterialBlendingMode MaterialBlendingMode(#Material, Mode) Changes the way the material will be blended with the scene (screen background). None
MaterialCullingMode MaterialCullingMode(#Material, Mode) Set the culling mode for the material. None
MaterialFilteringMode MaterialFilteringMode(#Material, Mode [, MaxAnisotropicValue]) Changes the material filtering mode. None
MaterialFog MaterialFog(#Material, Color, Intensity, StartDistance, EndDistance) Adds a fog effect on the specified material. None
MaterialID MaterialID = MaterialID(#Material) Returns the unique system identifier of the material. The unique system identifier of the material.
MaterialShaderAutoParameter MaterialShaderAutoParameter(#Material, ProgramType, ParameterName$, ParameterType, ExtraValue.f) Set a parameter value for the shader based material previous created with CreateShaderMaterial. None
MaterialShaderParameter MaterialShaderParameter(#Material, ProgramType, ParameterName$, ParameterType, v1.f, v2.f, v3.f, v4.f) Set specific parameters to the shader. None
MaterialShaderTexture MaterialShaderTexture(#Material, TextureID1, TextureID2, TextureID3, TextureID4) Sets the textures to use for the shader based material previous created with CreateShaderMaterial. None
MaterialShadingMode MaterialShadingMode(#Material, Mode) Changes the #Material shading mode. None
MaterialShininess MaterialShininess(#Material, Shininess [, SpecularColor]) Changes the shininess of the #Material (the size of the specular highlights). None
MaterialTextureAliases MaterialTextureAliases(#Material, TextureID1, TextureID2, TextureID3, TextureID4) Set textures for use in a material script. It allows to use the same material script with dynamic textures. In the material script, the texture reference needs to be changed from 'texture mytexture.jpg' to 'texture_alias texture1' (or 'texture_alias texture2', 'texture_alias texture3', 'texture_alias texture4'). None
ReloadMaterial ReloadMaterial(MaterialName$, ScriptFilename$, ParseScript) Reloads a material from an OGRE script based on its name. This is useful when using customized materials stored in script files. None

ResetMaterial ResetMaterial(ObjectType) Resets all materials for the specified object types. None
RotateMaterial RotateMaterial(#Material, Angle, Mode [, Layer]) Rotates the material layer according to the angle value. None
ScaleMaterial ScaleMaterial(#Material, x, y [, Layer]) Scales the material. The parameters 'x' and 'y' are scale factors. None
ScrollMaterial ScrollMaterial(#Material, x, y, Mode [, Layer]) Scrolls the material layer according to x,y values. None

SetMaterialColor SetMaterialColor(#Material, Type, Color) Set the specified material color. None

The result can be transformed into degrees using the Degree function.
Result.f Result.f(.d) = ATanH(Value.f(.d)) Returns the area hyperbolic tangent of the specified value. Returns the hyperbolic angle.
