Result.f Result.f(.d) = Exp(Number.f(.d)) Returns the result of the exponential function. This is the value e raised to the power 'Number'. Returns the value e raised to the power 'Number'.

Returns the value representing infinity. The result is a float or double value depending on whether it is assigned to a float or double variable.

Result.f Result.f(.d) = IsNaN(Value.f(.d)) Returns nonzero if the given value 'Not a Number'. This value is the result of some invalid calculations. It can also be generated using the NaN function. Returns nonzero if the input value is not a number and zero otherwise.
Result.f Result.f(.d) = Pow(Number.f(.d), Power.f(.d)) Returns the given number, raised to the given power. Returns the value of 'Number' raised to the power 'Power'.

Result.f Result.f(.d) = Log10(Number.f(.d)) Returns the log in base 10 of the given number. Returns the log in base 10.

Result.f Result.f(.d) = NaN() Returns the special floating-point value representing 'Not a Number'. This value is returned from invalid calculations such as calculating the square root of a negative number. Returns the value representing NaN. The result is a float or double value depending on whether it is assigned to a float or double variable.
Result.f Result.f(.d) = Radian(Angle.f(.d)) Converts the given angle from degrees into radian. Returns the angle in radian.
Result.f Result.f(.d) = Round(Number.f(.d), Mode) Round the specified float number according to the given mode.

Result.f Result.f(.d) = SinH(Angle.f(.d)) Returns the hyperbolic sine of the specified hyperbolic angle. Returns the hyperbolic sine of the angle.
Result.f Result.f(.d) = Sqr(Number.f(.d)) Returns the square root of the specified number. Returns the square root of the number.
Result.f Result.f(.d) = Tan(Angle.f(.d)) Returns the tangent of the specified angle. Returns the tangent of the specified angle.
Result.f Result.f(.d) = TanH(Angle.f(.d)) Returns the hyperbolic tangent of the specified hyperbolic angle. Returns the hyperbolic tangent of the angle.
Sign Result = Sign(Number.f(.d)) Returns an integer value representing the sign of the given number. - Returns 0 if Number is zero. - Returns 1 if Number is positive. - Returns -1 if Number is negative.

AllocateMemory *MemoryID = AllocateMemory(Size [, Flags]) Allocates a contiguous memory area with the specified size in bytes. The new memory area will be cleared and filled with zeros. Returns the address of the allocated memory, or zero if the memory cannot be allocated.

This dynamic structure item is properly initialized and ready to use, without the need to call InitializeStructure(). To access the structure data, a pointer associated with the specified 'StructureName' has to be used. The address of the new dynamic structure item, zero otherwise.

Returns one of the following values: #PB_String_Equal : if String1 equals String2 #PB_String_Lower : if String1 is lower than String2 #PB_String_Greater: if String1 greater than String2

FreeMemory FreeMemory(*MemoryID) Free the memory previously allocated with AllocateMemory, ReAllocateMemory, Ascii or UTF8. None
FreeStructure FreeStructure(*Item) Free the dynamic structure item previously allocated with AllocateStructure. There is no need to call ClearStructure() before freeing the structure. None
MemorySize Result = MemorySize(*MemoryID) Returns the length of the given memory area. Returns the size of the given memory area in bytes.
MemoryStringLength Result = MemoryStringLength(*String [, Flags]) Returns the length (in characters) of the given zero terminated string. Returns the length of the string in characters.
MoveMemory MoveMemory(*SourceMemoryID, *DestinationMemoryID, Size) Copy a memory area starting from the *SourceMemoryID to the *DestinationMemoryID. Overlapping of the two memory areas is allowed. None

PeekB Value.b = PeekB(*MemoryBuffer) Reads a byte (1 byte) number from the specified memory address. Returns the value of the byte.

PeekW Value.w = PeekW(*MemoryBuffer) Reads a word (2 bytes) number from the specified memory address. Returns the value of the word.

PokeQ PokeQ(*MemoryBuffer, Number) Writes a quad (8 bytes) number to the specified memory address. None

The amount of bytes written to memory, not including the terminating null-character. The amount of written bytes differs from the string length in characters if the format is #PB_UTF8 or #PB_Unicode.
PokeU PokeU(*MemoryBuffer, Number) Writes an unicode character (2 bytes) to the specified memory address. None
PokeW PokeW(*MemoryBuffer, Number) Writes a word (2 bytes) number to the specified memory address. None
ReAllocateMemory *NewMemoryID = ReAllocateMemory(*MemoryID, Size [, Flags]) Resizes the given memory buffer to a new size. The memory may be copied to a new location in the process if there is not enough memory available at its current location. Returns the new address of the memory area if it could be resized. In this case, the old '*MemoryID' address can no longer be used. If resizing the memory area failed (because there is not enough memory available), the result is zero, and the '*MemoryID' address is still valid with the existing memory area and the old size.

BindMenuEvent BindMenuEvent(#Menu, MenuItem, @Callback()) Bind a menu event to a callback. It's an additional way to handle events in PureBasic, which works without problem with the regulars WindowEvent / WaitWindowEvent commands. A menu event can be unbound with UnbindMenuEvent. None
CloseSubMenu CloseSubMenu() Close the current sub menu and return to the enclosing menu after a previous call to OpenSubMenu. None
CreateImageMenu Result = CreateImageMenu(#Menu, WindowID [, Flags]) Creates a new empty menu on the given window with support for images in the menu items. Nonzero if the menu was successfully created, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used for the #Menu parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
CreateMenu Result = CreateMenu(#Menu, WindowID) Creates a new empty menu on the given window. Nonzero if the menu was created successfully, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used for the #Menu parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
CreatePopupImageMenu Result = CreatePopupImageMenu(#Menu [, Flags]) Creates a new empty popup menu with image support for its items. Returns nonzero if the menu was created successfully and zero if not. If #PB_Any was used for the #Menu parameter, then the generated number is returned on success.
CreatePopupMenu Result = CreatePopupMenu(#Menu) Creates a new empty popup menu. Nonzero if the menu was successfully created, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used for the #Menu parameter then the generated number is returned on success.

GetMenuItemText Text$ = GetMenuItemText(#Menu, Item) Returns the text from the specified menu item. Returns the menu item text.
GetMenuTitleText Text$ = GetMenuTitleText(#Menu, Title) Returns the title text of the specified menu title item. Returns the text of the menu title item.
HideMenu HideMenu(#Menu, State) Hide or show the specified menu. None
IsMenu Result = IsMenu(#Menu) Tests if the given menu is valid and correctly initialized. Nonzero if the menu is valid, zero otherwise.
MenuBar MenuBar() Creates a separator bar in the current menu. None
MenuHeight Result = MenuHeight() Returns the height of the menu title bar. This allows the correct height of a window to be calculated when using a menu. Returns the height in pixels of the menu bar.
MenuID MenuID = MenuID(#Menu) Returns the unique system identifier of the given menu. Returns the ID of the menu. This sometimes also known as 'Handle'. Look at the extra chapter handles "Handles and Numbers" for more information.

MenuTitle MenuTitle(Title$) Creates a new title item on the menu. None

SetMenuTitleText SetMenuTitleText(#Menu, Title, Text$) Changes the specified menu title item text. None

NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
AddMeshManualLOD AddMeshManualLOD(#Mesh, #MeshLOD, Distance.f) Add a new level of detail (LOD) to the mesh. The #Mesh will be replaced automatically with #MeshLOD (which is often a simplified version of #Mesh, with less details) when displayed above the specified distance from the camera. Several LOD mesh can be used for the same #Mesh depending of the distance. None
AddSubMesh AddSubMesh([Type]) Add a new submesh to the current mesh previously created with CreateMesh. A mesh can have any number of submeshes. A submesh position is relative to the mesh position. Once a submesh is created, use the following commands to build it: MeshVertexPosition, MeshFace and MeshIndex. None
BuildMeshLOD BuildMeshLOD(#Mesh [, NbLOD, Distance.f, ReductionValue.f]) Build automatically one or several level of detail (LOD) for the mesh. The #Mesh will be replaced automatically with less complex mesh when displayed above the specified distance from the camera. If more precise LOD meshes are required, AddMeshManualLOD can be used. None
BuildMeshShadowVolume BuildMeshShadowVolume(#Mesh) Create the shadow volume for the specified #Mesh. It is required if the mesh needs to cast a shadow. It should be done once the mesh creation is completely done, or the shadow will not match the mesh. None
BuildMeshTangents BuildMeshTangents(#Mesh) Automatically computes the tangent vectors for all vertices of the specified mesh. Dynamic meshes are not supported (meshes created with the #PB_Mesh_Dynamic flag). None
CopyMesh Result = CopyMesh(#Mesh, #NewMesh) Creates a #NewMesh which is the exact copy of the specified #Mesh. If #PB_Any is used as the '#NewMesh' parameter, then the new mesh number will be returned as 'Result'. Dynamic meshes are not supported for copy (meshes created with the #PB_Mesh_Dynamic flag). If the Result equals 0, then the mesh copy has failed. If #NewMesh already exists, then it is freed and replaced by a new one.
CreateCapsule Result = CreateCapsule(#Mesh, Radius.f, Height.f [, NbRings, NbSegments, NbHeightSegments) Create a new capsule mesh. Returns nonzero if the mesh was created successfully and zero if there was an error. If #PB_Any was used as the #Mesh parameter, then the new generated number is returned on success.
CreateCone Result = CreateCone(#Mesh, Radius.f, Height.f [, NbBaseSegments, NbHeightSegments]) Create a new cone. Returns nonzero if the mesh was created successfully and zero if there was an error. If #PB_Any was used as the #Mesh parameter, then the new generated number is returned on success.
CreateCube Result = CreateCube(#Mesh, Size) Create a new cube mesh. Returns nonzero if the mesh was created successfully and zero if there was an error. If #PB_Any was used as the #Mesh parameter, then the new generated number is returned on success.
CreateCylinder Result = CreateCylinder(#Mesh, Radius.f, Height.f [, NbBaseSegments, NbHeightSegments, CloseTop]) Create a new cylinder mesh. Returns nonzero if the mesh was created successfully and zero if there was an error. If #PB_Any was used as the #Mesh parameter then the new generated number is returned on success.
CreateDataMesh Result = CreateDataMesh(#Mesh, Array.MeshVertex() [, Mode]) Creates a new #Mesh from the specified 2 dimensional array of MeshVertex type. This command allows faster mesh creation than using CreateMesh by preparing an array and submitting in one batch to the command.
CreateIcoSphere Result = CreateIcoSphere(#Mesh, Radius.f [, Iterations) Create a new ico-sphere mesh. Returns nonzero if the mesh was created successfully and zero if there was an error. If #PB_Any was used as the #Mesh parameter, then the new generated number is returned on success.
CreateLine3D Result = CreateLine3D(#Mesh, x, y, z, Color, x2, y2, z2, Color2) Create a new 3D line mesh. The line is a wireframe object which can be used to ease debugging. To change the line position, just create it again. Returns nonzero if the mesh was created successfully and zero if there was an error. If #PB_Any was used as the #Mesh parameter then the new generated number is returned on success.
CreateMesh Result = CreateMesh(#Mesh [, Type [, Mode]) Creates a new empty #Mesh. After creation, the further commands of this library like MeshVertexPosition or MeshFace can be used to build it. Returns nonzero if the mesh was created successfully and zero if there was an error. If #PB_Any was used as the #Mesh parameter, then the new generated number is returned on success.
CreatePlane Result = CreatePlane(#Mesh, TileSizeX, TileSizeZ, TileCountX, TileCountZ, TextureRepeatCountX, TextureRepeatCountZ) Create a new plane mesh. Returns nonzero if the mesh was created successfully and zero if there was an error. If #PB_Any was used as the #Mesh parameter then the new generated number is returned on success.
CreateSphere Result = CreateSphere(#Mesh, Radius.f [, NbSegments, NbRings]) Create a new sphere mesh. Returns nonzero if the mesh was created successfully and zero if there was an error. If #PB_Any was used as the #Mesh parameter then the new generated number is returned on success.
CreateTorus Result = CreateTorus(#Mesh, Radius.f, SectionRadius.f, Height.f [, NbSectionSegments, NbCircleSegments) Create a new torus mesh. Returns nonzero if the mesh was created successfully and zero if there was an error. If #PB_Any was used as the #Mesh parameter then the new generated number is returned on success.
CreateTube Result = CreateTube(#Mesh, OuterRadius.f, InnerRadius.f, Height.f [, NbBaseSegments, NbHeightSegments) Create a new tube mesh. Returns nonzero if the mesh was created successfully and zero if there was an error. If #PB_Any was used as the #Mesh parameter then the new generated number is returned on success.
FinishMesh FinishMesh(StaticMesh) Finish the creation of the current mesh started with CreateMesh. None
FreeMesh FreeMesh(#Mesh) Free the specified #Mesh. All its associated memory is released and the object may not be used anymore. None
GetMeshData Result = GetMeshData(#Mesh, SubMesh, DataArray(), Flags, FirstIndex, LastIndex) Get internal mesh data, like vertices, face etc. Dynamic meshes are not supported (meshes created with the #PB_Mesh_Dynamic flag). Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If success, DataArray() has been resized and contains the mesh information.
IsMesh Result = IsMesh(#Mesh) Tests if the given #Mesh is valid and the mesh has been correctly initialized. This function is bulletproof and may be used with any value. If Result equals zero then the given mesh has not been properly created or initialized. This is the correct way to ensure a mesh is ready to use.
LoadMesh Result = LoadMesh(#Mesh, Filename$) Loads a new mesh. Before loading a mesh, an archive must be specified with Add3DArchive. Nonzero if the mesh was successfully loaded, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used for the #Mesh parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
MeshDirectAdd MeshDirectAdd(#Mesh, MeshVertexArray(), MeshFaceArray(), Type, MaterialID) Add a new submesh to the specified #Mesh. A mesh can have any number of submeshes. A submesh position is relative to the mesh position. None
MeshFace MeshFace(Vertex1, Vertex2, Vertex3 [, Vertex4]) Add or update a face to the current mesh previously created with CreateMesh. The specified vertices must exist. The first vertex index starts from 0. The created face is a triangle or a quad. MeshIndex can be used if the number of vertices is more than four. None
MeshID Result = MeshID(#Mesh) Returns the unique MeshID of the #Mesh. The use of this function is required especially by the CreateEntity function.
MeshIndex MeshIndex(Index) Add or update a single vertex in the mesh being created with CreateMesh or updated with UpdateMesh. It behaves like the command MeshFace, but with an arbitrary number of vertices. When using the mode #PB_Mesh_LineList or #PB_Mesh_LineStrip, there are only two vertices per line, so MeshIndex needs to be used in this case. None
MeshIndexCount Result = MeshIndexCount(#Mesh [, SubMesh]) Return the number of indexes in the mesh. Returns the number of indexes in the mesh, or zero if the mesh or the submesh doesn't exists.
MeshRadius Result = MeshRadius(#Mesh) Returns the radius of the smallest sphere which can contain the mesh. Returns the radius the mesh.
MeshVertex MeshVertex(x, y, z, u.f, v.f, Color [, NormalX, NormalY, NormalZ]) Add a vertex to the current mesh previously created with CreateMesh. Specific attributes to the newly created vertex can be added with MeshVertexTangent. To create a new face use MeshFace. None
MeshVertexColor MeshVertexColor(Color) Set color information to the current vertex previously added with MeshVertexPosition or MeshVertex. To have any effect, the material associated to the mesh has to be defined with SetMaterialColor(#Material, #PB_Material_AmbientColor, -1) and AmbientColor() set to a positive value. This function needs a vertex created before to apply color to it. None
MeshVertexCount Result = MeshVertexCount(#Mesh [, SubMesh]) Return the number of vertices of the mesh. Returns the vertices number of the mesh, or zero if the mesh or the submesh doesn't exist.
MeshVertexNormal MeshVertexNormal(x, y, z) Set normal information to the current vertex previously added with MeshVertexPosition or MeshVertex. The normal vector is used to calculate lightning on an object. To automatically computes the vector normal once the mesh is created, use NormalizeMesh. None
MeshVertexPosition MeshVertexPosition(x, y, z) Add a new vertex to the current mesh previously created with CreateMesh. To set specific attributes to the newly created vertex, use the following commands: MeshVertexNormal, MeshVertexTangent, MeshVertexColor and MeshVertexTextureCoordinate. If several attributes needs to be specified, MeshVertex can be used instead. To create a new face use MeshFace. None
MeshVertexTangent MeshVertexTangent(x, y, z) Set tangent information to the current vertex previously added with MeshVertexPosition or MeshVertex. The tangent vector is mainly used in shader scripts. To automatically compute the tangent vector once the mesh is created, use BuildMeshTangents. None
MeshVertexTextureCoordinate MeshVertexTextureCoordinate(u.f [, v.f [, w.f]]) Set UVW information to the current vertex previously added with MeshVertexPosition or MeshVertex. The UVW information is used to apply the texture on the mesh. None
NormalizeMesh NormalizeMesh(#Mesh [, SubMesh]) Normalize the mesh or the submesh. It will automatically compute the normal vector for all vertices of the specified mesh or submesh. Dynamic meshes are not supported (meshes created with the #PB_Mesh_Dynamic flag). None
SaveMesh SaveMesh(#Mesh, Filename$) Save the mesh. The saved mesh can be loaded back with the LoadMesh command. None
SetMeshData Result = SetMeshData(#Mesh, SubMesh, DataArray(), Flags, FirstIndex, LastIndex) Set internal mesh data, like vertices, face etc. Dynamic meshes are not supported (meshes created with the #PB_Mesh_Dynamic flag). Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure.
SetMeshMaterial SetMeshMaterial(#Mesh, MaterialID [, SubMesh]) Set the mesh default material. None
SubMeshCount Result = SubMeshCount(#Mesh) Returns the number of submeshes of the mesh. Returns the number of submeshes of the mesh.
TransformMesh TransformMesh(#Mesh, x, y, z, ScaleX, ScaleY, ScaleZ, RotateX, RotateY, RotateZ [, SubMesh]) Transform the Mesh according to the given parameters. Dynamic meshes are not supported for transform (meshes created with the #PB_Mesh_Dynamic flag). None
UpdateMesh UpdateMesh(#Mesh, SubMesh) Start the mesh update, to modify in real time its vertices and other values. The mesh has to be created with the #PB_Mesh_Dynamic flag. Once the mesh modifications are finished, FinishMesh needs to be called. The mesh can use the following commands to change their properties: MeshIndex, MeshFace, MeshVertexPosition, MeshVertexNormal, MeshVertexTangent, MeshVertexColor and MeshVertexTextureCoordinate. None
UpdateMeshBoundingBox UpdateMeshBoundingBox(#Mesh) Update the bounding box of the mesh. If a mesh has been manually modified, its bounding box has to be recalculated, especially if the mesh is used for collisions. The bounding box is the smallest box which can contain the whole mesh. None

NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
ExamineMouse Result = ExamineMouse() Updates the mouse state. This function should be used before MouseDeltaX, MouseDeltaY, MouseX, MouseY or MouseButton. Nonzero if the mouse state has been updated, zero otherwise.
InitMouse Result = InitMouse() Initializes the mouse environment for later use. You should call this function before any other functions in this library. If the result is zero, no mouse is available. Nonzero if the mouse functions are available, zero otherwise. This function tries to open DirectX (v3.0 with NT4.0 compatibility or v7.0 otherwise); if it fails then DirectX is either not available or is too old to be used.
MouseButton Result = MouseButton(Button) Returns zero if the specified button number is not pressed, otherwise the button is pressed. Any number of buttons can be pressed at the same time. ExamineMouse must be called before this function to update the actual button's state. Nonzero if the specified mouse button is pressed, zero otherwise.
MouseDeltaX Result = MouseDeltaX() Returns the mouse 'x' movement (in pixels) since the last call of this function. The mouse 'x' movement (in pixels) since the last call of this function. It can be either a negative or positive value, depending on whether or not the mouse has been moved to the left or the right since the last call. ExamineMouse should be called before this function to update the actual mouse position.
MouseDeltaY Result = MouseDeltaY() Returns the mouse 'y' movement (in pixels) since the last call of this function. The mouse 'y' movement (in pixels) since the last call of this function. It can be either a negative or positive value, depending on whether or not the mouse has been moved up or down since the last call. ExamineMouse should be called before this function to update the actual mouse position.
MouseLocate MouseLocate(x, y) Changes the absolute position (in pixels) of the mouse in the current screen. This is useful when using MouseX or MouseY. None
MouseWheel Result = MouseWheel() Returns the number of ticks the mouse wheel has moved since the last function call. ExamineMouse should be called before this function to update the mouse status. The number of ticks the mouse wheel has moved since the last function call. The value is positive if the wheel has moved forward and negative if the wheel has moved backwards.
MouseX Result = MouseX() Returns the actual mouse 'x' position (in pixels) on the current screen. The position can be changed easily with the MouseLocate function. ExamineMouse should be called before this function to update the actual mouse position. The actual mouse 'x' position (in pixels) on the current screen.
MouseY Result = MouseY() Returns the actual mouse 'y' position (in pixels) on the current screen. The position can be changed easily with the MouseLocate function. ExamineMouse should be called before this function to update the actual mouse position. The actual mouse 'y' position (in pixels) on the current screen.
ReleaseMouse ReleaseMouse(State) Locks or releases the mouse to allow its use under standard OS. This is typically called after checking the result of IsScreenActive function. None
Movie (16)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
FreeMovie FreeMovie(#Movie) Frees the specified movie and all its resources. None
InitMovie Result = InitMovie() Initialize the movie environment for later use. You must call this function before any other functions in this library. Returns nonzero if initialization was successful. If zero is returned then the movie library cannot be used.
IsMovie Result = IsMovie(#Movie) Tests if the given #Movie number is a valid and correctly initialized movie. Returns nonzero if #Movie is a valid movie and zero otherwise.
LoadMovie Result = LoadMovie(#Movie, Filename$) Loads the specified movie file and prepares it for playback. Returns nonzero if the movie was loaded correctly and zero if loading the movie failed (format not supported or file not found). If #PB_Any was used for the #Movie parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
MovieAudio MovieAudio(#Movie, Volume, Balance) Control the audio stream of a movie. Volume and balance can be modified during playback. Changes occur immediately. None
MovieHeight Height = MovieHeight(#Movie) Returns the height of the movie. Returns the height of the movie in pixels. If the result equals -1, then no video stream is found (or isn't compatible), however the audio stream can still be played.
MovieInfo Result = MovieInfo(#Movie, Flags) Returns additional information about the movie. Returns the value specified in the 'Flags' parameter.
MovieLength Length = MovieLength(#Movie) Returns the length of the movie. Returns the length of the movie in frames.
MovieSeek MovieSeek(#Movie, Frame.q) Change the movie's playback position to the given frame. None
MovieStatus Result.q = MovieStatus(#Movie) Get the playback status of the movie. Returns one of the following values: -1: Movie is paused. 0: Movie is stopped > 0: Movie is playing. The returned value is the current frame number displayed.
MovieWidth Width = MovieWidth(#Movie) Returns the width of the movie. Returns the width of the movie in pixels. If the result equals -1, then no video stream is found (or isn't compatible), however the audio stream can still be played.
PauseMovie PauseMovie(#Movie) Pauses the movie playback. Playback can be resumed using the ResumeMovie function. None
PlayMovie Result = PlayMovie(#Movie, WindowID) Start to play a movie previously loaded with LoadMovie on the specified window. Returns nonzero if the movie started playing correctly and zero if there was an error.
ResizeMovie ResizeMovie(#Movie, x, y, Width, Height) Resize and move the movie display area on the movie window. None
ResumeMovie ResumeMovie(#Movie) Continue to play the movie, after a PauseMovie call. None
StopMovie StopMovie(#Movie) Stop playing the movie. If the movie is played again, it will restart from the beginning. None

ModPlug supports a lot of music formats, which includes: Protracker (4 channels), FastTracker (up to 32 channels, 16-bit quality), Impulse Tracker, etc. Nonzero if the music module has been successfully loaded, zero otherwise.
FreeMusic FreeMusic(#Music) Stop and remove the specified music previously loaded with the LoadMusic or CatchMusic functions from memory. Once a music has been freed, it can't be played anymore. None
GetMusicPosition Position = GetMusicPosition(#Music) Returns the current pattern position of the playing music module. The current pattern position of the playing music module. The first pattern position is zero.
GetMusicRow Row = GetMusicRow(#Music) Returns the current row position in the pattern of the playing music module. The current row position of the playing music module. The first row position is zero.
IsMusic Result = IsMusic(#Music) Tests if the given music module is valid and correctly initialized. Nonzero if the music module is valid, zero otherwise.
LoadMusic Result = LoadMusic(#Music, Filename$) Loads the specified music module. PlayMusic can be used to start playing the music. ModPlug supports a lot of music formats, which includes: Protracker (4 channels), FastTracker (up to 32 channels, 16-bit quality), Impulse Tracker, etc. Nonzero if the music module has been successfully loaded, zero otherwise.
MusicVolume MusicVolume(#Music, Volume.f) Change the master volume of the specified music, in real-time. None
PlayMusic PlayMusic(#Music) Starts to play the specified music previously loaded with the LoadMusic or CatchMusic functions. None
SetMusicPosition SetMusicPosition(#Music, Position) Changes the current pattern position of the playing #Music to the new one. None
StopMusic StopMusic(#Music) Stop the #Music (if it was playing). None
Network (23)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
CloseNetworkConnection CloseNetworkConnection(Connection) Close the specified connection. None
CloseNetworkServer CloseNetworkServer(#Server) Shutdown the specified running server. All clients connected to this server are automatically removed. The port is freed and can be reused. None
ConnectionID Result = ConnectionID(Connection) Returns the unique system identifier of the connection. Returns the system identifier. This result is sometimes also known as 'Handle'. Look at the extra chapter Handles and Numbers for more information.
CreateNetworkServer Result = CreateNetworkServer(#Server, Port [, Flags [, BoundIP$]]) Create a new network server on the local computer using the specified port. To support TLS encryption, UseNetworkTLS needs to be called before this command and a TLS flag needs to be specified. Returns nonzero if the server was created successfully and zero if creation failed, for example, due to the port being already in use. If #PB_Any was used as the #Server parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
EventClient Connection = EventClient() This function returns the connection of the client that sent data and is only needed on the server side. Returns the connection of the client that caused the event.
EventServer Server = EventServer() This function returns the number of the server which has received data, allowing multiple servers to be managed on one computer. It is only needed on the server side. Returns the #Server number of the server causing the event.
ExamineIPAddresses Result = ExamineIPAddresses([Format]) Start examining the available IP addresses on the local computer. NextIPAddress is used to retrieve each IP. Returns nonzero if examining the addresses works and zero if it failed.
FreeIP FreeIP(IPAddress) Free an IPv6 address. This function only works with IPv6 addresses returned by MakeIPAddress, NextIPAddress and GetClientIP, and must not be used with IPv4 addresses. None
GetClientIP IP = GetClientIP(Client) This function returns the IP address of the client and should be called after EventClient(). If the connection is an IPv6 connection the returned address must be freed with FreeIP(). Returns the IP address of the client.
GetClientPort Port = GetClientPort(Client) Returns the client port and should be called after EventClient. Returns the port of the client.
HostName String$ = HostName() Returns the computer's hostname. Returns the host name.
IPAddressField Result = IPAddressField(IPAddress, Field [, Format]) Returns the given field value of the specified IP address. Returns the value of the specified field, in the range 0 to 255.
IPString String$ = IPString(IPAddress [, Format]) Returns the string representation in dotted form (ie: "127.0.0.1" for IPv4 or "::1" for IPv6) of the specified numerical IPAddress. Returns the IP address as a string.
MakeIPAddress Result = MakeIPAddress(Field0, Field1, Field2, Field3 [, Field4, Field5, Field6, Field7]) Returns the equivalent numeric value of the specified IP address. Returns the IP address.
NetworkClientEvent Result = NetworkClientEvent(Connection) Checks if an event happened on a network connection created with OpenNetworkConnection. Returns one of the following values: #PB_NetworkEvent_None : Nothing has happened #PB_NetworkEvent_Data : Raw data has been received (to be read with ReceiveNetworkData) #PB_NetworkEvent_Disconnect: The client has been disconnected (connection closed).
NetworkServerEvent Result = NetworkServerEvent([#Server]) Checks if an event happened on one of the open network servers. Returns one of the following values: #PB_NetworkEvent_None : Nothing has happened #PB_NetworkEvent_Connect : A new client has been connected to the server (not available with #PB_Network_UDP connections) #PB_NetworkEvent_Data : Raw data has been received (to be read with ReceiveNetworkData) #PB_NetworkEvent_Disconnect: A client has quit the server (disconnection). Its associated connection is automatically closed, CloseNetworkConnection must not be called for this client. (Not available with #PB_Network_UDP connections.)
NextIPAddress Result = NextIPAddress() Returns the next IP address of the local machine. ExamineIPAddresses must be called before this command. Returns the next IP address in numerical form. If the result is 0 then there are no more IP addresses to be examined. If ExamineIPAddresses is called with the #PB_Network_IPv6 format, the returned IP needs to freed with FreeIP after use.
OpenNetworkConnection Connection = OpenNetworkConnection(ServerName$, Port [, Flags [, TimeOut [, LocalIP$ [, LocalPort]]]]) Opens a network connection to the specified server. To support TLS encryption, UseNetworkTLS needs to be called before this command and a TLS flag needs to be specified. Returns the connection identifier for the opened connection if the connection was established correctly. If there was an error the result is zero.
ReceiveNetworkData Result = ReceiveNetworkData(Connection, *DataBuffer, DataBufferLength) Receives raw data from the specified client. This function can be used by both client and server applications and should be called only after having received a #PB_NetworkEvent_Data event. Returns the number of bytes received. If 'Result' is equal to DataBufferLength then more data is available to be read. If an error occurred on the connection (link broken, connection close by the server etc...) 'Result' will be -1.
SendNetworkData Result = SendNetworkData(Connection, *MemoryBuffer, Length) Sends raw data to the specified client. This function can be used by both client and server applications. Returns the number of bytes actually sent. If the number of bytes returned is not equal to the 'Length' parameter the receiving buffer of the user is probably full. If nothing could be sent then 'Result' will equal -1.
SendNetworkString Result = SendNetworkString(Connection, String$ [, Format]) Send a string to the specified client. This function can be used by both client and server applications. Returns the number of bytes sent.
ServerID Result = ServerID(#Server) Returns the unique system identifier of the server. Returns the system identifier. This result is sometimes also known as 'Handle'. Look at the extra chapter Handles and Numbers for more information.
UseNetworkTLS UseNetworkTLS([PrivateKey$, Certificate$ [, CaCertificate$]]) Enable and configure TLS support for network library. This command must be called before using CreateNetworkServer or OpenNetworkConnection with the TLS flags. None
Node (17)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
AttachNodeObject AttachNodeObject(#Node, ObjectID) Attaches an existing object to a node. None
CreateNode Result = CreateNode(#Node [, x, y, z]) Creates a new node at the specified position. Nonzero if the node was successfully created, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used for the #Node parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
DetachNodeObject DetachNodeObject(#Node, ObjectID) Detaches a previously attached object from a node. None
FreeNode FreeNode(#Node) Frees the specified node created with CreateNode before. All its associated memory is released and this object can't be used anymore. The attached objects are not freed automatically, and can be re-used. None
IsNode Result = IsNode(#Node) Tests if the given node is valid and correctly initialized. Nonzero if the node is valid, zero otherwise.
MoveNode MoveNode(#Node, x, y, z [, Mode]) Move the specified node. None
NodeFixedYawAxis NodeFixedYawAxis(#Node, Enable [, VectorX, VectorY, VectorZ]) Change the fixed yaw axis of the node. The default behaviour of a node is to yaw around its own Y axis. None
NodeID NodeID = NodeID(#Node) Returns the unique system identifier of the node. Returns the unique system identifier of the node.
NodeLookAt NodeLookAt(#Node, x, y, z [, DirectionX, DirectionY, DirectionZ]) The point (in world unit) that a node is facing. The position of the node is not changed. None
NodePitch Result = NodePitch(#Node [, Mode]) Get the pitch of the node. The current pitch value of the node.
NodeRoll Result = NodeRoll(#Node [, Mode]) Get the roll of the node. The current roll value of the node.
NodeX Result = NodeX(#Node [, Mode]) Returns the 'x' position of the node in the world. The 'x' position of the node in the world.
NodeY Result = NodeY(#Node [, Mode]) Returns the 'y' position of the node in the world. The 'y' position of the node in the world.
NodeYaw Result = NodeYaw(#Node [, Mode]) Get the yaw of the node. The current yaw value of the node.
NodeZ Result = NodeZ(#Node [, Mode]) Returns the 'z' position of the node in the world. The 'z' position of the node in the world.
RotateNode RotateNode(#Node, x, y, z [, Mode]) Rotates the node according to the specified x,y,z angle values. None
ScaleNode ScaleNode(#Node, x, y, z [, Mode]) Scales the node according to the specified x,y,z values. When using #PB_Relative mode, this is a factor based scale which means the node size will be multiplied with the given value to obtain the new size. None
NodeAnimation (23)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
AddNodeAnimationTime AddNodeAnimationTime(#NodeAnimation, Time) Add time to the specified #NodeAnimation. None
CreateNodeAnimation Result = CreateNodeAnimation(#NodeAnimation, NodeID, Length, Interpolation, RotationInterpolation) Creates a new node animation of the specified length. A node animation doesn't exist physically in the 3D world, it is an virtual track to move a node (and its attached object) easily around the world. Returns zero if the #NodeAnimation can't be created. If #PB_Any is used as '#NodeAnimation' parameter, the new node animation number is returned.
CreateNodeAnimationKeyFrame CreateNodeAnimationKeyFrame(#NodeAnimation, Time, x, y, z) Create a new keyframe for the #NodeAnimation. A keyframe is a point in the world at a specified time. When the node animation will be played, it will follow every keyframe and thus moving from points to points. The move will be interpolated to respect the time constraint. For example, if the first keyframe is set at time 0, the second at time 1000 and the third at time 3000, going from the first keyframe to the second will takes 1000 milliseconds, and going from the second keyframe to the third will takes 2000 milliseconds. The overall animation will take 3000 milliseconds. None
FreeNodeAnimation FreeNodeAnimation(#NodeAnimation) Frees a node animation and releases all its associated memory. This node animation must not be used (by using its number with the other functions in this library) after calling this function, unless you create it again. None
GetNodeAnimationKeyFramePitch Result = GetNodeAnimationKeyFramePitch(#NodeAnimation, KeyFrame) Returns the #NodeAnimation keyframe pitch. Returns the current node animation keyframe pitch, or zero if the keyframe doesn't exists.
GetNodeAnimationKeyFrameRoll Result = GetNodeAnimationKeyFrameRoll(#NodeAnimation, KeyFrame) Returns the #NodeAnimation keyframe roll. Returns the current node animation keyframe roll, or zero if the keyframe doesn't exists.
GetNodeAnimationKeyFrameTime Result = GetNodeAnimationKeyFrameTime(#NodeAnimation, KeyFrame) Returns the #NodeAnimation keyframe time. Returns the node animation keyframe time (in milliseconds), or zero if the keyframe doesn't exists.
GetNodeAnimationKeyFrameX Result = GetNodeAnimationKeyFrameX(#NodeAnimation, KeyFrame) Returns the #NodeAnimation keyframe 'x' position. Returns the node animation keyframe 'x' position in the world, or zero if the keyframe doesn't exists.
GetNodeAnimationKeyFrameY Result = GetNodeAnimationKeyFrameY(#NodeAnimation, KeyFrame) Returns the #NodeAnimation keyframe 'y' position. Returns the node animation keyframe 'y' position in the world, or zero if the keyframe doesn't exists.
GetNodeAnimationKeyFrameYaw Result = GetNodeAnimationKeyFrameYaw(#NodeAnimation, KeyFrame) Returns the #NodeAnimation keyframe yaw. Returns the current node animation keyframe yaw, or zero if the keyframe doesn't exists.
GetNodeAnimationKeyFrameZ Result = GetNodeAnimationKeyFrameZ(#NodeAnimation, KeyFrame) Returns the #NodeAnimation keyframe 'z' position. Returns the node animation keyframe 'z' position in the world, or zero if the keyframe doesn't exists.
GetNodeAnimationLength Result = GetNodeAnimationLength(#NodeAnimation) Returns the #NodeAnimation length. The node animation length (in milliseconds).
GetNodeAnimationTime Result = GetNodeAnimationTime(#NodeAnimation) Returns the current #NodeAnimation time. The current node animation time (in milliseconds) or 0 if the animation isn't running.
GetNodeAnimationWeight Result = GetNodeAnimationWeight(#NodeAnimation) Returns the #NodeAnimation weight. The weight is useful when playing several animations at once. For example to do a smooth transition from one animation to another, it is possible to reduce progressively the weight of the first animation and increase the weight of the second animation. The current node animation weight (value between 0.0 and 1.0). If the weight is 0, then the animation has no effect. If the weight is 1, then animation is fully playing.
NodeAnimationStatus Result = NodeAnimationStatus(#NodeAnimation) Return the specified #NodeAnimation status. The return value can be one of the following constants: #PB_NodeAnimation_Stopped: The animation is stopped (or has ended). #PB_NodeAnimation_Started: The animation is running.
SetNodeAnimationKeyFramePosition SetNodeAnimationKeyFramePosition(#NodeAnimation, KeyFrame, x, y, z) Changes the keyframe position for the #NodeAnimation. None
SetNodeAnimationKeyFrameRotation SetNodeAnimationKeyFrameRotation(#NodeAnimation, KeyFrame, x, y, z [, w, Mode]) Changes the keyframe rotation for the #NodeAnimation. None
SetNodeAnimationKeyFrameScale SetNodeAnimationKeyFrameScale(#NodeAnimation, KeyFrame, x, y, z) Changes the keyframe scale factor for the #NodeAnimation. The scale factor will be applied to the node associated to the animation. None
SetNodeAnimationLength SetNodeAnimationLength(#NodeAnimation, Length) Change the #NodeAnimation length.
SetNodeAnimationTime SetNodeAnimationTime(#NodeAnimation, Time) Changes the current #NodeAnimation time. This is an absolute time position. To change the time relative to the current time, use AddNodeAnimationTime. None
SetNodeAnimationWeight SetNodeAnimationWeight(#NodeAnimation, Weight) Changes the #NodeAnimation weight. The weight is useful when playing several animations at once. For example to do a smooth transition from one animation to another, it is possible to reduce progressively the weight of the first animation and increase the weight of the second animation. None
StartNodeAnimation StartNodeAnimation(#NodeAnimation [, Flags]) Start the specified #NodeAnimation. The animation is always started from the beginning. None
StopNodeAnimation StopNodeAnimation(#NodeAnimation) Stop the specified #NodeAnimation. None
OnError (16)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
ErrorAddress Result = ErrorAddress() Returns the memory address of the assembly instruction that caused the current error. This command only returns a meaningful value if there was an error handled by OnErrorCall or OnErrorGoto. The memory address of the assembly instruction that caused the current error.
ErrorCode Result = ErrorCode() Returns the error code of the currently handled error. This command only returns a meaningful value if there was an error handled by OnErrorCall or OnErrorGoto. One of the following values: #PB_OnError_InvalidMemory : Read or write operation on an invalid location #PB_OnError_Floatingpoint : Floating-point error #PB_OnError_Breakpoint : Debugger breakpoint reached (non-PureBasic breakpoints) #PB_OnError_IllegalInstruction : Attempt to execute an illegal instruction #PB_OnError_PriviledgedInstruction: Attempt to execute a privileged (system-) instruction #PB_OnError_DivideByZero : Division by zero (Windows only) Linux and Mac OSX report #PB_OnError_Floatingpoint for division by zero errors. In addition, every OS may have more possible error values. On Windows, custom errors can be raised with the RaiseError command.
ErrorFile Result$ = ErrorFile() Returns the filename of the source code or includefile where the current error occurred. This command only returns a meaningful value if there was an error handled by OnErrorCall or OnErrorGoto. The tracking of line numbers needs to be enabled on compilation for this command to return the actual file name. To enable this feature, enable the "Enable OnError lines support" checkbox in the compiler options or specify the /LINENUMBERING (Windows) or --linenumbering (Linux, Mac OSX) command-line switch when compiling from the command-line. The filename of the error, or "OnError line support disabled" if the OnError lines support is disabled. (A simple way to check if the OnError lines support is enabled is to check if the result of ErrorLine is not -1.)
ErrorLine Result = ErrorLine() Returns the line number in the source code where the current error occurred. This command only returns a meaningful value if there was an error handled by OnErrorCall or OnErrorGoto. The tracking of line numbers needs to be enabled on compilation for this command to return the actual line number. To enable this feature, enable the "Enable OnError lines support" checkbox in the compiler options or specify the /LINENUMBERING (Windows) or --linenumbering (Linux, Mac OSX) command-line switch when compiling from the command-line. The line number of the error, or -1 if the OnError lines support is disabled.
ErrorMessage Result$ = ErrorMessage([ErrorCode]) Returns an error-message for the given error code in english. The message for the currently handled error. If the 'ErrorCode' parameter is set, an english error-message for this specific error will be returned.
ErrorRegister Result = ErrorRegister(Register) Returns the content of the specified CPU register at the time of the error. This command only returns a meaningful value if there was an error handled by OnErrorCall or OnErrorGoto. The content of the specified CPU register at the time of the error.
ErrorTargetAddress Result = ErrorTargetAddress() After an error with the code #PB_OnError_InvalidMemory, this command returns the memory address which was read/written when the error occurred. This command has no meaning for other error codes. The memory address which was read/written when the error occurred, after a #PB_OnError_InvalidMemory error.
ExamineAssembly Result = ExamineAssembly(*Address [, *EndAddress]) Initializes the disassembling at the given address or address range. Important: The disassembly commands use the Udis86 disassembler library to decode the instructions. This library is released under the BSD license which can be viewed here. If ExamineAssembly and the related commands are used in a program that is to be made public, the above linked licence text must be included with the software. Nonzero if disassembling is possible, zero otherwise.
InstructionAddress Result = InstructionAddress() Returns the address of the instruction that was disassembled by a call to NextInstruction. The address of the instruction that was disassembled by a call to NextInstruction.
InstructionString Result$ = InstructionString() Returns a string representation of the instruction that was disassembled by a call to NextInstruction. A string representation of the instruction that was disassembled by a call to NextInstruction.
NextInstruction Result = NextInstruction() Disassembles the next instruction after a call to ExamineAssembly. Information about the disassembled instruction can be read with InstructionString and InstructionAddress. Nonzero if the instruction was successfully disassembled, zero otherwise ('*EndAddress' that was specified in ExamineAssembly was reached).
OnErrorCall OnErrorCall(@ErrorHandler()) Changes the action taken if an error occurs to call the specified handler procedure. The handler can display information about the error to the user using the commands of this library and do any needed cleanup to shutdown the application. The program will end as soon as the handler returns. None
OnErrorDefault OnErrorDefault() Changes the action taken when an error occurs back to the system default. This usually means displaying an error dialog and exiting the program, but it may also mean to just ignore certain errors. To exit the program on every error, use OnErrorExit. None
OnErrorExit OnErrorExit() Changes the action taken if an error occurs to directly exit the program, even if the default action on the system is not to exit the program on this kind of error. The system may display an error dialog or print an error-message on the console on exit. None
OnErrorGoto OnErrorGoto(?LabelAddress) Changes the action taken when an error occurs to jump to the specified label address and continue program execution there. After the jump to the label, the functions of this library can be used to get further information about the error. None
RaiseError RaiseError(ErrorNumber) Artificially create the given error. The appropriate error action will be taken (call of the error handler or program termination by the system if no handler is set). The ErrorNumber will be available inside the error handler with the ErrorCode command. None
Packer (24)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
AddPackDirectory Result = AddPackDirectory(#Pack, DirectoryName$) Add a new empty directory to the specified pack previously created with CreatePack. Nonzero if the empty directory has been successfully added to the packfile.
AddPackFile Result = AddPackFile(#Pack, Filename$, PackedFilename$) Add and compress the file to the specified pack previously created with CreatePack. Adding a large file can take a long time. PackerCallback can be used to monitor or abort the compression. Nonzero if the file has been successfully added to the packfile. If the file can't be compressed, it will be stored as is in the packfile.
AddPackMemory Result = AddPackMemory(#Pack, *Buffer, Size, PackedFilename$) Add and compress the memory buffer to the specified pack previously created with CreatePack. PackerCallback can be used to monitor or abort the compression. Nonzero if the buffer has been successfully added to the packfile. If the memory buffer can't be compressed, it will be stored as is in the packfile.
CatchPack Result = CatchPack(#Pack, *MemoryAddress, Size [, Plugin]) Open a previously existing pack file from memory. Before opening a pack file, at least one packer has to be registered with one of the following command: UseZipPacker, UseLzmaPacker, UseTarPacker, UseBriefLZPacker. Once opened, the pack content can be listed with ExaminePack. Returns nonzero if the pack file has been successfully opened, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used as the #Pack parameter then the generated pack number is returned.
ClosePack ClosePack(#Pack) Close the specified pack file. None
CompressMemory Result = CompressMemory(*Buffer, Size, *Output, OutputSize [, Plugin [, Level]]) Compress the buffer content into the output buffer. The output buffer length needs to be at least as long as the buffer to compress. PackerCallback can be used to monitor or abort the compression. Return the compressed size if the buffer has been successfully compressed, zero otherwise. If the buffer data can't be compressed (already compressed data generally don't compress anymore), it will return zero.
CreatePack Result = CreatePack(#Pack, Filename$ [, Plugin [, Level]]) Create a new empty pack file. If the file already exists, it will be replaced with a new empty file. Before creating a pack file, at least one packer has to be registered with one of the following command: UseZipPacker, UseBriefLZPacker. Returns nonzero if the pack file has been successfully created, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used as the #Pack parameter then the generated pack number is returned.
ExaminePack Result = ExaminePack(#Pack) Start to examine the pack content. NextPackEntry has to be called to list the entries found in the pack file. The pack has to be previously opened with OpenPack or CatchPack. Packs being created with CreatePack can not be examined. Nonzero if the pack can be examined, zero otherwise.
IsPack Result = IsPack(#Pack) Tests if the given pack number is a valid and correctly initialized pack. Returns nonzero if #Pack is a valid pack and zero if not.
NextPackEntry Result = NextPackEntry(#Pack) Go to the next entry in the pack file. ExaminePack has to be called before calling this command. To get more information about the current entry, use PackEntrySize, PackEntryType and PackEntryName. To uncompress the current entry, use UncompressPackMemory or UncompressPackFile. Nonzero if the pack contain another entry, zero otherwise.
OpenPack Result = OpenPack(#Pack, Filename$ [, Plugin]) Open a previously existing pack file. Before opening a pack file, at least one packer has to be registered with one of the following command: UseZipPacker, UseLzmaPacker, UseTarPacker, UseBriefLZPacker. Once opened, the pack content can be listed with ExaminePack. Returns nonzero if the pack file has been successfully opened, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used as the #Pack parameter then the generated pack number is returned.
PackEntryDate Result.q = PackEntryDate(#Pack [, DateType]) Returns the file date of the current pack entry, set with NextPackEntry. Returns the file date or -1 if no date is available.
PackEntryName Result$ = PackEntryName(#Pack) Returns the name of the current entry, set with NextPackEntry. Returns the name of the current entry.
PackEntrySize Result = PackEntrySize(#Pack [, Mode]) Returns the size of the current entry, set with NextPackEntry. Returns the size of the current entry.
PackEntryType Result = PackEntryType(#Pack) Returns the type of the current entry, set with NextPackEntry. Returns one of the following values: #PB_Packer_File : the current entry is a file #PB_Packer_Directory: the current entry is a directory
PackerCallback Result = PackerCallback(@Callback()) Set a callback to monitor or abort the compression for CompressMemory, AddPackFile and AddPackMemory. The callback will be called at regular intervalls during the compression process. None
UncompressMemory Result = UncompressMemory(*Buffer, Size, *Output, OutputSize [, Plugin]) Uncompress the buffer content into the output buffer. The output buffer length needs to be at least as long as the buffer to uncompress. Return the uncompressed size if the buffer has been successfully uncompressed, -1 otherwise.
UncompressPackFile Result = UncompressPackFile(#Pack, Filename$ [, PackedFilename$]) Uncompress into the specified filename from the current pack entry being examined with ExaminePack and NextPackEntry. If the filename already exists, it will erased and replaced with the new uncompressed data. Return the uncompressed size if the pack entry has been successfully uncompressed into the filename, -1 otherwise.
UncompressPackMemory Result = UncompressPackMemory(#Pack, *Buffer, Size [, PackedFilename$]) Uncompress into the memory buffer from the current pack entry being examined with ExaminePack and NextPackEntry. Return the uncompressed size if the pack entry has been successfully uncompressed into the memory buffer, -1 otherwise.
UseBriefLZPacker UseBriefLZPacker() Enable BriefLZ compress, uncompress and archive support to the packer library. The created archives are a custom format created for PureBasic. BriefLZ compression is very fast and the packer is very small, it could be the right choice for program which needs a small executable size. Uncompress is also very fast, but compress ratio is not as good as Zip or Lzma. None
UseJcalg1Packer UseJcalg1Packer() Enable Jcalg1 uncompress support to the packer library. This is an old algorithm which was used in previous version of PureBasic, so it is still available to allow to support old compressed files. Compression and archive support is no more available. This packer is only available on Windows x86 (32-bit). This packer is deprecated and no more supported. None
UseLzmaPacker UseLzmaPacker() Enable Lzma compress, uncompress and 7z archive support to the packer library. Lzma compression is considered as one of the best available multipurpose compression algorithm. It provides very good compress ratio and fast uncompress. Compressing can be slow. For more information: Wikipedia - Lzma. None
UseTarPacker UseTarPacker() Enable Tar compress, uncompress and Tar archive support to the packer library. Bzip2 and Gzip compression are both supported. Compressing and uncompressing Tar archives are usually fast. None
UseZipPacker UseZipPacker() Enable Zip compress, uncompress and archive support to the packer library. The created pack will be compatible with other Zip archives in 2.0 format. The created archive size can be up to 2GB. For more information: Wikipedia - Zip. None
Particle (25)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
CreateParticleEmitter Result = CreateParticleEmitter(#ParticleEmitter, Width, Height, Depth, Type, [, x.f, y.f, z.f]) Creates a new empty particle emitter of the given size. Nonzero if the particle emitter has been successfully created, zero otherwise. CreatePreferences Result = CreatePreferences(Filename$ [, Flags]) Creates a new empty preference file. If the file already exists, the file is erased. Nonzero if the file has been successfully created, zero otherwise.
ExaminePreferenceGroups Result = ExaminePreferenceGroups() Starts the enumeration of all the groups found in the current preference file. NextPreferenceGroup can be used to list all the group found. Nonzero if the enumeration has been successfully started, zero otherwise.
ExaminePreferenceKeys Result = ExaminePreferenceKeys() Starts the enumeration of all the keys found in the current group of the preference file. Nonzero if the enumeration has been successfully started, zero otherwise.
FlushPreferenceBuffers Result = FlushPreferenceBuffers() Ensures that all preferences changes are written to disk. Nonzero if the preferences has been successfully written the disk. If an error occurred (ie: disk full, disk error), it will return zero.
NextPreferenceGroup Result = NextPreferenceGroup() Retrieves information about the next group found in the enumeration started with ExaminePreferenceGroups. To get the name of the group, use PreferenceGroupName. Nonzero if more groups are available in the current enumeration, zero otherwise.
NextPreferenceKey Result = NextPreferenceKey() Retrieves information about the next key found in the enumeration started with ExaminePreferenceKeys. ReadPreferenceDouble Result.d = ReadPreferenceDouble(Key$, DefaultValue) Try to read the specified associated 'Key$' value. The value associated to the specified key, as a double number. if the key isn't found the default value is returned.

NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
DefaultPrinter Result = DefaultPrinter() Selects the default printer as the current printer for print operation. This function has to be called before all other printer functions. Once DefaultPrinter has been successfully called, StartPrinting is used to actually start printing. Nonzero if a default printer is available, zero otherwise.
NewPrinterPage NewPrinterPage() Creates a new empty page. The previous page is sent to the printer and can't be modified anymore. It has to be called inside a StartDrawing/StopDrawing block. None
PrinterOutput OutputID = PrinterOutput() Returns the OutputID of the current printer to be used with the StartDrawing function. Drawing on the printer will be performed using pixel based drawing operations. The OutputID of the current printer to be used with the StartDrawing function.
PrinterPageHeight Result = PrinterPageHeight() Returns the height of the drawing area. The height of the drawing area, in pixels. The number changes with the DPI of the printer. This means than a document printed at 75 DPI will have a drawing area 4 times smaller than a document printed at 150 DPI. This value refers to the client area, the one you can write on. It doesn't count the hardware printer margins, but doesn't add any 'soft' margins.
PrinterPageWidth Result = PrinterPageWidth() Return the width of the drawing area. The width of the drawing area, in pixels. The number changes with the DPI of the printer. This means than a document printed at 75 DPI will have a drawing area 4 times smaller than a document printed at 150 DPI. This value refers to the client area, the one you can write on. It doesn't count the hardware printer margins, but doesn't add any 'soft' margins.
PrinterVectorOutput VectorOutputID = PrinterVectorOutput([Unit]) Returns the OutputID of the current printer to be used with the StartVectorDrawing function. The OutputID of the current printer to be used with the StartVectorDrawing function.
PrintRequester Result = PrintRequester() Open a regular print requester, to choose the printer and do some adjustments. This function must be called before all other printer functions. Once PrintRequester has been successfully called, StartPrinting is used to actually start printing. Nonzero if the user successfully selected a printer, zero otherwise.
StartPrinting Result = StartPrinting(JobName$) Initializes the printer and starts the print operation. Nonzero if the print operation has been started successfully, zero otherwise.
StopPrinting StopPrinting() Stop all the print operations and send the data to the printer. None

NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
AvailableProgramOutput Result = AvailableProgramOutput(Program) Returns the number of bytes available to be read from the programs output. The number of bytes available to be read from the programs output.
CloseProgram CloseProgram(Program) Closes the connection with the given program (which was started with RunProgram) and frees all related data. None
CountProgramParameters Result = CountProgramParameters() Returns the number of parameters specified on the command line (or via RunProgram). The number of parameters specified on the command line (or via RunProgram).
EnvironmentVariableName Result$ = EnvironmentVariableName() Returns the name of the current environment variable currently examined with ExamineEnvironmentVariables and NextEnvironmentVariable. EnvironmentVariableValue may be used to return its value. The name of the current environment variable currently examined with ExamineEnvironmentVariables and NextEnvironmentVariable.
EnvironmentVariableValue Result$ = EnvironmentVariableValue() Returns the value of the current environment variable currently examined with ExamineEnvironmentVariables and NextEnvironmentVariable. EnvironmentVariableName may be used to return its name. The value of the current environment variable currently examined with ExamineEnvironmentVariables and NextEnvironmentVariable.
ExamineEnvironmentVariables Result = ExamineEnvironmentVariables() Starts to examine the environment block of the program. NextEnvironmentVariable, EnvironmentVariableName and EnvironmentVariableValue may be used to read the individual environment variables. Nonzero if the environment block can be read, zero otherwise.
GetEnvironmentVariable Result$ = GetEnvironmentVariable(Name$) Returns the content of the specified environment variable from the programs environment block. The environment variable value, or an empty string if the environment variable does not exist.
IsProgram Result = IsProgram(Program) Tests if the given program is a program that is executed by the RunProgram function. Nonzero if the program is executed by the RunProgram function, zero otherwise.
KillProgram KillProgram(Program) Immediately terminates the given program (which was previously started with RunProgram). None
NextEnvironmentVariable Result = NextEnvironmentVariable() This function must be called after ExamineEnvironmentVariables. It will go step-by-step through the environment variables of the program. Nonzero if there is still more variables to read, zero otherwise.
ProgramExitCode Result = ProgramExitCode(Program) Returns the exitcode that was returned when the given program ended. The exitcode that was returned when the specified program ended.
ProgramFilename Result$ = ProgramFilename() Returns the full path and filename of this program and may be used to find where the program is installed or the executable name. GetPathPart or GetFilePart may be used to get the path or filename of the program from the return string. The full path and filename of this program. If used inside a DLL, this function returns the path and filename of the DLL, not the main program that loaded it.
ProgramID Result = ProgramID(Program) Returns the unique system identifier for the given program. This is the so called "Process ID" or "PID". The unique system identifier for the given program. If the identifier cannot be returned, -1 will be returned. This will happen if RunProgram is used to open a file in another program, like RunProgram("Source.pb"). Note: the value returned here is not a handle (unlike with most other ...ID() functions). Rather, it is the Process ID which may be viewed within the Taskmanager. To get a process handle, use the OpenProcess_() API. Note: The returned value may be false if the process is launched by a wrapper as is the case with Windows 10 and UWP (Universal Windows Platform) applications launched by ApplicationFrameHost.exe (AFH).
ProgramParameter Result$ = ProgramParameter([Index]) Gets the next parameter string that was passed to the executable when it was launched. The next parameter value, or an empty string if no more parameters are found. If index is specified it will return the specified parameter value.
ProgramRunning Result = ProgramRunning(Program) Tests if the specified program is still running. Nonzero as long as the program has not yet ended, zero otherwise. If the program has been run with #PB_Program_Read flag, it will return nonzero as long there is something to read, even if the program is already ended.
ReadProgramData Result = ReadProgramData(Program, *Buffer, Size) Reads data from the given programs output (stdout) and puts it in the specified buffer. This function waits until there is data available to read from the program. To prevent this wait, AvailableProgramOutput may be used first to check if there is something to read. The number of bytes actually read.
ReadProgramError Result$ = ReadProgramError(Program [, Flags]) Reads a line from the specified programs error output (stderr). Unlike ReadProgramData, this function doesn't halt the program flow if no error output is available. The error string, or an empty string if there is no error output.
ReadProgramString Result$ = ReadProgramString(Program [, Flags]) Reads a line from the output (stdout) of the given program. This function waits until there is data available to read from the program. To prevent this wait, AvailableProgramOutput may be used first to check if there is something to read. This function also waits until a full line of output is available. If not line-based or raw output is to be read, ReadProgramData may be used. A string created from program output.
RemoveEnvironmentVariable RemoveEnvironmentVariable(Name$) Removes the given environment variable from the programs environment block. None
RunProgram Result = RunProgram(Filename$ [, Parameter$, WorkingDirectory$ [, Flags [, SenderProgram]]]) Launches an external program. Nonzero if the program has been successfully launched, zero otherwise. If #PB_Program_Open was included in the Flags, the return-value is a number that identifies the program. It may be used in calls to get information about the program such as ReadProgramString or ProgramExitCode or other functions mentioned above.
SetEnvironmentVariable SetEnvironmentVariable(Name$, Value$) Creates an environment variable in the environment block of this program with given name and value. If a variable with this name already existed, its content will be changed to the new value. The environment block of the program is passed on to other programs executed with RunProgram, so this method may be used to pass on information to a program executed by this program. (The executed program may use GetEnvironmentVariable to read the variables.) None
WaitProgram Result = WaitProgram(Program [, Timeout]) Halts the execution of the code until the specified program has ended or the optional timeout is reached. Nonzero if the program has ended, zero if the timeout was reached.
WriteProgramData Result = WriteProgramData(Program, *Buffer, Size) Writes the data from the buffer to the specified programs input (stdin). The number of bytes actually written.
WriteProgramString WriteProgramString(Program, String$ [, Flags]) Writes the given string to the specified programs input (stdin). None
WriteProgramStringN WriteProgramStringN(Program, String$ [, Flags]) Writes the given string to the specified programs input (stdin) with an extra newline character. None
Reference (71)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
Bool Compiler Functions Result = Bool(<boolean expression>) Bool can be used to evaluate a boolean expression outside of regular conditional operator like If, While, Until etc. Returns #True if the boolean expression is true, #False otherwise.
Break Break : Continue Break [Level] Break provides the ability to exit during any iteration, for the following loops: Repeat, For, ForEach and While. The optional 'level' parameter specifies the number of loops to exit from, given several nested loops. If no parameter is given, Break exits from the current loop.
CallDebugger Debugger keywords in PureBasic CallDebugger This invokes the "debugger" and freezes the program immediately.
ClearStructure Compiler Functions ClearStructure(*Pointer, Structure) ClearStructure clears a structured memory area. This is useful when the structure contains strings, array, list or map which have been allocated internally by PureBasic. This function is for advanced users and should be used with care. None
CompareStructure Compiler Functions Result = CompareStructure(*Pointer1, *Pointer2, Structure [, Flags]) CompareStructure compares the memory of two structures for equality. The comparison is recursively applied also to child elements such as arrays, lists, and maps. Returns nonzero if the structures are the same or zero if they differ.
CompilerError Compiler Directives CompilerError <string constant>
CompilerWarning <string constant>		 Generates an error or a warning, as if it was a syntax error and display the associated message. It can be useful when doing specialized routines, or to inform a source code is not available on an particular OS. Note: CompilerWarning displays warnings, but the compilation process continues, while the command CompilerError stops the compilation process.
CompilerIf Compiler Directives CompilerIf <constant expression>
...
[CompilerElseIf]
...
[CompilerElse]
...
CompilerEndIf		 If the <constant expression> result is true, the code inside the CompilerIf will be compiled, else it will be totally ignored. It's useful when building multi-OSes programs to customize some programs part by using OS specific functions. The And and Or Keywords can be used in <constant expression> to combine multiple conditions.
CompilerSelect Compiler Directives CompilerSelect <numeric constant>
CompilerCase <numeric constant>
...
[CompilerDefault]
...
CompilerEndSelect		 Works like a regular Select : EndSelect except that only one numeric value is allowed per case. It will tell the compiler which code should be compiled. It's useful when building multi-OSes programs to customize some programs part by using OS specific functions.
Continue Break : Continue Continue Continue provides the ability to skip straight to the end of the current iteration (bypassing any code in between) in the following loops: Repeat, For, ForEach, and While.
CopyStructure Compiler Functions CopyStructure(*Source, *Destination, Structure) CopyStructure copy the memory of a structured memory area to another. This is useful when dealing with dynamic allocations, through pointers. Every fields will be duplicated, even array, list, and map. The destination structure will be automatically cleared before doing the copy, it's not needed to call ClearStructure before CopyStructure. Warning: the destination should be a valid structure memory area, or a cleared memory area. If the memory area is not cleared, it could crash, as random values will be used by the clear routine. There is no internal check to ensures that the structure match the two memory area. This function is for advanced users and should be used with care. None
Data Data.TypeName Defines data. The type can only be a native basic type (integer, long, word, byte, ascii, unicode, float, double, quad, character, string). Any number of data can be put on the same line, each one delimited with a comma ','. A literal string cannot exceed 8192 characters.
DataSection Data DataSection Start a data section.
Debug Debugger keywords in PureBasic Debug <expression> [, DebugLevel] Display the DebugOutput window and the result inside it. The expression can be any valid PureBasic expression, from numeric to string. An important point is the Debug command and its associated expression is totally ignored (not compiled) when the debugger is deactivated. Note: This is also true, if you're using complete command lines after Debug (e.g. Debug LoadImage(1,"test.bmp")). They will not be compiled with disabled debugger! This means this command can be used to trace easily in the program without having to comment all the debug commands when creating the final executable. The 'DebugLevel' is the level of priority of the debug message. All normal debug message (without specifying a debug level) are automatically displayed. When a level is specified then the message will be only displayed if the current DebugLevel (set with the following DebugLevel command) is equals or above this number. This allows hierarchical debug mode, by displaying more and more precise information in function of the used DebugLevel.
DebugLevel Debugger keywords in PureBasic DebugLevel <constant expression> Set the current debug level for the 'Debug' message. Note: The debug level is set at compile time, which means you have to put the DebugLevel command before any other Debug commands to be sure it affects them all.
Declare Procedures Declare[.<type>] name(<parameter1[.<type>]> [, <parameter2[.<type>] [= DefaultValue]>, ...]) Sometimes a procedure need to call another procedure which isn't declared before its definition. This is annoying because the compiler will complain 'Procedure <name> not found'. Declare can help in this particular case by declaring only the header of the procedure. Nevertheless, the Declare and real Procedure declaration must be identical (including the correct type and optional parameters, if any). For advanced programmers DeclareC is available and will declare the procedure using 'CDecl' instead of 'StandardCall' calling convention.
Define Define.<type> [<variable> [= <expression>], <variable> [= <expression>], ...] Assign the same data type to a series of variables. Without this keyword, variables are created with the default type of PureBasic which is the type INTEGER. As a reminder, the type INTEGER is: 4 bytes (with a 32-bit compiler) ranging from -2147483648 to + 2147483647 8 bytes (with a 64-bit compiler) ranging from -9223372036854775808 to +9223372036854775807 Define is very flexible because it also allows you to assign a different type to a particular variable within a series. Define can also be used with arrays, the lists and the maps.
Define Define <variable>.<type> [= <expression>] [, <variable>.<type> [= <expression>], ...] Alternative possibility for the variable declaration using Define.
Defined Compiler Functions Result = Defined(Name, Type) Defined checks if a particular object of a code source like structure, interface, variables etc. is already defined or not. Returns nonzero if the object is defined, zero otherwise.
Dim Dim name.<type>(<expression>, [<expression>], ...) Dim is used to create new arrays (the initial value of each element will be zero). An array in PureBasic can be of any types, including structured, and user defined types. Once an array is defined it can be resized with ReDim. Arrays are dynamically allocated which means a variable or an expression can be used to size them. To view all commands used to manage arrays, see the Array library. When you define a new array, please note that it will have one more element than you used as parameter, because the numbering of the elements in PureBasic (like in other BASIC's) starts at element 0. For example when you define Dim(10) the array will have 11 elements, elements 0 to 10. This behavior is different for static arrays in structures. Static arrays use brackets "[]", for example ArrayStatic[2] has only 2 elements from 0 to 1 and library functions Array don't work with them. The new arrays are always locals, which means Global or Shared commands have to be used if an array declared in the main source need to be used in procedures. It is also possible to pass an array as parameter to a procedure - by using the keyword Array. It will be passed "by reference" (which means, that the array will not be copied, instead the functions in the procedure will manipulate the original array). To delete the content of an array and release its used memory during program flow, call FreeArray. If Dim is used on an existing array, it will reset its contents to zero. For fast swapping of array contents the Swap keyword is available. Note: Array bound checking is only done when the runtime Debugger is enabled.
DisableDebugger Debugger keywords in PureBasic DisableDebugger This will disable the debugger checks on the source code which follow this command. It doesn't not fully turn off the debugger, so performance checks should not be done using DisableDebugger command, but by disabling the debugger before compiling the program.
DisablePureLibrary Compiler Directives DisablePureLibrary <LibraryName> Disables the specified PureLibrary. All its associated commands won't be available when compiling this program. This is especially useful when creating a PureLibrary.
EnableASM Compiler Directives EnableASM
DisableASM		 Enables or disables the inline assembler. When enabled, all the assembler keywords are available directly in the source code, see the inline assembler section for more information.
EnableDebugger Debugger keywords in PureBasic EnableDebugger This will enable the debugger checks on the source code which follow this command (if the debugger was previously disabled with DisableDebugger). Note: EnableDebugger doesn't have an effect, if the debugger is completely disabled in the IDE (look at Compiler settings).
EnableExplicit Compiler Directives EnableExplicit
DisableExplicit		 Enables or disables the explicit mode. When enabled, all the variables which are not explicitly declared with Define, Global, Protected or Static are not accepted and the compiler will raise an error. It can help to catch typo bugs.
End Others Commands End [ExitCode] Ends the program execution correctly. The 'ExitCode' optional parameter can be specified if the program need to returns an error code (widely used in console programs). The 'ExitCode' can be further used e.g. with the ProgramExitCode command.
EndDataSection Data EndDataSection End a data section.
Enumerations Enumeration [name] [<constant> [Step <constant>]]
#Constant1
#Constant2 [= <constant>]
#Constant3
...
EndEnumeration
Or
EnumerationBinary [name] [<constant>]
#Constant1
#Constant2 [= <constant>]
#Constant3
...
EndEnumeration		 Enumerations are very handy to declare a sequence of constants quickly without using fixed numbers.
