Sound3D (10)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
FreeSound3D FreeSound3D(#Sound3D) Stop and remove a 3D sound previously loaded with LoadSound3D from memory. Once a sound has been freed, it can't be played anymore. None
IsSound3D Result = IsSound3D(#Sound3D) Tests if the given sound is valid and correctly initialized. Nonzero if the sound is valid, zero otherwise.
LoadSound3D Result = LoadSound3D(#Sound3D, Filename$ [, Flags]) Loads a mono WAV or OGG sound file. The sound has to be mono, as stereo sounds don't allow spacial positioning. Nonzero if the sound has been successfully loaded, zero otherwise.
PlaySound3D PlaySound3D(#Sound3D [, Flags]) Starts to play the specified sound. None
SoundCone3D SoundCone3D(#Sound3D, InnerCone.f, OuterCone.f, OuterConeVolume) Set the cone angle, to create a directional sound. None
SoundID3D SoundID3D = SoundID3D(#Sound3D) Returns the unique system identifier of the sound. Returns the unique system identifier of the sound.
SoundListenerLocate SoundListenerLocate(x, y, z) Changes the absolute sound listener (the ear) location in the world. None
SoundRange3D SoundRange3D(#Sound3D, Minimum, Maximum) Set the range, in world units, for the sound emission. None
SoundVolume3D SoundVolume3D(#Sound3D, Volume) Set the new volume, in real-time, for the #Sound3D. The volume value is saved for the #Sound3D, so it's not needed to call it every time. None
StopSound3D StopSound3D(#Sound3D) Stops the specified sound (if it was playing). None
SoundPlugin (8)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
UseFLACSoundDecoder UseFLACSoundDecoder() Enables the FLAC (Free Lossless Audio Codec) sound support for CatchSound and LoadSound. Sound streaming is supported for this plug-in. None
UseFLACSoundEncoder UseFLACSoundEncoder() Enables the FLAC (Free Lossless Audio Codec) sound support for SaveSound and EncodeSound. Only 16-bit mono/stereo sounds are supported. None
UseMP3SoundDecoder UseMP3SoundDecoder() Enables the MP3 (MPEG-1/2 Audio Layer III) sound support for CatchSound and LoadSound. Sound streaming is supported for this plug-in. None
UseMP3SoundEncoder UseMP3SoundEncoder([LibraryName$]) Enables the MP3 sound support for SaveSound and EncodeSound. Only 16-bit mono/stereo sounds are supported. Unlike the other sound encoders, this one is not built into PureBasic: MP3 encoding is provided by the LAME library (LGPL-licensed), which is loaded dynamically at runtime from libmp3lame.dll / libmp3lame.so / libmp3lame.dylib. If the library can't be found or loaded, SaveSound and EncodeSound simply fail (return zero) for the MP3 format. None
UseOGGSoundDecoder UseOGGSoundDecoder() Enables the OGG (OGG Vorbis) sound support for CatchSound and LoadSound. Sound streaming is supported for this plug-in. None
UseOGGSoundEncoder UseOGGSoundEncoder() Enables the OGG (OGG Vorbis) sound support for SaveSound and EncodeSound. Only 16-bit mono/stereo sounds are supported. None
UseOpusSoundDecoder UseOpusSoundDecoder() Enables the Opus sound support for CatchSound and LoadSound. Sound streaming is supported for this plug-in. None
UseOpusSoundEncoder UseOpusSoundEncoder() Enables the Opus sound support for SaveSound and EncodeSound. Only 16-bit mono/stereo sounds are supported, and the sound's sample rate must already be one of 8000, 12000, 16000, 24000 or 48000 hz (the fixed set of rates the Opus encoder accepts). None
SpecialEffect (12)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
AttachRibbonEffect AttachRibbonEffect(#Effect, NodeID) Attach the ribbon to the given node. None
CompositorEffectParameter CompositorEffectParameter(#Effect, TechniqueID, PassID, EffectName$, DataType, *Data) Set real-time parameter on the specified effect. None
CreateCompositorEffect Result = CreateCompositorEffect(#Effect, CameraID, EffectName$) Create a new compositor effect. Once created, the effect is immediately applied to the rendering. It is possible to hide the effect with HideEffect. Returns nonzero if the effect was created successfully and zero if there was an error. If #PB_Any was used as the #Effect parameter then the new generated number is returned on success.
CreateLensFlareEffect CreateLensFlareEffect(#Effect, CameraID, NodeID, BurstSize, HaloSize, HaloMaterialID, CircleMaterialID, BurstMaterialID) Create a new lensflare effect for the given camera. A lensflare is always attached to a node, and will be displayed automatically depending of the node position relative to the camera view. Returns nonzero if the lensflare effect was created successfully and zero if there was an error. If #PB_Any was used as the #Effect parameter then the new generated number is returned on success.
CreateRibbonEffect Result = CreateRibbonEffect(#Effect, MaterialID, NbChains, NbElements, Length) Create a new ribbon trail effect. Once created, the effect has to be attached with AttachRibbonEffect. It is possible to hide the effect with HideEffect. Returns nonzero if the effect was created successfully and zero if there was an error. If #PB_Any was used as the #Effect parameter then the new generated number is returned on success.
DetachRibbonEffect DetachRibbonEffect(#Effect, NodeID) Detach the ribbon from the given node. None
FreeEffect FreeEffect(#Effect) Free the specified effect. None
HideEffect HideEffect(#Effect, State) Hide or show the specified effect. None
IsEffect Result = IsEffect(#Effect) Tests if the given effect number is a valid and correctly initialized effect. Returns nonzero if #Effect is a valid effect, zero otherwise.
LensFlareEffectColor LensFlareEffectColor(#Effect, ColorType, Color) Changes the color of the specified lens flare effect part. None
RibbonEffectColor RibbonEffectColor(#Effect, ChainIndex, Color, FadeoutColor) Set the colors for the ribbon trail. None
RibbonEffectWidth RibbonEffectWidth(#Effect, ChainIndex, Width, FadeoutWidth) Changed the ribbon chain width. None
Spline (13)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
AddSplinePoint AddSplinePoint(#Spline, x, y, z) Add a new point to the spline. The time to go from one point to another is always the same, independent from the distance between these points. None
ClearSpline ClearSpline(#Spline) Clear the spline. All points will be removed from the spline. None
ComputeSpline ComputeSpline(#Spline, Offset) Computes the spline point position at the specified offset. Once the point has been computed, its position is available with SplineX, SplineY and SplineZ. None
CountSplinePoints Result = CountSplinePoints(#Spline) Returns the number of points in the spline. Returns the number of points in the spline.
CreateSpline Result = CreateSpline(#Spline) Creates a new spline. A spline doesn't exist physically in the 3D world, it is a virtual object which can be used for different purposes, like path-finding, smooth node moving (be sure to check NodeAnimation library for this as well) and more. To calculate the position of an intermediate point, see ComputeSpline. Returns zero if the spline can't be created. If #PB_Any is used as '#Spline' parameter, the new spline number is returned.
FreeSpline FreeSpline(#Spline) Frees a spline and releases all its associated memory. This spline must not be used (by using its number with the other functions in this library) after calling this function, unless you create it again. None
SplinePointX Result = SplinePointX(#Spline, PointIndex) Returns the spline point 'x' position. Returns the spline point 'x' position.
SplinePointY Result = SplinePointY(#Spline, PointIndex) Returns the spline point 'y' position. Returns the spline point 'y' position.
SplinePointZ Result = SplinePointZ(#Spline, PointIndex) Returns the spline point 'z' position. Returns the spline point 'z' position.
SplineX Result = SplineX(#Spline) Returns the spline's 'x' position in the world, after a ComputeSpline. Returns the spline point's 'x' position in the world, after a ComputeSpline.
SplineY Result = SplineY(#Spline) Returns the spline's 'y' position in the world, after a ComputeSpline. Returns the spline point's 'y' position in the world, after a ComputeSpline.
SplineZ Result = SplineZ(#Spline) Returns the spline's 'z' position in the world, after a ComputeSpline. Returns the spline point's 'z' position in the world, after a ComputeSpline.
UpdateSplinePoint UpdateSplinePoint(#Spline, PointIndex, x, y, z) Update the specified point in the spline. The time to go from one point to another is always the same, independent from the distance between these points. None
Sprite (26)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
CatchSprite Result = CatchSprite(#Sprite, *MemoryAddress [, Mode]) Loads the specified sprite from the given memory area. A screen should be opened with OpenScreen or OpenWindowedScreen before loading a sprite. Sprites can be in BMP format or any other format supported by the ImagePlugin library. A catched sprite can be freed by using the FreeSprite function. The 'CatchSprite' function is useful when using the 'IncludeBinary' PureBasic keyword. The images can be packed inside the executable. Nevertheless, use this option very carefully, as it will take more memory than storing the file in an external file (the file will be in both executable memory and loaded into physical memory). The following functions can be used to enable automatically more image formats: UseJPEGImageDecoder UseJPEG2000ImageDecoder UsePNGImageDecoder UseTIFFImageDecoder UseTGAImageDecoder UseWebPImageDecoder Nonzero if the sprite has been created, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used for the #Sprite parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
ClipSprite ClipSprite(#Sprite, x, y, Width, Height) Adds a clip zone to the specified sprite. For example, if a sprite is 100*100 (Width*Height) and a clipping zone is added as x=10, y=10, Width=20, Height=20 then when the sprite is displayed, only the rectangular area starting from x=10, y=10 with width=20 and height=20 will be displayed. None
CopySprite Result = CopySprite(#Sprite1, #Sprite2 [, Mode]) Copy the #Sprite1 to #Sprite2. Nonzero if the sprite has been copied, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used for the #Sprite2 parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
CreateSprite Result = CreateSprite(#Sprite, Width, Height [, Flags]) Creates an empty sprite with the specified dimensions. SpriteOutput can be used to draw on the sprite. Nonzero if the sprite has been created, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used for the #Sprite parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
DisplaySprite DisplaySprite(#Sprite, x.f, y.f) Displays the #Sprite at the specified position on the current screen. As there is no transparent color or blending, this function is faster than DisplayTransparentSprite. This function is clipped, so it's perfectly legal to display the sprite outside of the screen. None
DisplayTransparentSprite DisplayTransparentSprite(#Sprite, x.f, y.f [, Intensity [, Color]]) Display the #Sprite at the specified position on the current screen. The default transparent color is 0 (black - this color will not be displayed). It's possible to change the transparent color with TransparentSpriteColor. This function is clipped, so it's perfectly legal to display the sprite outside of the screen. The sprite has to be created with #PB_Sprite_AlphaBlending flag to use this command. None
FreeSprite FreeSprite(#Sprite) Removes the specified sprite from memory. It's not possible to use the sprite anymore after calling this function. None
GrabSprite Result = GrabSprite(#Sprite, x, y, Width, Height [, Flags]) Grabs the screen content from the area x, y, Width, Height and creates a new sprite. Nonzero if the sprite has been grabbed, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used for the #Sprite parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
InitSprite Result = InitSprite() Initializes the sprite environment for later use. You must put this function at the top of your source code if you want to use the sprite functions. Nonzero if the initialization of the sprite environment has succeeded, zero otherwise. You should always test this result to see if the sprite environment has been correctly initialized. If not you must quit the program or disable all the calls to the sprite related functions. This function tries to initialize DirectX 9, so if it fails, it's probably because DirectX is not found or is a previous version.
IsSprite Result = IsSprite(#Sprite) Tests if the given #Sprite number is a valid and correctly initialized, sprite. Nonzero if #Sprite is a valid sprite and zero otherwise.
LoadSprite Result = LoadSprite(#Sprite, Filename$ [, Mode]) Load the specified sprite into memory for immediate use. A screen should be opened with OpenScreen or OpenWindowedScreen before loading a sprite. The sprite can be in BMP format or any other format supported by the ImagePlugin library. The following functions can be used to enable automatically more image formats: UseGIFImageDecoder UseJPEGImageDecoder UseJPEG2000ImageDecoder UsePNGImageDecoder UseTIFFImageDecoder UseTGAImageDecoder UseWebPImageDecoder Nonzero if the sprite has been loaded, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used for the #Sprite parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
RotateSprite RotateSprite(#Sprite, Angle.f, Mode) Rotates the specified #Sprite to the given 'Angle'. None
SaveSprite Result = SaveSprite(#Sprite, Filename$ [, ImagePlugin [, Flags]]) Saves the specified sprite to a file. By default, the saved image will be in 24-bit BMP format. Very useful for screenshots when used with the GrabSprite function. Nonzero if the sprite has been successfully saved, zero otherwise.
SpriteBlendingMode SpriteBlendingMode(SourceMode, DestinationMode) Changes the way the sprite are blended with the background (when using DisplayTransparentSprite). This function is for advanced users only. The result can differ depending of the underlying subsystem: for example OpenGL and DirectX doesn't behave the same. None
SpriteCollision Result = SpriteCollision(#Sprite1, x1, y1, #Sprite2, x2, y2) Tests if the two sprites are overlapping. Nonzero if the two sprites are overlapping, zero otherwise.
SpriteDepth Result = SpriteDepth(#Sprite) Returns the color depth of the specified sprite. The color depth of the specified sprite.
SpriteHeight Result = SpriteHeight(#Sprite) Returns the height (in pixels) of the specified sprite. The height (in pixels) of the specified sprite.
SpriteID SpriteID = SpriteID(#Sprite) Returns the unique system identifier of the given sprite. The ID of the sprite. This sometimes also known as 'Handle'. Look at the extra chapter handles "Handles and Numbers" for more information.
SpriteOutput OutputID = SpriteOutput(#Sprite [, Flags]) Returns the OutputID of the sprite to perform 2D rendering operation on it. The output ID or zero if drawing is not possible. This value should be passed directly to the StartDrawing function to start the drawing operation. The return-value is valid only for one drawing operation and cannot be reused.
SpritePixelCollision Result = SpritePixelCollision(#Sprite1, x1, y1, #Sprite2, x2, y2) Tests if the two sprites are overlapping. #PB_Sprite_PixelCollision has to be specified at the sprite creation to have this command working. Nonzero if the two sprites are overlapping, zero otherwise.
SpriteQuality SpriteQuality(Quality) Changes the way the sprites are rendered. None
SpriteVectorOutput VectorOutputID = SpriteVectorOutput(#Sprite [, Flags]) Returns the OutputID of the sprite to perform 2D vector drawing operations on it. The drawing is done in an intermediate buffer which is copied back to the sprite by StopVectorDrawing. Returns the output ID or zero if drawing is not possible. This value should be passed directly to the StartVectorDrawing function to start the drawing operation. The return-value is valid only for one drawing operation and cannot be reused.
SpriteWidth Result = SpriteWidth(#Sprite) Returns the width (in pixels) of the specified sprite. The width (in pixels) of the specified sprite.
TransformSprite TransformSprite(#Sprite, x1, y1, [z1], x2, y2, [z2], x3, y3, [z3], x4, y4, [z4]) Transforms the sprite to the new given coordinates. This is typically used to perform real-time transformations. Warning, as a sprite is a combination of 2 triangles, the transformation could looks strange. If one of the optional 'z' parameter is specified, all need to be specified. None
TransparentSpriteColor TransparentSpriteColor(#Sprite, Color) Use the specified color as the transparent sprite color (when displayed with DisplayTransparentSprite). Only one color can be set as the transparent color and the previous alpha channel values are lost. If the sprite already have alpha information, this command is probably not needed. The sprite has to be created with #PB_Sprite_AlphaBlending flag to use this command. None
ZoomSprite ZoomSprite(#Sprite, Width, Height) Zooms the specified #Sprite from the given dimension. None
StaticGeometry (5)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
AddStaticGeometryEntity AddStaticGeometryEntity(#StaticGeometry, EntityID, x, y, z [, ScaleX, ScaleY, ScaleZ [, RotationX, RotationY, RotationZ [, RotationW, Mode]]]) Add an entity to the specified #StaticGeometry. The original entity is left untouched by this function and can be freed after the add. The same entity can be added multiple times. None
BuildStaticGeometry BuildStaticGeometry(#StaticGeometry) Build the final static geometry. Once created, a static geometry can't be modified anymore. None
CreateStaticGeometry Result = CreateStaticGeometry(#StaticGeometry, Width, Height, Length, EnableShadows) Create an empty static geometry. Returns nonzero if the static geometry has been successfully created and zero if not. If #PB_Any was used for the #StaticGeometry parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
FreeStaticGeometry FreeStaticGeometry(#StaticGeometry) Free the given StaticGeometry, previously initialized by CreateStaticGeometry. None
IsStaticGeometry Result = IsStaticGeometry(#StaticGeometry) Tests if the given #StaticGeometry is a valid and correctly initialized static geometry. Returns nonzero if #StaticGeometry is a valid static geometry and zero otherwise.
StatusBar (9)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
AddStatusBarField AddStatusBarField(Width) Adds a field to the current status bar previously created with CreateStatusBar. Each new field is created after the previous one. None
CreateStatusBar Result = CreateStatusBar(#StatusBar, WindowID) Create and add an empty #StatusBar to the specified WindowID. Once the bar is created, AddStatusBarField can be used to setup the different parts of the bar. Nonzero if the status bar has been successfully created, zero otherwise.
FreeStatusBar FreeStatusBar(#StatusBar) Free the given status bar. None
IsStatusBar Result = IsStatusBar(#StatusBar) Tests if the given status bar number is a valid and correctly initialized status bar. Nonzero if the status bar is valid, zero otherwise.
StatusBarHeight Result = StatusBarHeight(#StatusBar) Returns the height in pixel of the #StatusBar. This is useful for correct calculation on window height when using a statusbar. The height in pixels of the status bar.
StatusBarID StatusBarID = StatusBarID(#StatusBar) Returns the unique system identifier of the status bar. The system identifier. This result is sometimes also known as 'Handle'. Look at the extra chapter Handles and Numbers for more information.
StatusBarImage StatusBarImage(#StatusBar, Field, ImageID [, Appearance]) Sets the specified status bar field to display an image. None
StatusBarProgress StatusBarProgress(#StatusBar, Field, Value [, Appearance [, Min, Max]]) Display a progress bar in the specified 'Field' in the given '#StatusBar'. None
StatusBarText StatusBarText(#StatusBar, Field, Text$ [, Appearance]) Sets the text for the specified status bar field. None
String (37)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
Asc Result = Asc(String$) Return the first character value of the specified string. The string first character value.
Ascii *Buffer = Ascii(String$) Creates an Ascii representation of the string. When the buffer is no longer needed, the buffer needs to be freed with FreeMemory(). The Ascii representation of the string.
Bin Result$ = Bin(Value.q [, Type]) Converts a quad numeric number into a string, in binary format. A string holding the binary representation of the specified value.
Chr Text$ = Chr(CharacterValue) Returns a string created with the given character value. Returns a string created with the given character value. If the value is invalid, it will returns an empty string.
CountString Result = CountString(String$, StringToCount$) Returns the number of occurrences of StringToCount$ found in String$. The number of occurrences of 'StringToCount$' found in 'String$'.
EscapeString Result$ = EscapeString(String$ [, Mode]) Returns the escaped version of the string. UnescapeString can be used to do the reverse operation. An escaped string. Warning: On Windows, \t does not work with the graphical functions of the 2DDrawing and VectorDrawing libraries.
FindString Position = FindString(String$, StringToFind$ [, StartPosition [, Mode]]) Find the 'StringToFind$' within the given 'String$'. Returns the position (in character) of the string to find, or zero is the string isn't found. The first character index is 1.
FormatNumber Result$ = FormatNumber(Number.d [, NbDecimals [, DecimalPoint$ [, ThousandSeparator$]]]) Format a number into money-like format. The formatted number.
Hex Result$ = Hex(Value.q [, Type]) Converts a quad numeric number into a string, in hexadecimal format. A string holding the hexadecimal representation of the specified value.
InsertString Result$ = InsertString(String$, StringToInsert$, Position) Inserts 'StringToInsert$' into 'String$' at the specified 'Position'. A new string with the inserted string at the specified position.
LCase Result$ = LCase(String$) Returns the string converted into lower case characters. The string converted into lowercase.
Left Result$ = Left(String$, Length) Returns the specified number of characters from the left side of the string. A string holding the specified number of characters from the left side of the string.
Len Length = Len(String$) Returns the character length of the string. The character length of the string.
LSet Result$ = LSet(String$, Length [, Character$]) Adjusts the length of a string by adding characters at the end of the string if necessary to reach the specified length. A new string holding the original string padded with the specified character to fit the length.
LTrim Result$ = LTrim(String$ [, Character$]) Removes all the specified characters located in the front of a string. A new string holding the original string with the front characters removed.
Mid Result$ = Mid(String$, StartPosition [, Length]) Extracts a string of specified length from the given string. A new string holding the extracted characters.
RemoveString String$ = RemoveString(String$, StringToRemove$ [, Mode [, StartPosition [, NbOccurrences]]]) Finds all occurrences of 'StringToRemove$' within the specified 'String$' and removes them. A new string without the removed strings.
ReplaceString String$ = ReplaceString(String$, StringToFind$, ReplacementString$ [, Mode [, StartPosition [, NbOccurrences]]]) Try to find any occurrences of 'StringToFind$' in the given 'String$' and replace them with 'ReplacementString$'. A new string with the replaced strings.
ReverseString Result$ = ReverseString(String$) Reverses all the characters in the 'String$'. The last characters becomes the first characters, and vice-versa. A string holding the reversed string.
Right Result$ = Right(String$, Length) Returns the specified number of characters from the right side of the string. A string holding the specified number of characters from the right side of the string.
RSet Result$ = RSet(String$, Length [, Character$]) Adjusts the length of the string by adding characters at the beginning of the string if necessary to reach the specified length. A new string holding the original string padded with the specified character to fit the length.
RTrim Result$ = RTrim(String$ [, Character$]) Removes all the specified characters located at the end of a string. A new string holding the original string with the end characters removed.
Space Result$ = Space(Length) Creates a string of the given length filled with 'space' characters. A new string filled with 'space' characters.
Str Result$ = Str(Value.q) Convert a signed quad number into a string. A string holding the converted value.
StrD Result$ = StrD(Value.d [, NbDecimal]) Converts a double number into a string. A string holding the converted value.
StrF Result$ = StrF(Value.f [, NbDecimal]) Converts a float number into a string. A string holding the converted value.
StringByteLength Result = StringByteLength(String$ [, Format]) Returns the number of bytes required to store the string in memory in a given format. The number of bytes required to store the string in memory in a given format.
StringField Result$ = StringField(String$, Index, Delimiter$) Returns the string field at the specified index.
StrU Result$ = StrU(Value.q [, Type]) Converts an unsigned numeric number into a string. A string holding the converted value.
Trim Result$ = Trim(String$ [, Character$]) Removes all the specified characters located at the beginning and at the end of a string. A new string holding the original string without the removed characters.
UCase Result$ = UCase(String$) Returns the original string converted into upper case characters. The string converted into uppercase.
UnescapeString Result$ = UnescapeString(String$ [, Mode]) Returns the unescaped version of the string. EscapeString can be used to do the reverse operation. An unescaped string. Warning: On Windows, \t does not work with the graphical functions of the 2DDrawing and VectorDrawing libraries.
Unicode *Buffer = Unicode(String$) Creates an Unicode representation of the string. When the buffer is no longer needed, the buffer needs to be freed with FreeMemory(). The Unicode representation of the string.
UTF8 *Buffer = UTF8(String$) Creates a buffer with an UTF8 representation of the string. When the buffer is no longer needed, the buffer needs to be freed with FreeMemory(). The UTF8 representation of the string.
Val Result.q = Val(String$) Converts a string into a quad numeric value. The string may be an integer in decimal, hexadecimal (with '$' prefix) or binary (with '%' prefix) format. The number parsing stops at the first non numeric character. The numeric value of the string.
ValD Result.d = ValD(String$) Converts a string into a double value. The string must be a double in decimal or in scientific (exponent) format. The number parsing stops at the first non numeric character. The double value of the string.
ValF Result.f = ValF(String$) Converts a string into a float value. The string must be a float in decimal or in scientific (exponent) format. The number parsing stops at the first non numeric character. The float value of the string.

NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
CocoaMessage Result = CocoaMessage(ReturnValueAddress, Object, Method$ [, ParameterValue [, Parameter$, [, ParamaterValue, ...]]]) For advanced users. Available on OS X only, it allows to easily send an Objective-C message to the OS X framework and access any API. Usually Objective-C use brackets to have a clear syntax for messages. As PureBasic doesn't have built-in Objective-C support, it needs to emulate it, so the syntax is a bit different. Once learnt, it's easy to call the required API. To get more examples, please read the following thread on the forums. Integer return value. Useful for object creation id.

CPUName Result$ = CPUName() Returns the name of the CPU. Returns the name of the CPU (the full vendor information). There is no standardized output across CPU, so this information shouldn't be used to identify the CPU at runtime, but can be useful for logging purpose.
Delay Delay(Time) Halts the program execution for the specified amount of time. None
DoubleClickTime Result = DoubleClickTime() Returns the system setting for the double-click time. If two mouse clicks happen within this time, they are considered a double-click. Returns the double-click time in milliseconds.
ElapsedMilliseconds Result.q = ElapsedMilliseconds() Returns the number of milliseconds that have elapsed since a specific time in the past. Returns the elapsed time in milliseconds.
MemoryStatus Result.q = MemoryStatus(Type) Returns the specified memory type information. Returns the specified memory type information.
OSLanguage Result$ = OSLanguage() Returns the language the operating system is currently running in. Returns the language as a lowercase two-letter ISO 639-1 code (for example 'en', 'fr', 'de' or 'ja'). Any region or script part is stripped, so only the language itself is reported. An empty string is returned if the language can't be determined. On Windows the user default UI language is used, on macOS the first entry of the preferred languages list, and on Linux the 'LC_ALL', 'LC_MESSAGES' or 'LANG' environment variable (in that order).
OSVersion Result = OSVersion() Returns the version of the operating system on which the program has been launched. Returns one of the following values, depending on the OS on which the command run: Windows #PB_OS_Windows_NT3_51 #PB_OS_Windows_95 #PB_OS_Windows_NT_4 #PB_OS_Windows_98 #PB_OS_Windows_ME #PB_OS_Windows_2000 #PB_OS_Windows_XP #PB_OS_Windows_Server_2003 #PB_OS_Windows_Vista #PB_OS_Windows_Server_2008 #PB_OS_Windows_7 #PB_OS_Windows_Server_2008_R2 #PB_OS_Windows_8 #PB_OS_Windows_Server_2012 #PB_OS_Windows_8_1 #PB_OS_Windows_Server_2012_R2 #PB_OS_Windows_10 #PB_OS_Windows_Server_2016 #PB_OS_Windows_Server_2019 #PB_OS_Windows_Server_2022 #PB_OS_Windows_11 #PB_OS_Windows_Server_2025 #PB_OS_Windows_Future ; New Windows version (not existing when the program was written) Linux #PB_OS_Linux_2_2 #PB_OS_Linux_2_4 #PB_OS_Linux_2_6 #PB_OS_Linux_Future ; New Linux version (not existing when the program was written) Mac OSX #PB_OS_MacOSX_10_0 #PB_OS_MacOSX_10_1 #PB_OS_MacOSX_10_2 #PB_OS_MacOSX_10_3 #PB_OS_MacOSX_10_4 #PB_OS_MacOSX_10_5 #PB_OS_MacOSX_10_6 #PB_OS_MacOSX_10_7 #PB_OS_MacOSX_10_8 #PB_OS_MacOSX_10_9 #PB_OS_MacOSX_10_10 #PB_OS_MacOSX_10_11 #PB_OS_MacOSX_10_12 #PB_OS_MacOSX_10_13 #PB_OS_MacOSX_10_14 #PB_OS_MacOSX_10_15 #PB_OS_MacOSX_11 #PB_OS_MacOSX_12 #PB_OS_MacOSX_13 #PB_OS_MacOSX_14 #PB_OS_MacOSX_15 #PB_OS_MacOSX_Future ; New MacOS X version (not existing when the program was written)

EventGadget can be used to know which SysTrayIcon has been used. EventType functions is also updated by this function. Nonzero if the SysTray icon has been successfully added, zero otherwise.

NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
AddTerrainTexture AddTerrainTexture(#Terrain, Layer, WorldSize, DiffuseSpecular$, NormalHeight$) Adds a texture to the #Terrain. None
BuildTerrain BuildTerrain(#Terrain) Builds the terrain. Before building a terrain, tiles have to be defined with DefineTerrainTile, and textures added with AddTerrainTexture. None
CreateTerrain Result = CreateTerrain(#Terrain, Size, WorldSize, Scale, NbLayers, Filename$, Extension$) Creates a new terrain. SetupTerrains has to be called before to set the default parameter for the new terrain. After the terrain creation, new tiles can be defined with DefineTerrainTile and textures applied with AddTerrainTexture. Once the terrain definition is finished, BuildTerrain needs to be called to build the final terrain. Returns zero if the #Terrain can't be created. If #PB_Any is used as '#Terrain' parameter, the new terrain number is returned.
CreateTerrainBody CreateTerrainBody(#Terrain, Restitution, Friction) Adds a static physic body to the terrain. This enable physic objects to collide with the terrain. None
DefineTerrainTile Result = DefineTerrainTile(#Terrain, TileX, TileY, HeightMap$, FlipX, FlipY) Defines the content of a tile in the terrain grid. Returns zero if the #Terrain can't be created.
FreeTerrain FreeTerrain(#Terrain) Frees a terrain and releases all its associated memory. This terrain must not be used (by using its number with the other functions in this library) after calling this function, unless you create it again. None
FreeTerrainBody FreeTerrainBody(#Terrain) Free the body associated with the terrain. None
GetTerrainTileHeightAtPoint Result = GetTerrainTileHeightAtPoint(#Terrain, TileX, TileY, x, y) Returns the height of the terrain tile at the specified position. Returns the terrain tile height (in world unit) at the specified coordinates.
GetTerrainTileLayerBlend Result = GetTerrainTileLayerBlend(#Terrain, TileX, TileY, Layer, x, y) Returns the terrain tile layer blend value at the specified position. Returns the terrain tile layer blend value at the specified position. The blend value ranges from 0.0 (fully transparent) to 1.0 (fully opaque).
SaveTerrain SaveTerrain(#Terrain, ModifiedOnly) Saves the terrain to disk, using the filename and extension defined with CreateTerrain. None
SetTerrainTileHeightAtPoint SetTerrainTileHeightAtPoint(#Terrain, TileX, TileY, x, y, Height) Sets the height of the terrain tile at the specified position. The change will not be reflected immediately, UpdateTerrain has to be called once all the modifications are done. None
SetTerrainTileLayerBlend SetTerrainTileLayerBlend(#Terrain, TileX, TileY, Layer, x, y, Value) Changes the terrain tile layer blend value at the specified position. The change will not be reflected immediately, UpdateTerrainTileLayerBlend has to be called once all the modifications are done. None
SetupTerrains SetupTerrains(LightID, CompositeMapDistance.f, Flags) Setup the default parameters for all the future created terrains. None
TerrainHeight Result = TerrainHeight(#Terrain, x, z) Gets the terrain height at the specified position in the world. Returns the terrain height (in world unit) at the specified position. If the terrain is not found at the specified position, the result will be zero.
TerrainLocate TerrainLocate(#Terrain, x, y, z) Changes the terrain absolute location in the world. None
TerrainMousePick Result = TerrainMousePick(#Terrain, CameraID, x, y) Simulates a mouse click on the terrain under the specified 2D point (x,y - in pixels) on the specified camera. If the terrain has been hit by the simulated mouse click, it will return #True, else it will return #False. To get information about the pick position, use PickX, PickY and PickZ.
TerrainRenderMode TerrainRenderMode(#Terrain, Flag) Changes the way the terrain is rendered. None
TerrainTileHeightAtPosition Result = TerrainTileHeightAtPosition(#Terrain, TileX, TileY, Layer, x, y) Returns the height of the terrain tile at the specified coordinates. Returns the terrain tile height (in world unit) at the specified coordinates.
TerrainTileLayerMapSize Result = TerrainTileLayerMapSize(#Terrain, TileX, TileY) Returns the terrain tile layer blend map size. Returns the size (in pixels) of the terrain blend map. As a blend map layer is always square, the size is the width and the height of the blend map layer.
TerrainTilePointX Result = TerrainTilePointX(#Terrain, TileX, TileY, x, y, z) Returns the 'x' position of the point in the terrain tile. Returns 'x' position (in pixels) of the point in the terrain tile.
TerrainTilePointY Result = TerrainTilePointY(#Terrain, TileX, TileY, x, y, z) Returns the 'y' position of the point in the terrain tile. Returns 'y' position (in pixels) of the point in the terrain tile.
TerrainTileSize Result = TerrainTileSize(#Terrain, TileX, TileY) Returns the size of the terrain tile. Returns the size (in pixels) of the terrain tile. As a tile is always square, the size is the width and the height of the tile.
UpdateTerrain UpdateTerrain(#Terrain) Updates the terrain. This is needs after altering the terrain with commands like SetTerrainTileHeightAtPoint. None
UpdateTerrainTileLayerBlend UpdateTerrainTileLayerBlend(#Terrain, TileX, TileY, Layer) Updates the terrain tile blend layer. This is needed after modifying the layer blend value with SetTerrainTileLayerBlend. None

NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
CopyTexture Result = CopyTexture(#Texture, #NewTexture) Creates a new texture which is the exact copy of the specified texture. Nonzero if the texture was successfully duplicated, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used for the #NewTexture parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
CreateCubeMapTexture Result = CreateCubeMapTexture(#Texture, Width, Height, TextureName$ [, BackColor]) Creates a new cube map texture. A cube map texture use the surrounding to render itself as reflection on it. This texture has to exist in an OGRE script. Returns zero if the texture can't be created. If #PB_Any is used as '#Texture' parameter, the new texture number is returned.
CreateCubicTexture Result = CreateCubicTexture(#Texture, #Texture1, #Texture2, #Texture3, #Texture4, #Texture5, #Texture6) Creates a new cubic texture using the specified textures. Cubic textures are useful to create world like reflections. #PB_Material_EnvironmentMap should be specified with SetMaterialAttribute to enable cubic reflection. Nonzero if the cubic texture was successfully created, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used for the #Texture parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
CreateRenderTexture Result = CreateRenderTexture(#Texture, CameraID, Width, Height [, Flags [, RenderTextureName$]]) Creates a new render texture. The camera associated to the texture will render its view directly on the texture, without being displayed on screen. This can be very useful to have objects which display a part of the scene (like a TV screen, a mirror etc). Returns zero if the texture can't be created. If #PB_Any is used as '#Texture' parameter, the new texture number is returned.
CreateTexture Result = CreateTexture(#Texture, Width, Height [, TextureName$]) Creates a new blank texture with the specified dimension. Nonzero if the texture was successfully created, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used for the #Texture parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
EntityCubeMapTexture Result = EntityCubeMapTexture(#Texture, #Entity) Applies the cube map texture to the entity. The entity will reflect the world around it. None
FreeTexture FreeTexture(#Texture) Frees the specified texture. All its associated memory is released and this object can't be used anymore. None
GetScriptTexture Result = GetScriptTexture(#Texture, Name$) Get a texture defined in an OGRE script file. Scripts are loaded and parsed when calling Parse3DScripts. Nonzero if the texture was successfully created, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used for the #Texture parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
IsTexture Result = IsTexture(#Texture) Tests if the given texture is valid and correctly initialized. Nonzero if the texture is valid, zero otherwise.
LoadTexture Result = LoadTexture(#Texture, Filename$) Loads a new texture from the disk. Before loading a texture, an archive has to be specified with Add3DArchive. Texture format can be in PNG, TGA or JPG. It's strongly recommended to make the texture dimension square and with power of 2 width/height: 64x64, 128x128, 256x256... Old GFX cards can have limitation, so if possible limit the texture size to 256x256. Nonzero if the texture was successfully loaded, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used for the #Texture parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
SaveRenderTexture Result = SaveRenderTexture(#Texture, Filename$) Save the render texture content. It can be useful to do screenshots of a particular scene. The save format can only be PNG. If the texture can't be saved (permission error, disk full etc), the returned value will be zero.
TextureHeight Height = TextureHeight(#Texture) Returns the height of the specified texture. The height of the texture, in pixels.
TextureID TextureID = TextureID(#Texture) Returns the unique system identifier of the texture. Returns the unique system identifier of the texture.
TextureOutput OutputID = TextureOutput(#Texture [, Flags]) Returns the OutputID of the image to perform 2D rendering operation on it. Textures created with CreateRenderTexture are not supported. Returns the output ID or zero if drawing is not possible. This value should be passed directly to the StartDrawing function to start the drawing operation. The return-value is valid only for one drawing operation and cannot be reused.

Thread (18)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
CreateMutex Mutex = CreateMutex() Creates a new mutex object. The mutex is initially unlocked. The main objective of the mutex functions is thread synchronization. They do not create too much overhead, but they only work within one program, not system-wide. A mutex is an object that can only be "owned" or locked by one thread at a time, so it is used to protect shared resources. Only the thread that has the mutex locked may access a certain file, memory area, ... See LockMutex and UnlockMutex for locking/unlocking a mutex. The new mutext object, or zero if the mutex creation has failed.
CreateSemaphore Semaphore = CreateSemaphore([InitialCount]) Creates a new semaphore object. A semaphore is a thread synchronization object that keeps an internal count. It has two kinds of operations: signal and wait. A wait operation decreases the count of the semaphore by one. If the count would drop below 0, the wait operation will block until a signal call is made. A signal operation increases the count one, releasing a blocking thread if there is one. A semaphore allows to enforce minimum or maximum counts across threads for example to prevent a queue from running out or getting too many items. Unlike a mutex, a semaphore object is not "owned" by a particular thread, which means that signal/wait calls do not need to be done from the same thread as it is the case with LockMutex and UnlockMutex. In fact a common use for a semaphore objects is for one thread to do the SignalSemaphore calls and for another one to do all WaitSemaphore calls to implement a producer/consumer pattern. The new semaphore, or zero if the semaphore creation has failed.
CreateThread Thread = CreateThread(@ProcedureName(), *Value) Creates a new thread running in the application background. If the thread is correctly created, it returns the Thread number which is used with the other thread functions, such as KillThread, PauseThread, etc. The procedure which you use as a thread must take one parameter and cannot return anything. The '*Value' argument of CreateThread() is passed as the parameter to the procedure. If you do try to return a value from your thread it will simply be lost. The number for the newly created thread, or zero if a new thread could not be created. This number is required if you want to control the thread using the other functions in this library.
FreeMutex FreeMutex(Mutex) Frees a mutex object and the memory it requires. None
FreeSemaphore FreeSemaphore(Semaphore) Destroys the given Semaphore object and frees all resources used by it. None
IsThread Result = IsThread(Thread) Tests if the given thread number is a valid thread created with the CreateThread function, and if it is still running. Nonzero if the thread is still valid and running, zero otherwise.
KillThread KillThread(Thread) Immediately kills the specified thread, which had previously been created with CreateThread. This is a very dangerous function, and should only be used rarely. The problem is that the thread is killed immediately and has no chance to perform any cleanup code (for example, freeing memory, releasing items, de-allocating its own stack). If possible, a flag like a global variable should be used to tell the thread to quit itself (which does the needed cleanup) and this function should only be used if this is not possible for some reason. None
LockMutex LockMutex(Mutex) Waits until the mutex object is available (not locked by another thread) and then locks the object so no other thread can get a lock on the object. After this function returns, it is assured that this thread is the only one with a locked state on the mutex. The thread can now freely access the shared resource that is protected by this mutex, as it is the only one with exclusive access to the mutex. If another thread calls LockMutex() while this one has the lock, it will wait inside the LockMutex() function until this thread calls UnlockMutex to release its lock on the mutex. Note: Since the LockMutex() function waits until the mutex is available, it can easily lead to lockup situations if a UnlockMutex call is forgotten. See CreateMutex for a code example. None
PauseThread PauseThread(Thread) Pauses the execution of the specified thread, previously created with CreateThread. The thread can be resumed with ResumeThread. None
ResumeThread ResumeThread(Thread) Resumes execution of the specified thread, previously paused with PauseThread. None
SignalSemaphore SignalSemaphore(Semaphore) Increases the internal count of the semaphore by one, releasing a waiting thread if there is one. None
ThreadID ThreadID = ThreadID(Thread) Returns the unique system identifier of the thread. The system identifier. This result is sometimes also known as 'Handle'. Look at the extra chapter Handles and Numbers for more information.
ThreadPriority OldPriority = ThreadPriority(Thread, Priority) Change the priority of the specified thread and returns the old priority. The priority value can go from 1 to 32. 1 is the lowest priority available, 16 is the normal priority and 32 is the time critical priority (highest, please don't use it unless you know what you're doing). If the priority is 0, then the priority isn't changed (useful to only retrieve the thread priority without change it). All threads are created with a normal priority. Typically you would give a thread which is always running (for example, an image processing thread) a priority which is not greater than any other thread in your system. The reason for this is that if it is always running, and it has a high priority, then no other thread will get a chance to run. If a thread needs to be highly responsive but spends most of its time waiting for some event you might consider giving it a higher than normal priority. Windows schedules threads (chooses which one to run for a short length of time) using a preemptive priority based scheduling strategy, with round robin scheduling within the same priority level. This means that if it is time for execution of a different thread (known as a context switch) then the thread with the highest priority that is available to run will be the next one to be executed. If there is more than one thread with the highest priority, and they are available to run, then each thread will be cycled through on successive context switches. The priority of the thread before this function was called. This can be useful if you only want to boost the priority of the thread for a short time and then return it to its previous level. The returned value is not necessary the same than the one set with ThreadPriority(), as it depends of the granularity of the priority tuning offered by the system.
TryLockMutex Result = TryLockMutex(Mutex) Tries to lock the specified mutex. Unlike LockMutex, this function does not stop execution until the mutex is available. It returns immediately and the return-value indicates if the lock was successful or not. This is useful in situations were the thread should not wait for the mutex to be available but rather do other things in the meantime. Nonzero if the mutex was successfully locked, zero otherwise.
TrySemaphore Result = TrySemaphore(Semaphore) Decreases the internal count of the semaphore by one only if the count is above 0. This is the same as a WaitSemaphore operation, but without blocking if the count would fall below 0. Nonzero if the semaphore count was decreased, or zero if the count could not be decreased because it was already zero.
UnlockMutex UnlockMutex(Mutex) Unlocks a mutex previously locked by LockMutex. The mutex is then available again for other threads to lock it. None
WaitSemaphore WaitSemaphore(Semaphore) Decreases the internal count of the semaphore by one, blocking thread execution if the count would fall below zero. A blocked thread is resumed as soon as another thread calls SignalSemaphore. None
WaitThread Result = WaitThread(Thread [, Timeout]) Stop the program execution until the specified 'Thread' exits, or the optional timeout (in milliseconds) is reached. If the thread is already finished, it returns immediately. Nonzero if the thread has ended, or zero if the timeout was reached.
