VectorDrawing (67)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
AddPathArc AddPathArc(x1.d, y1.d, x2.d, y2.d, Radius.d, [, Flags]) Adds a straight line towards (x1, y2) followed by an arc in the direction of (x2, y2) to the vector drawing path. This function can be used to create paths with rounded corners. The new cursor position will be the endpoint of the arc. None
AddPathBox AddPathBox(x.d, y.d, Width.d, Height.d [, Flags]) Add a box to the vector drawing path. This is a convenience function that combines the needed AddPathLine calls to create a simple box shape. By default, this function ends the current figure in the path and adds the box as an unconnected and closed figure to the path (i.e. a box that can be filled). This behavior can be changed with the appropriate flags. None
AddPathCircle AddPathCircle(x.d, y.d, Radius.d [, StartAngle.d, EndAngle.d [, Flags]]) Add a circle (or a partial circle) to the vector drawing path. By default, this function ends the current figure in the path and adds the circle as an unconnected figure to the path (full circles are marked as closed). This behavior can be changed with the appropriate flags. None
AddPathCurve AddPathCurve(x1.d, y1.d, x2.d, y2.d, x3.d, y3.d [, Flags]) Adds a cubic bezier curve to the vector drawing path. The curve starts at the current path position and ends at (x3, y3). The other two points determine the shape of the curve. None
AddPathEllipse AddPathEllipse(x.d, y.d, RadiusX.d, RadiusY.d [, StartAngle.d, EndAngle.d [, Flags]]) Add an ellipse (or a partial ellipse) to the vector drawing path. By default, this function ends the current figure in the path and adds the ellipse as an unconnected figure to the path (full ellipses are marked as closed). This behavior can be changed with the appropriate flags. None
AddPathLine AddPathLine(x.d, y.d [, Flags]) Adds a straight line to the vector drawing path. The line starts at the current cursor position and ends at the given coordinates. None
AddPathSegments AddPathSegments(Segments$ [, Flags]) Add multiple segments described in string format to the vector drawing path. This command can be used to reproduce the path commands recorded with the PathSegments command. None
AddPathText AddPathText(Text$) Add the outline of the characters in the given text to the current cursor position in the vector drawing path. The current position can be set with MovePathCursor. After the call to this function the cursor is moved to the end of the added text. The DrawVectorText function should be preferred if possible. See the below remarks for details. None
BeginVectorLayer BeginVectorLayer([Alpha]) Begins a new empty layer on top of the current vector drawing output. All future drawing operations will be performed on this layer until EndVectorLayer is called. This command also saves the current drawing state in the same way as SaveVectorState. Multiple layers can be created. None
ClipPath ClipPath([Flags]) Clip the vector drawing output to the area defined by the current vector drawing path. Future drawing operations will only affect areas within the current path. The clipping will be combined with any clipping that previously existed on the drawing output. By default, the path is reset after calling this function. This can be prevented with the appropriate flags. None
ClosePath ClosePath() Closes the current figure in the vector drawing path by adding a straight line to the starting point of the figure. The starting point is the location of the last MovePathCursor call. When a path is filled, only closed figures are taken into account. None
ConvertCoordinateX Result.d = ConvertCoordinateX(x.d, y.d [, Source, Target]) Convert a point from one coordinate system to another in the vector drawing output. This function returns the X coordinate of the conversion. The Y coordinate can be retrieved with the ConvertCoordinateY function. Returns the X coordinate of the point in the target coordinate system.
ConvertCoordinateY Result.d = ConvertCoordinateY(x.d, y.d [, Source, Target]) Convert a point from one coordinate system to another in the vector drawing output. This function returns the Y coordinate of the conversion. The X coordinate can be retrieved with the ConvertCoordinateX function. Returns the Y coordinate of the point in the target coordinate system.
CustomDashPath CustomDashPath(Width.d, Array.d() [, Flags [, StartOffset.d]]) Draw the current drawing path with a custom dashing pattern. By default, the path is reset after calling this function. This can be prevented with the appropriate flags. None
DashPath DashPath(Width.d, Length.d [, Flags [, StartOffset.d]]) Draw the current drawing path as a series of dashes of equal length and distance. By default, the path is reset after calling this function. This can be prevented with the appropriate flags. None
DotPath DotPath(Width.d, Distance.d [, Flags [, StartOffset.d]]) Draw the current drawing path as a line of dots. By default, the path is reset after calling this function. This can be prevented with the appropriate flags. None
DrawVectorImage DrawVectorImage(ImageID [, Alpha [, Width.d, Height.d]]) Draw the specified image directly to the vector drawing output. The image will be drawn at the location of the path cursor. The cursor will be moved to the location of the bottom/right corner of the image after the image is drawn. None
DrawVectorParagraph DrawVectorParagraph(Text$, Width.d, Height.d [, Flags]) Draw a paragraph of text (multiple lines) within a given bounding box with automatic layout for linebreaks. If the text does not fit the defined box, it will be cut at the end. The font to use can be set with VectorFont. None
DrawVectorText DrawVectorText(Text$) Draw the given text at the current location of the path cursor. The cursor will be moved horizontally to the end of the drawn text. The font to use can be set with VectorFont. None
EndVectorLayer EndVectorLayer() Finishes drawing on a temporary layer created by BeginVectorLayer. The contents of the layer are drawn to the next lower layer using the alpha transparency of the temporary layer. This command also restores the drawing state that was in effect when BeginVectorLayer was called. None
FillPath FillPath([Flags]) Fill all closed figures in the current vector drawing path with color from the drawing source. By default, the path is reset after calling this function. This can be prevented with the appropriate flags. None
FillVectorOutput FillVectorOutput() Fills the entire drawing area (except areas outside the clipping path) with the current drawing source. This operation is equivalent to constructing a path that covers the entire drawing area and calling FillPath on it. None
FlipCoordinatesX FlipCoordinatesX(AxisX.d [, System]) Mirrors the vector drawing coordinate system at the specified X axis. None
FlipCoordinatesY FlipCoordinatesY(AxisY.d [, System]) Mirrors the vector drawing coordinate system at the specified Y axis. None
IsInsidePath Result = IsInsidePath(x.d, y.d [, CoordinateSystem]) Tests if the given coordinates are within a closed figure in the current vector drawing path. That is, this function returns non-zero if the given point would be filled by a call to FillPath. Returns non-zero if the point is within the path and zero if not.
IsInsideStroke Result = IsInsideStroke(x.d, y.d, Width.d [, Flags [, CoordinateSystem]]) Tests if the given coordinates are within an area that will be drawn to by a call to StrokePath. Returns non-zero if the point is within the stroke and zero if not.
IsPathEmpty Result = IsPathEmpty() Tests if the current vector drawing path is empty. Returns non-zero if the path is empty and zero if the path contains any line segments.
MovePathCursor MovePathCursor(x.d, y.d [, Flags]) Moves the cursor of the vector drawing path to a new location. This also starts a new figure within the path, which means that a call to ClosePath will draw a line back to this location. None
NewVectorPage NewVectorPage() Finishes the current page on the vector drawing output and starts a fresh page. The following outputs support multiple pages: PrinterVectorOutput PdfVectorOutput None
PathBoundsHeight Result.d = PathBoundsHeight() Returns the height of the bounding box for the current vector drawing path. The result is the difference between the lowest & highest Y coordinate that stroking/filling the current path would reach. The height of the bounding box.
PathBoundsWidth Result.d = PathBoundsWidth() Returns the width of the bounding box for the current vector drawing path. The result is the difference between the lowest & highest X coordinate that stroking/filling the current path would reach. The width of the bounding box.
PathBoundsX Result.d = PathBoundsX() Returns the X coordinate (top/left corner) of the bounding box for the current vector drawing path. The result is the lowest X coordinate that stroking/filling the current path would reach. The X coordinate of the bounding box.
PathBoundsY Result.d = PathBoundsY() Returns the Y coordinate (top/left corner) of the bounding box for the current vector drawing path. The result is the lowest Y coordinate that stroking/filling the current path would reach. The Y coordinate of the bounding box.
PathCursorX Result.d = PathCursorX() Returns the current X coordinate of the vector drawing cursor. This is the location where new path segments will be added or text will be drawn. The X coordinate of the path cursor.
PathCursorY Result.d = PathCursorY() Returns the current Y coordinate of the vector drawing cursor. This is the location where new path segments will be added or text will be drawn. The Y coordinate of the path cursor.
PathLength Result.d = PathLength() Returns the total length of the current vector drawing path. Returns the length of the current path.
PathPointAngle Result.d = PathPointAngle(Distance.d) Returns the angle of the path at the point at the given distance from the start of the current vector drawing path. The angle of the path at the given point in degrees. The angle 0 marks at the positive X axis.
PathPointX Result.d = PathPointX(Distance.d) Returns the X coordinate of the point at the given distance from the start of the current vector drawing path. The X coordinate of the point of the path.
PathPointY Result.d = PathPointY(Distance.d) Returns the Y coordinate of the point at the given distance from the start of the current vector drawing path. The Y coordinate of the point of the path.
PathSegments Result$ = PathSegments() Returns a string description of the current vector drawing path. The result can be used to examine the current path or in the AddPathSegments command to reproduce the same path later. The returned string contains one letter commands followed by the appropriate number of coordinate parameters. Each value is separated by a single space. All coordinates are absolute. M x y MovePathCursor L x y AddPathLine C x1 y1 x2 y2 x3 y3 AddPathCurve Z ClosePath There are no string representations for commands like AddPathCircle or AddPathEllipse, as their results are internally converted to curves by the vector drawing library.
PdfVectorOutput Result = PdfVectorOutput(Filename$, Width.d, Height.d [, Unit]) Creates a PDF file and returns the OutputID to perform vector drawing operations. The actual drawing operations must be enclosed in a StartVectorDrawing / StopVectorDrawing block. The PDF file can have multiple pages using the NewVectorPage command. The OutputID of the given file to perform 2D rendering operation on it using StartVectorDrawing.
ResetCoordinates ResetCoordinates([System]) Reset any coordinate transformations that were applied to the current vector drawing output and restore the coordinate system that was in effect when StartVectorDrawing was called. None
ResetPath ResetPath() Resets the vector drawing path to an empty path and moves to cursor to position (0, 0). None
RestoreVectorState RestoreVectorState() Restores the vector drawing state that was stored in the corresponding call to SaveVectorState. None
RotateCoordinates RotateCoordinates(x.d, y.d, Angle.d [, System]) Rotate the vector drawing coordinate system around the given center point. The center point is expressed in terms of the current coordinate system. None
SaveVectorState SaveVectorState() Saves the current vector drawing state to be restored later. Multiple states can be saved on a stack and restored in the reverse order they were saved. The following information is saved with this command: - The coordinate transformations - The drawing source - The drawing font - The clipping path Note that the current path is not saved by this command. None
ScaleCoordinates ScaleCoordinates(ScaleX.d, ScaleY.d [, System]) Scale the vector drawing coordinate system by stretching it in the x/y direction. None
SkewCoordinates SkewCoordinates(AngleX.d, AngleY.d [, System]) Apply a shearing angle in the x and/or y direction to the vector drawing coordinate system. None
StartVectorDrawing Result = StartVectorDrawing(Output) Prepares the vector drawing library to draw to the specified output. Returns nonzero if drawing is possible or zero if the operation failed.
StopVectorDrawing StopVectorDrawing() Finishes a sequence of drawing operations and frees all resources allocated by it. None
StrokePath StrokePath(Width.d [, Flags]) Stroke the current drawing path with the current drawing source. This draws the path as a solid line. By default, the path is reset after calling this function. This can be prevented with the appropriate flags. None
SvgVectorOutput Result = SvgVectorOutput(Filename$, Width.d, Height.d [, Unit]) Creates an SVG (scalable vector graphics) file and returns the OutputID to perform vector drawing operations. The actual drawing operations must be enclosed in a StartVectorDrawing / StopVectorDrawing block. The SVG file can have multiple pages using the NewVectorPage command. The OutputID of the given file to perform 2D rendering operation on it using StartVectorDrawing.
TranslateCoordinates TranslateCoordinates(x.d, y.d [, System]) Move the origin of the vector drawing coordinate system. The move will be applied along the x/y axis of the current coordinate system. All future drawing operations will be relative to the new origin. None
VectorFont VectorFont(FontID [, Size.d]) Specifies the font to use for vector drawing. Only vector fonts are allowed, like TrueType, bitmap fonts are not allowed. None
VectorOutputHeight Result.d = VectorOutputHeight() Returns the height of the vector drawing output area. Returns the output height.
VectorOutputWidth Result.d = VectorOutputWidth() Returns the width of the vector drawing output area. Returns the output width.
VectorParagraphHeight Result.d = VectorParagraphHeight(Text$, Width.d, Height.d) Returns the height needed to draw the given paragraph of text using the DrawVectorParagraph function. The actual height needed to draw the paragraph of text.
VectorResolutionX Result.d = VectorResolutionX() Returns the horizontal resolution of the vector drawing output area. Returns the horizontal resolution in DPI (dots per inch).
VectorResolutionY Result.d = VectorResolutionY() Returns the vertical resolution of the vector drawing output area. Returns the vertical resolution in DPI (dots per inch).
VectorSourceCircularGradient VectorSourceCircularGradient(x.d, y.d, Radius.d, [CenterX.d, CenterY.d]) Selects a circular gradient as the source for vector drawing operations such as FillPath or StrokePath. Initially, the gradient is solid black. Color stops have to be added with the VectorSourceGradientColor after this function. None
VectorSourceColor VectorSourceColor(Color) Selects a single color as the source for vector drawing operations such as FillPath, StrokePath and others. None
VectorSourceGradientColor VectorSourceGradientColor(Color, Position.d) Add a new color stop (a defined color position) to the gradient defined by VectorSourceLinearGradient or VectorSourceCircularGradient. A gradient must at least have a color at position 0.0 and 1.0. If no colors are added for these positions then they default to solid black. Any number of color positions can be added to a gradient. None
VectorSourceImage VectorSourceImage(ImageID [, Alpha [, Width.d, Height.d [, Flags]]]) Selects an image as the source for vector drawing operations such as FillPath or StrokePath. These functions will apply pixels from the specified image to the drawing output wherever they draw something. None
VectorSourceLinearGradient VectorSourceLinearGradient(x1.d, y1.d, x2.d, y2.d) Selects a linear color gradient as the source for vector drawing operations such as FillPath or StrokePath. Initially, the gradient is solid black. Color stops have to be added with the VectorSourceGradientColor after this function. None
VectorTextHeight Result.d = VectorTextHeight(Text$ [, Flags]) Measures the height of the given text in the current vector drawing font. Returns the text height in units of the vector drawing output.
VectorTextWidth Result.d = VectorTextWidth(Text$ [, Flags]) Measures the width of the given text in the current vector drawing font. Returns the text width in units of the vector drawing output.
VectorUnit Result = VectorUnit() Returns the unit in which all coordinates and sizes are measured on the current vector drawing output. This unit has been specified when the output was created. Returns one of the following values: #PB_Unit_Pixel : Values are measured in pixels (or dots in case of a printer) #PB_Unit_Point : Values are measured in points (1/72 inch) #PB_Unit_Inch : Values are measured in inches #PB_Unit_Millimeter: Values are measured in millimeters
Vehicle (8)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
AddVehicleWheel AddVehicleWheel(#Entity, #WheelEntity, ConnectX.f, ConnectY.f, ConnectZ.f, AxisX.f, AxisY.f, AxisZ.f, MaxSuspensionLength.f, WheelRadius.f, TractionWheel, RollInfluence.f) Add a new wheel to a vehicle previous created with CreateVehicle. None
ApplyVehicleBrake ApplyVehicleBrake(#Entity, Wheel, Brake.f) Apply the specified brake force to the vehicle wheel. The new brake force value replace any previous force previously applied to the vehicle wheel. None
ApplyVehicleForce ApplyVehicleForce(#Entity, Wheel, Force.f) Apply the specified traction force to the vehicle wheel. The new traction force value replace any previous force previously applied to the vehicle wheel. None
ApplyVehicleSteering ApplyVehicleSteering(#Entity, Wheel, Steering.f) Apply the specified steering force to the vehicle wheel. The new steering force value replace any previous force previously applied to the vehicle wheel. None
CreateVehicle Result = CreateVehicle(#Entity) Creates a new vehicle #Entity. Returns zero if the vehicle entity can't be created. If #PB_Any is used as '#Entity' parameter, the new vehicle entity number is returned.
CreateVehicleBody CreateVehicleBody(#Entity, Mass.f, Restitution.f, Friction.f [, SuspensionStiffness.f, SuspensionCompression.f, SuspensionDamping.f, MaxSuspensionCompression.f, Friction.f) Creates a physic body associated with the vehicle #Entity. To have its collisions managed by the physic engine, an entity has to set a body. In fact, only the body is known by the physic engine, which will do all the calculation about the entity, check the mass, friction and if it collides will move back the real entity. To have any effect, the physic engine needs to be activated with the EnableWorldPhysics. None
GetVehicleAttribute Result.f = GetVehicleAttribute(#Entity, Attribute, Wheel) Get the specified attribute of the given vehicle entity. Returns the value of the specified attribute or 0 if the vehicle does not support the attribute.
SetVehicleAttribute SetVehicleAttribute(#Entity, Attribute, Value.f [, Wheel]) Set the specified attribute value to the given vehicle entity. For more info about attributes possible value, . None
VertexAnimation (8)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
AddVertexPoseReference AddVertexPoseReference(#Mesh, Animation$, Track, Keyframe, PoseIndex, Influence) Adds a new pose reference to the animation. The animation should already be created with CreateVertexAnimation. None
CreateVertexAnimation Result = CreateVertexAnimation(#Mesh, Animation$, Length) Creates a new vertex animation on the specified mesh. Returns nonzero if the animation has been successfully created, zero otherwise.
CreateVertexPoseKeyFrame Result = CreateVertexPoseKeyFrame(#Mesh, Animation$, Track, Time) Creates a new keyframe in the vertex animation. The animation should already be created with CreateVertexAnimation, or be predefined in the mesh. Returns the new keyframe index.
CreateVertexTrack Result = CreateVertexTrack(#Mesh, Animation$, Index) Creates a new vertex animation track on the specified mesh. The animation should already be created with CreateVertexAnimation, or be predefined in the mesh. Every track has the same length, as defined in CreateVertexAnimation. Returns nonzero if the animation track has been successfully created, zero otherwise.
MeshPoseCount Result = MeshPoseCount(#Mesh) Returns the number of pose's in the mesh. A pose is a predefined vertex animation in the mesh. Returns the number of pose's in the specified mesh.
MeshPoseName Result$ = MeshPoseName(#Mesh, PoseIndex) Returns the pose name in the mesh. A pose is a predefined vertex animation in the mesh. Returns the pose name at the specified index.
UpdateVertexPoseReference UpdateVertexPoseReference(#Mesh, Animation$, Track, Keyframe, PoseIndex, Influence) Updates a new pose reference to the animation. The animation should already be created with CreateVertexAnimation, or be predefined in the mesh. None
VertexPoseReferenceCount Result = VertexPoseReferenceCount(#Mesh, Animation$, Track, Keyframe) Returns the number of pose references in the specified keyframe. The animation should already be created with CreateVertexAnimation. Returns the number of pose references in the specified keyframe.
WebView (5)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
BindWebViewCallback BindWebViewCallback(#Gadget, JavaScriptFunction$, @Callback()) Bind a PureBasic callback to a new JavaScript function. The JavaScript function will be automatically created in the web view and will be available in the JavaScript code. When the JavaScript function will be called in the webview gadget, the PureBasic 'Callback' will be called. The JavaScript code will be halted until the PureBasic callback finish its execution. None
UnbindWebViewCallback UnbindWebViewCallback(#Gadget, JavaScriptFunction$) Unbind a JavaScript function previously bound with BindWebViewCallback. The JavaScript function will be automatically removed from the web view and won't be be available anymore in the JavaScript code. None
WebViewExecuteScript WebViewExecuteScript(#Gadget, JavaScript$) Executes a JavaScript expression asynchronuously in the web view. None
WebViewGadget Result = WebViewGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height [, Flags]) Creates a new web view gadget in the current GadgetList. If needed a proxy can be set with WebViewProxy. Nonzero on success, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
WebViewProxy WebViewProxy(URL$, Port [Username$, Password$]) Setup a proxy for all the future WebViewGadget created. This means than all the external link and URL will goes trough this proxy before reaching the destination. It can be useful in a company environment where security level is high. None
Window (53)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
AddKeyboardShortcut AddKeyboardShortcut(#Window, Shortcut, Event) Add or replace a keyboard shortcut to the specified window. A shortcut generates a menu event (like a menu item) as most of them are used in conjunction with menus. None
AddWindowTimer AddWindowTimer(#Window, Timer, Timeout) Adds a new timer to the specified window. This will cause #PB_Event_Timer events to be received periodically in the WindowEvent or WaitWindowEvent functions. The RemoveWindowTimer function can be used to remove the timer again. None
BindEvent BindEvent(Event, @Callback() [, Window [, Object [, EventType]]]) Bind an event to a callback. It's an additional way to handle events in PureBasic, which works without problem with the regulars WindowEvent / WaitWindowEvent commands. It also allows to have real-time event notifications as the callback can be invoked as soon as the event occurs (useful for ScrollBarGadget, live window resize, etc.). An event can be unbound with UnbindEvent. None
CloseWindow CloseWindow(#Window) Close the specified window. None
DisableWindow DisableWindow(#Window, State) Enables or disables user input to the specified Window. None
Event Event = Event() Return the current event. It is the same value returned by WindowEvent and WaitWindowEvent, it is mainly useful when using a callback to determine which event triggered it. Returns the current event.
EventData Data = EventData() Get the data associated with the current event. The event needs to be a custom event sent with PostEvent. Returns the value associated with the current event. If the current event isn't a custom event sent with PostEvent, this value is undefined.
EventGadget GadgetNumber = EventGadget() After an event of type #PB_Event_Gadget (returned by WindowEvent or WaitWindowEvent), use this function to determine which gadget has been triggered. Returns the #Gadget number associated to the event.
EventlParam Result = EventlParam() This function is not supported anymore and shouldn't used in new project. Use a callback to get full control over Windows message with SetWindowCallback.
EventMenu MenuItem = EventMenu() After an event of type #PB_Event_Menu (returned by WindowEvent or WaitWindowEvent), use this function to determine which menu item, toolbar item or keyboard shortcut has been selected. Returns the menu item, toolbar item or keyboard shortcut number associated to the event.
EventTimer Timer = EventTimer() After an event of type #PB_Event_Timer (returned by WindowEvent or WaitWindowEvent), use this function to determine which timer caused the event. The same value that was used in AddWindowTimer to create the timer.
EventType EventType = EventType() After a WindowEvent or WaitWindowEvent function, use this function to determine of which type the event is. The following gadgets support EventType(): - CanvasGadget - The CanvasGadget has a special set of event types. - ComboBoxGadget - DateGadget - EditorGadget - ExplorerListGadget - ExplorerTreeGadget - ImageGadget - ListViewGadget - ListIconGadget - MDIGadget - OpenGLGadget - SpinGadget - StringGadget - TreeGadget - WebGadget - The WebGadget has a special set of event types. (See the gadget definition to see which events are supported.) The following values are possible, if an event of the type #PB_Event_Gadget (library Gadget) or #PB_Event_SysTray (library Systray) occurs: #PB_EventType_LeftClick : Left mouse button click #PB_EventType_RightClick : right mouse button click #PB_EventType_LeftDoubleClick : Left mouse button double click #PB_EventType_RightDoubleClick: Right mouse button double click #PB_EventType_Focus : Get the focus. #PB_EventType_LostFocus : Lose the focus. #PB_EventType_Change : Content change. #PB_EventType_DragStart : The user tries to start a Drag & Drop operation.
EventWindow WindowNumber = EventWindow() After a WindowEvent or WaitWindowEvent function, use this function to determine on which window the event has occurred. The window number on which the event has occurred.
EventwParam Result = EventwParam() This function is not supported anymore and shouldn't used in new project. Use a callback to get full control over Windows message with SetWindowCallback.
GetActiveWindow WindowNumber = GetActiveWindow() Returns the number of the window which currently has the keyboard focus or -1 if no window within the program is active. The number of the window which currently has the keyboard focus or -1 if no window is active.
GetWindowColor Color = GetWindowColor(#Window) Returns the background color of the specified window that was set with SetWindowColor. The background color of the specified window that was set with SetWindowColor. If no background color was set yet, -1 is returned.
GetWindowData Result = GetWindowData(#Window) Returns the 'Data' value that has been stored for this window with the SetWindowData function. This allows to associate a custom value with any window. Returns the current data value. If there was never a data value set for this window, the return-value will be 0.
GetWindowState State = GetWindowState(#Window) Checks whether the specified window is maximized, minimized or displayed normally. It can be one of the following values: #PB_Window_Normal : The window is neither maximized nor minimized. #PB_Window_Maximize: The window is maximized. #PB_Window_Minimize: The window is minimized.
GetWindowTitle Result$ = GetWindowTitle(#Window) Returns the text currently displayed in the specified window's title bar. The text currently displayed in the specified window's title bar.
HideWindow HideWindow(#Window, State [, Flags]) Hides or shows the specified window. None
IsWindow Result = IsWindow(#Window) Tests if the given #Window number is a valid and correctly initialized, window. Returns nonzero if #Window is a valid window and zero otherwise.
OpenWindow Result = OpenWindow(#Window, x, y, InnerWidth, InnerHeight, Title$ [, Flags [, ParentID]]) Opens a new window according to the specified parameters. The new window becomes the active window, it's not needed to use SetActiveWindow (unless the window is created as invisible). Nonzero if the window was successfully created, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used for the #Window parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
PostEvent Result = PostEvent(Event [, Window, Object [, Type [, Data]]]) Posts an event at the end of the internal event queue and continues program execution without waiting for message processing. Returns a non-zero value if the event was sent without error, zero otherwise.
RemoveKeyboardShortcut RemoveKeyboardShortcut(#Window, Shortcut) Removes a keyboard shortcut previously defined with AddKeyboardShortcut from the specified #Window. None
RemoveWindowTimer RemoveWindowTimer(#Window, Timer) Removes the timer from the specified window. None
ResizeWindow ResizeWindow(#Window, x, y, Width, Height) Move and resize the given window to the given position and size. If any of the parameters should be ignored (not be changed) #PB_Ignore can be passed at this place. None
SetActiveWindow SetActiveWindow(#Window) Activates the specified window, which means the focus has been put on this window. None
SetWindowCallback SetWindowCallback(@ProcedureName() [, #Window [, Mode]]) For experienced programmers only. It's only supported on Microsoft Windows. Normal events should be handled with the regular WaitWindowEvent or WindowEvent. This function associates a callback to handle the events of the all open windows. All the events are caught by this callback and can be processed here. To set a callback for a specific window only, the optional parameter can be used to pass the PB window number. To remove/disable a previous set callback just call SetWindowCallback(0 [, #Window]). Warning: this way is lowlevel. Incorrect handling of the messages in the callback can interfere with PB's own message processing. None
SetWindowColor SetWindowColor(#Window, Color) Changes the background color of the specified window. None
SetWindowData SetWindowData(#Window, Value) Stores the given value with the specified window. This value can later be read with the GetWindowData function. This allows to associate a custom value with any window. None
SetWindowState SetWindowState(#Window, State) Changes the minimized/maximized of the specified window.
SetWindowTitle SetWindowTitle(#Window, Title$) Changes the text which is currently displayed in the window title bar. None
SmartWindowRefresh SmartWindowRefresh(#Window, State) Enables a smart way to refresh the window to reduce the flickering when resizing the window. If the window isn't resizable, the function isn't needed. This function just try to help with the flickering problems, but it won't always give good results. The only way to see if it will work for a specific window is to enable it, see if there is any difference and see if the window content isn't trashed when a resize is done. None
StickyWindow StickyWindow(#Window, State) Makes the specified window stay on top of all other open windows (also from other programs), even if it does not have the focus. None
UnbindEvent UnbindEvent(Event, @Callback() [, Window [, Object [, EventType]]]) Unbind an event from a callback. If no matching event callback is found, this command has no effect. None
WaitWindowEvent Event = WaitWindowEvent([Timeout]) Wait until an event occurs. It's the same function as WindowEvent but locks the program execution, which is very important in a multitasking environment. Return the event which occurred, see WindowEvent for more information. Event can be used to get back this value.
WindowBounds WindowBounds(#Window, MinimumWidth, MinimumHeight, MaximumWidth, MaximumHeight) Changes the minimal and maximal #Window dimensions (in pixels). This is useful to prevent a window from becoming too small or too big when the user resizes it. None
WindowEvent Event = WindowEvent() Checks if an event has occurred on any of the opened windows. The next event from the event queue or zero if there are no more events. Unlike WaitWindowEvent it doesn't wait for the next event - it always returns immediately. Event can be used to get back this value. This makes it useful for window event loops, where other processing needs to be done without waiting for an event to happen (e.g. Network transactions) and therefore WaitWindowEvent can't be used. It must be handled with care though if used on a continuing basis, because unlike WaitWindowEvent, it will not give CPU time to other programs while waiting for an event and therefore consume all CPU power. In this case, either Delay should be used somewhere in the loop or WaitWindowEvent with a small timeout value. To get the window number in which the event occurred, use the EventWindow function. Possible Events are : #PB_Event_Menu : a menu has been selected #PB_Event_Gadget : a gadget has been pushed #PB_Event_SysTray : an icon in the systray zone was clicked #PB_Event_Timer : a timer has reached its timeout #PB_Event_CloseWindow : the window close gadget has been pushed #PB_Event_Repaint : the window content has been destroyed and must be repainted (useful for 2D graphics operations) #PB_Event_SizeWindow : the window has been resized #PB_Event_MoveWindow : the window has been moved #PB_Event_MinimizeWindow : the window has been minimized #PB_Event_MaximizeWindow : the window has been maximized #PB_Event_RestoreWindow : the window has been restored to normal size (either from a minimum or maximum size) #PB_Event_ActivateWindow : the window has been activated (got the focus) #PB_Event_DeactivateWindow: the window has been deactivated (lost the focus) #PB_Event_WindowDrop : a Drag & Drop operation was finished on a window #PB_Event_GadgetDrop : a Drag & Drop operation was finished on a gadget #PB_Event_RightClick : a right mouse button click has occurred on the window. This can be useful to display a popup menu #PB_Event_LeftClick : a left mouse button click has occurred on the window #PB_Event_LeftDoubleClick : a left mouse button double-click has occurred on the window #PB_Event_WindowResolutionChanged : the window has been moved to a screen with a different DPI, and it (and its gadgets) have been rescaled. The new scale factor is available from WindowResolutionX / WindowResolutionY. Only fired on Windows, for executables compiled with the 'DPI Aware' switch set to 'Per-Monitor'. A basic example for event handling can be found in the WaitWindowEvent description.
WindowHeight Result = WindowHeight(#Window [, Mode]) Returns the height (in pixels) of the given window. Returns the height (in pixels) of the given window.
WindowID WindowID = WindowID(#Window) Returns the unique system identifier of the window. The system identifier. This result is sometimes also known as 'Handle'. Look at the extra chapter Handles and Numbers for more information.
WindowMouseX x = WindowMouseX(#Window) Returns the mouse x position in the inner area of the specified window. The mouse x position in the inner area of the given window. If the mouse is outside of the window area, it will return -1.
WindowMouseY y = WindowMouseY(#Window) Returns the mouse y position in the inner area of the given window. The mouse y position in the inner area of the specified window. If the mouse is outside of the window area, it will return -1.
WindowOutput OutputID = WindowOutput(#Window) Returns the OutputID of the given window to perform 2D rendering operation on it. It will use the PureBasic 2DDrawing library and can only be used within a StartDrawing / StopDrawing block. The memory allocated in WindowOutput() is released on StopDrawing(). The OutputID of the given window to perform 2D rendering operation on it using StartDrawing.
WindowResolutionX Result.d = WindowResolutionX(#Window) Returns the DPI resolution factor, on the 'x' axis, of the screen the given window is currently displayed on. Unlike DesktopResolutionX (which always reports the primary screen), this follows the window: on a 'Per-Monitor' 'DPI Aware' executable the returned value changes when the window is moved to a screen with another DPI, right after the #PB_Event_WindowResolutionChanged event. The DPI resolution factor on the 'x' axis. '1' means no scaling, '1.5' means a 150% factor is applied, etc. Without the 'DPI Aware' compiler option, or on the platforms that do not support per-window scaling (Linux), the result is always '1'.
WindowResolutionY Result.d = WindowResolutionY(#Window) Returns the DPI resolution factor, on the 'y' axis, of the screen the given window is currently displayed on. Unlike DesktopResolutionY (which always reports the primary screen), this follows the window: on a 'Per-Monitor' 'DPI Aware' executable the returned value changes when the window is moved to a screen with another DPI, right after the #PB_Event_WindowResolutionChanged event. The DPI resolution factor on the 'y' axis. '1' means no scaling, '1.5' means a 150% factor is applied, etc. Without the 'DPI Aware' compiler option, or on the platforms that do not support per-window scaling (Linux), the result is always '1'.
WindowScaledX Result = WindowScaledX(#Window, x) Scales a value on the 'x' axis according to the DPI of the screen the given window is currently displayed on. Same as DesktopScaledX, but relative to the window's screen instead of the primary one: on a 'Per-Monitor' 'DPI Aware' executable the scaling follows the window across screens with different DPI. The scaled value. For example, on a screen with a 125% DPI factor, a value of 100 returns 125. Without the 'DPI Aware' compiler option, or on the platforms that do not support per-window scaling (Linux), the value is returned unchanged.
WindowScaledY Result = WindowScaledY(#Window, y) Scales a value on the 'y' axis according to the DPI of the screen the given window is currently displayed on. Same as DesktopScaledY, but relative to the window's screen instead of the primary one: on a 'Per-Monitor' 'DPI Aware' executable the scaling follows the window across screens with different DPI. The scaled value. For example, on a screen with a 125% DPI factor, a value of 100 returns 125. Without the 'DPI Aware' compiler option, or on the platforms that do not support per-window scaling (Linux), the value is returned unchanged.
WindowUnscaledX Result = WindowUnscaledX(#Window, x) Unscales a value on the 'x' axis according to the DPI of the screen the given window is currently displayed on. This is the exact reverse of WindowScaledX. The unscaled value. For example, on a screen with a 125% DPI factor, a value of 125 returns 100. Without the 'DPI Aware' compiler option, or on the platforms that do not support per-window scaling (Linux), the value is returned unchanged.
WindowUnscaledY Result = WindowUnscaledY(#Window, y) Unscales a value on the 'y' axis according to the DPI of the screen the given window is currently displayed on. This is the exact reverse of WindowScaledY. The unscaled value. For example, on a screen with a 125% DPI factor, a value of 125 returns 100. Without the 'DPI Aware' compiler option, or on the platforms that do not support per-window scaling (Linux), the value is returned unchanged.
WindowVectorOutput VectorOutputID = WindowVectorOutput(#Window [, Unit]) Returns the OutputID of the given window to perform vector drawing operations. It will use the PureBasic VectorDrawing library and can only be used within a StartVectorDrawing / StopVectorDrawing block. The memory allocated in WindowVectorOutput is released on StopVectorDrawing. The OutputID of the given window to perform 2D rendering operation on it using StartVectorDrawing.
WindowWidth Result = WindowWidth(#Window [, Mode]) Returns the width (in pixels) of the given window. Returns the width (in pixels) of the given window.
WindowX Result = WindowX(#Window [, Mode]) Returns the x position on the screen of the given window. Returns the x position (from the left) on the screen (in pixels) of the given window.
WindowY Result = WindowY(#Window [, Mode]) Returns the y position on the screen of the given window. Returns the y position (from the top) on the screen (in pixels) of the given window.
Window3D (20)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
CloseWindow3D CloseWindow3D(#Window3D) Close the specified window. None
DisableWindow3D DisableWindow3D(#Window3D, State) Enables or disables user input to the specified Window. None
EventGadget3D Result = EventGadget3D() After an event of type #PB_Event3D_Gadget (returned by WindowEvent3D), use this function to determine which gadget has been triggered. The 3D gadget number associated to the last #PB_Event3D_Gadget event.
EventType3D Result = EventType3D() After a WindowEvent3D function, use this function to determine of which type the event is. The following values are possible, if an event of the type #PB_Event3D_Gadget (library Gadget3D) occurs: #PB_EventType3D_Focus : Get the focus. #PB_EventType3D_LostFocus: Lose the focus. #PB_EventType3D_Change : Content change. The following gadgets support EventType3D(): - SpinGadget3D - StringGadget3D (See the gadget definition to see which events are supported).
EventWindow3D Result = EventWindow3D() After a WindowEvent3D function, use this function to determine on which window the event has occurred. The 3D window number associated with the last event.
GetActiveWindow3D Result = GetActiveWindow3D() Returns the 3D window number which currently has the keyboard focus. The 3D window number which currently has the keyboard focus. If no window has the focus, -1 is returned.
GetWindowTitle3D Result$ = GetWindowTitle3D(#Window3D) Returns the text which is currently displayed in the title bar of the specified 3D window. The text which is currently displayed in the specified 3D window title bar.
HideWindow3D HideWindow3D(#Window3D, State) Hides or shows the specified #Window3D. None
InputEvent3D InputEvent3D(MouseX, MouseY, LeftMouseButton [, Text$, SpecialKey]) Send an event to the 3D GUI system. It is required to have WindowEvent3D working. None
IsWindow3D Result = IsWindow3D(#Window3D) Tests if the given 3D window is valid and correctly initialized. Nonzero if the 3D window is valid, zero otherwise.
OpenWindow3D Result = OpenWindow3D(#Window3D, x, y, InnerWidth, InnerHeight, Title$ [, Flags]) Opens a new window on the current screen according to the specified parameters. The new window becomes the active window, it's not needed to use SetActiveWindow3D (unless the window is created as invisible). All possible events in a window are handled with WindowEvent3D. Nonzero if the 3D window has been successfully opened, zero otherwise.
ResizeWindow3D ResizeWindow3D(#Window3D, x, y, Width, Height) Move and resize the given window to the given position and size. None
SetActiveWindow3D SetActiveWindow3D(#Window3D) Activate the specified window, which means the focus has been put on this window. None
SetWindowTitle3D SetWindowTitle3D(#Window3D, Title$) Changes the text which is currently displayed in the specified 3D window title bar. None
WindowEvent3D Result = WindowEvent3D() Checks if an event has occurred on any of the opened 3D windows. InputEvent3D needs to be used to send events to the 3D GUI system to be able to have window events. WindowEvent3D() returns the next event from the event queue and returns zero when there are no more events. It doesn't wait for the next event - it always returns immediately. To get the number of the window on which the event occurred, use the EventWindow3D function. Possible Events are: #PB_Event3D_Gadget : a Gadget3D has been used #PB_Event3D_CloseWindow : the window close gadget has been pushed #PB_Event3D_SizeWindow : the window has been resized #PB_Event3D_MoveWindow : the window has been moved #PB_Event3D_ActivateWindow : the window has been activated (got the focus)
WindowHeight3D Result = WindowHeight3D(#Window3D) Returns the height of the given window. The height, in pixels, of the given window.
WindowID3D Result = WindowID3D(#Window3D) Returns the unique system identifier of the 3D window. The unique system identifier of the 3D window.
WindowWidth3D Result = WindowWidth3D(#Window3D) Return the width of the given window. The width, in pixels, of the given window.
WindowX3D Result = WindowX3D(#Window3D) Returns the left position on the screen of the given window. The left position on the screen, in pixels, of the given window.
WindowY3D Result = WindowY3D(#Window3D) Returns the top position on the screen, of the given window. The top position on the screen, in pixels, of the given window.
XML (57)
NameSyntaxDescriptionReturn value
CatchXML Result = CatchXML(#XML, *Address, Size [, Flags [, Encoding]]) Creates a new XML tree from XML data in the given memory area. The markup can be parsed in blocks by multiple calls to this function to allow parsing XML data while it arrives from the network for example. This function only returns zero on memory errors or invalid Flags. To check for parser errors XMLStatus should be used. In case of a parsing error, all data parsed before the error is accessible in the XML tree.
ChildXMLNode Result = ChildXMLNode(Node [, Index]) Returns a child node of the given XML node. The requested child node or zero if there are no children or index is out of range.
ComposeXML Result$ = ComposeXML(#XML [, Flags]) Returns the XML tree as markup in a single string. The XML will be returned in the string format of the executable (Ascii or Unicode) independent of the setting returned by GetXMLEncoding. The ExportXML function can be used to create markup in a different encoding. Returns the markup as a string.
CopyXMLNode Result = CopyXMLNode(Node, ParentNode [, PreviousNode]) Copies the given XML node and all its contained text and children to a new location. This function can even be used to copy nodes into a different XML tree. For moving a complete node to a new location MoveXMLNode can be used. The new XML node if it was copied successfully or zero if copying was not possible.
CreateXML Result = CreateXML(#XML [, Encoding]) Creates a new empty XML tree identified by the #XML number. Nonzero if the XML tree was created successfully, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used for the #XML parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
CreateXMLNode Result = CreateXMLNode(ParentNode, Name$ [, PreviousNode [, Type]]) Creates a new XML node and inserts it into the given parent node. The new XML node if it was created successfully or zero if no node could be inserted at this point.
DeleteXMLNode DeleteXMLNode(Node) Deletes the specified XML node and all its contained text and children from its XML tree.
ExamineXMLAttributes Result = ExamineXMLAttributes(Node) Starts to examine the attributes of the given XML node. Nonzero if the node is of type #PB_XML_Normal and zero else (as such nodes cannot have attributes).
ExportXML Result = ExportXML(#XML, *Address, Size [, Flags]) Writes the XML tree as markup to the given memory buffer. Nonzero if the specified length was large enough to hold the entire markup of the tree. ExportXMLSize can be used to determine the needed size for this buffer.
ExportXMLSize Result = ExportXMLSize(#XML [, Flags]) Returns the size in bytes that will be needed to export the given XML tree to a memory buffer. This function should be used to determine the needed buffersize for the ExportXML command. The size in bytes that will be needed to export the given XML tree to a memory buffer.
ExtractXMLArray ExtractXMLArray(Node, Array() [, Flags]) Extract elements from the given XML node into the specified Array(). The array will be resized to the number of elements contained in the node. None
ExtractXMLList ExtractXMLList(Node, List() [, Flags]) Extract elements from the given XML node into the specified List(). The list will be cleared before extracting the elements. None
ExtractXMLMap ExtractXMLMap(Node, Map() [, Flags]) Extract elements from the given XML node into the specified Map(). The map will be cleared before extracting the elements. None
ExtractXMLStructure ExtractXMLStructure(Node, *Buffer, Structure [, Flags]) Extract elements from the given XML node into the specified structure memory. The structure will be cleared before extracting XML nodes. None
FormatXML FormatXML(#XML, Flags [, IndentStep]) Cleans up or reformats the XML tree for a better look when exporting/saving. It can be used to have a very compact output for efficient transfer or a more formatted output for better reading. The formatting of the parsed XML document is stored in the 'text' and 'offset' fields of each node in the tree (see GetXMLNodeText and GetXMLNodeOffset for more information). None
FreeXML FreeXML(#XML) Frees the XML object and all data it contains. None
GetXMLAttribute Result$ = GetXMLAttribute(Node, Attribute$) Returns the value of an attribute in the given XML node. The value of the attribute in the specified XML node. If the attribute does not exist an empty string is returned. Only nodes of type #PB_XML_Normal can have attributes. For all other node types the compiler raises an error.
GetXMLEncoding Result = GetXMLEncoding(#XML) Returns the text encoding used for exporting/saving the given XML tree. It can be one of the following values: #PB_Ascii #PB_Unicode (UTF16) #PB_UTF8
GetXMLNodeName Result$ = GetXMLNodeName(Node) Returns the tagname of the given XML node. The tagname of the given XML node. If the node is not of type #PB_XML_Normal or #PB_XML_Instruction, an empty string is returned.
GetXMLNodeOffset Result = GetXMLNodeOffset(Node) Returns the character offset of this node within its parent. The number of characters in the parent nodes text data that lie between this node and the previous child node. So, if this node directly follows the previous one, this value will be zero.
GetXMLNodeText Result$ = GetXMLNodeText(Node) Returns the text inside the given XML node. The text inside the given XML node.
GetXMLStandalone Result = GetXMLStandalone(#XML) Returns the value of the "standalone" attribute in the XML declaration of the document. It can be one of the following values: #PB_XML_StandaloneYes : The document mode is standalone #PB_XML_StandaloneNo : The document mode is not standalone #PB_XML_StandaloneUnset: The standalone mode is not specified in the declaration
InsertXMLArray Result = InsertXMLArray(ParentNode, Array() [, PreviousNode]) Insert the specified Array() as a new XML node into the given parent node. The new XML node if it was created successfully or zero if no node could be inserted at this point.
InsertXMLList Result = InsertXMLList(ParentNode, List() [, PreviousNode]) Insert the specified List() as a new XML node into the given parent node. The new XML node if it was created successfully or zero if no node could be inserted at this point.
InsertXMLMap Result = InsertXMLMap(ParentNode, Map() [, PreviousNode]) Insert the specified Map() as a new XML node into the given parent node. The new XML node if it was created successfully or zero if no node could be inserted at this point.
InsertXMLStructure Result = InsertXMLStructure(ParentNode, *Buffer, Structure [, PreviousNode]) Insert the specified structure memory as a new XML node into the given parent node. The new XML node if it was created successfully or zero if no node could be inserted at this point.
IsXML Result = IsXML(#XML) Tests if the given #XML number is a valid and correctly initialized, XML. Nonzero if #XML is a valid XML, zero otherwise.
LoadXML Result = LoadXML(#XML, Filename$ [, Encoding]) Loads a XML tree from the specified file. Nonzero if the file could be opened and read. Note that this does not mean that the XML contained in the file was valid. To check for parser errors XMLStatus should be used. In case of a parsing error, all data parsed before the error is accessible in the XML tree. If #PB_Any was used for the #XML parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
MainXMLNode Result = MainXMLNode(#XML) Returns the main XML node of the tree. A valid XML document must have one "main" or "document" node which contains all other nodes. Except this node, there can only be comments on the first level below the root node. The type of this node is #PB_XML_Normal. The main node, or zero if the tree has no main node (which happens if the tree is empty or the main node was deleted).
MoveXMLNode Result = MoveXMLNode(Node, ParentNode [, PreviousNode]) Moves the given XML node and all its contained text and children to a new location. This function can even be used to move nodes into a different XML tree. For copying a complete node to a new location CopyXMLNode can be used. Nonzero if the move was successful or zero if the node could not be moved.
NextXMLAttribute Result = NextXMLAttribute(Node) This function must be called after ExamineXMLAttributes to move step by step through the attributes of the given XML node. Zero if there are no more attributes or nonzero if there still is one.
NextXMLNode Result = NextXMLNode(Node) Returns the next XML node after the given one (inside their parent node). The node after the specified node or zero if there are no more nodes.
ParentXMLNode Result = ParentXMLNode(Node) Returns the parent node of the given XML node. Every XML node has a parent, except the root node. The parent node or zero if 'Node' was the root node.
ParseXML Result = ParseXML(#XML, Input$) Creates a new XML tree from XML data in the string. The XML is expected to be encoded in the string format of the executable (Ascii or Unicode). If another encoding needs to be parsed, the CatchXML function can be used instead. This function only returns zero on memory errors. To check for parser errors XMLStatus should be used. In case of a parsing error, all data parsed before the error is accessible in the XML tree.
PreviousXMLNode Result = PreviousXMLNode(Node) Returns the previous XML node from the given one (inside their parent node). The node before the specified node or zero if the given node was the first child of its parent.
RemoveXMLAttribute RemoveXMLAttribute(Node, Attribute$) Removes the attribute from the given XML node. None
ResolveXMLAttributeName Result$ = ResolveXMLAttributeName(Node, Attribute$ [, Separator$]) Returns the expanded name of the given node's attribute in a document that uses XML namespaces. The expanded name consists of the namespace uri (if any) and the local attribute name, separated by the separator character given in 'Separator$'. In a document using namespaces, returns the expanded name of the attribute if it could be correctly resolved or an empty string if a namespace prefix is used that is never declared (which is invalid). In a document without namespaces, returns the attribute name itself.
ResolveXMLNodeName Result$ = ResolveXMLNodeName(Node [, Separator$]) Returns the expanded name of the given node in a document that uses XML namespaces. The expanded name consists of the namespace uri (if any) and the local node name, separated by the separator character given in 'Separator$'. In a document using namespaces, returns the expanded name of the node if it could be correctly resolved or an empty string if a namespace prefix is used that is never declared (which is invalid). In a document without namespaces, returns the node name itself.
RootXMLNode Result = RootXMLNode(#XML) Returns the root node of the XML tree. This node is always present. It represents the XML document itself. The text contained in this node represents the whitespace outside of any XML node (there can be no text outside of nodes). The children of this node are the main node and any comments outside the main node. The type of this node is #PB_XML_Root. Always returns a valid XML node if #XML is an existing XML tree.
SaveXML Result = SaveXML(#XML, Filename$ [, Flags]) Saves the #XML tree to the given file. Nonzero if the file was successfully saved, zero otherwise.
SetXMLAttribute SetXMLAttribute(Node, Attribute$, Value$) Sets the value of the attribute on the given XML node. If the attribute does not exist yet, it will be added. None
SetXMLEncoding SetXMLEncoding(#XML, Encoding) Changes the text encoding used for exporting/saving the given XML tree. None
SetXMLNodeName SetXMLNodeName(Node, Name$) Changes the tagname of the given XML node. If the node is not of type #PB_XML_Normal or #PB_XML_Instruction, this function is ignored. None
SetXMLNodeOffset SetXMLNodeOffset(Node, Offset) Changes the character offset of the given XML node within its parent nodes text data. See GetXMLNodeOffset for more information. None
SetXMLNodeText SetXMLNodeText(Node, Text$) Changes the text contained within the given XML node. See GetXMLNodeText for more information. None
SetXMLStandalone SetXMLStandalone(#XML, Standalone) Changes the "standalone" attribute of the XML declaration when exporting/saving the document.
XMLAttributeName Result$ = XMLAttributeName(Node) After calling ExamineXMLAttributes and NextXMLAttribute this function returns the attribute name of the currently examined attribute on the given XML node. The attribute name of the currently examined attribute on the given XML node.
XMLAttributeValue Result$ = XMLAttributeValue(Node) After calling ExamineXMLAttributes and NextXMLAttribute this function returns the attribute value of the currently examined attribute on the given XML node. The attribute value of the currently examined attribute on the given XML node.
XMLChildCount Result = XMLChildCount(Node) Returns the number of child nodes inside the specified XML node. The number of child nodes inside the specified XML node.
XMLError Result$ = XMLError(#XML) In case of an error while parsing XML data this function returns an error-message describing the error. XMLStatus can be used to detect parsing errors. The english readable error string.
XMLErrorLine Result = XMLErrorLine(#XML) In case of an error while parsing XML data this function returns the line in the input that caused the error (one based). XMLStatus can be used to detect parsing errors. The line in the XML where the error occurred. The first line index starts from 1.
XMLErrorPosition Result = XMLErrorPosition(#XML) In case of an error while parsing XML data this function returns character position within the line returned by XMLErrorLine at which the error was caused. (The first character of the line is at position 1) XMLStatus can be used to detect parsing errors. The character position in the XML where the error occurred. The first character index starts from 1.
XMLNodeFromID Result = XMLNodeFromID(#XML, ID$) In valid XML, if a node has an attribute called "ID", the value of this attribute must be unique within the XML document. This function can be used to search for a node in the document based on its ID attribute. The node with the given ID tag or zero if no such node exists within the tree.
XMLNodeFromPath Result = XMLNodeFromPath(ParentNode, Path$) Returns the XML node inside ParentNode who's relation to ParentNode is described through 'Path$'. XMLNodePath can be used to get such a path to a node. The target node or zero if the path did not lead to a valid node.
XMLNodePath Result$ = XMLNodePath(Node [, ParentNode]) Returns a string representing the relation between Node and ParentNode. A string representing the relation between 'Node' and 'ParentNode'. See XMLNodeFromPath for a description of the returned path string.
XMLNodeType Result = XMLNodeType(Node) Returns the type of the given XML node. It can be one of the following: #PB_XML_Root This is the trees root node. It represents the document itself. This node cannot be created or deleted manually. Inside the root node, there can be only one node of type #PB_XML_Normal and also no plain text. (this is required to be a well-formed XML document) #PB_XML_Normal This is a normal node in the tree. It can have a list of attributes and contain text and/or child nodes. Example: <node attribute="hello"> contained text </node> #PB_XML_Comment This node represents a comment. It can have no children or attributes. Its text represents the content of the comment. Example: <!-- comment text --> #PB_XML_CData This is a CData section. A CData section contains only text. Its content is not interpreted by the parser so it can contain unescaped "<" and ">" characters for example. CData sections can be used to include other markup or code inside a document without having to escape all characters that could be interpreted as XML. Example: <![CDATA[ cdata content ]]> #PB_XML_DTD This is a document type declaration (DTD). This library does not use a validating parser, so these declarations are actually ignored when parsing a document. In order to save them back correctly, they are contained within such a DTD node. The text content of the node is the entire DTD tag. It can be read and modified through commands like SetXMLNodeText and will be written back to the document when exporting/saving without modification. The SetXMLStandalone command could be useful as well when working with DTDs. Example: <!DOCTYPE name SYSTEM "external dtd uri"> #PB_XML_Instruction This node represents a Processing Instruction. Processing Instructions contain information that is intended to be interpreted/executed by the target application. They have a name to specify the content of the instruction and the instruction data which can be accessed with GetXMLNodeText. Example: <?php if (...) ... ?> (here "php" is the node name, and the rest up to the "?>" is the node text.)
XMLStatus Result = XMLStatus(#XML) Returns the status of the last parsing operation done on this XML tree (using LoadXML or CatchXML). This function should be called after every LoadXML or CatchXML call to ensure that the parsing succeeded. A string representation of the parsing status (ie a readable error-message) is returned by the XMLError function. A value of zero (#PB_XML_Success) indicates a successful parsing, all other values indicate various error conditions. The following returnvalues are possible: #PB_XML_Success : no error #PB_XML_NoMemory : out of memory #PB_XML_Syntax : syntax error #PB_XML_NoElements : no element found #PB_XML_InvalidToken : not well-formed (invalid token) #PB_XML_UnclosedToken : unclosed token #PB_XML_PartialCharacter : partial character #PB_XML_TagMismatch : mismatched tag #PB_XML_DublicateAttribute : duplicate attribute #PB_XML_JunkAfterDocElement : junk after document element #PB_XML_ParamEntityRef : illegal parameter entity reference #PB_XML_UndefinedEntity : undefined entity #PB_XML_RecursiveEntityRef : recursive entity reference #PB_XML_AsyncEntity : asynchronous entity #PB_XML_BadCharacterRef : reference to invalid character number #PB_XML_BinaryEntityRef : reference to binary entity #PB_XML_AttributeExternalEntityRef: reference to external entity in attribute #PB_XML_MisplacedXML : XML or text declaration not at start of entity #PB_XML_UnknownEncoding : unknown encoding #PB_XML_IncorrectEncoding : encoding specified in XML declaration is incorrect #PB_XML_UnclosedCDataSection: unclosed CDATA section #PB_XML_ExternalEntityHandling: error in processing external entity reference #PB_XML_NotStandalone : document is not standalone #PB_XML_UnexpectedState : unexpected parser state #PB_XML_EntityDeclaredInPE : entity declared in parameter entity #PB_XML_FeatureRequiresDTD : requested feature requires XML_DTD support in Expat #PB_XML_CantChangeFeatures : cannot change setting once parsing has begun #PB_XML_UnboundPrefix : unbound prefix #PB_XML_UndeclaringPrefix : must not undeclare prefix #PB_XML_IncompletePE : incomplete markup in parameter entity #PB_XML_XMLDeclaration : XML declaration not well-formed #PB_XML_TextDeclaration : text declaration not well-formed #PB_XML_PublicID : illegal character(s) in public id #PB_XML_Suspended : parser suspended #PB_XML_NotSuspended : parser not suspended #PB_XML_Aborted : parsing aborted #PB_XML_Finished : parsing finished #PB_XML_SuspendedPE : cannot suspend in external parameter entity #PB_XML_ReservedPrefixXML : reserved prefix (xml) must not be undeclared or bound to another namespace name #PB_XML_ReservedPrefixXMLNS : reserved prefix (xmlns) must not be declared or undeclared #PB_XML_ReservedNamespaceURI: prefix must not be bound to one of the reserved namespace names
